News.title: Student overstayer tricked more than 70 girls as young as 10 to send naked photos and videos & used them as blackmail
News.content:
TWISTED FIEND Student overstayer tricked more than 70 girls as young as 10 to send naked photos and videos & used them as blackmail







Next

AN Indian student who tricked more than 70 girls across the UK to send naked photos and videos has been jailed for 30 years.

Bilal Kazi, 27, who had overstayed his visa, preyed on his victims by pretending to be a 14-year-old white, blond-haired schoolboy named Reece.



The predator then posed as their boyfriend, pressuring them, even while they were at school, to send explicit pictures and videos of themselves on Snapchat.

Kazi would then threaten to leak the material online, so victims sent more indecent images out of fear, Chester Crown Court heard.



He admitted to 33 child sex offences relating to 19 victims, including causing a child to engage in penetrative sexual activity, making indecent images of children and six counts of blackmail, between 2021 and 2025.

But police fear Kazi, who targeted young girls on apps including Snapchat, Wizz and Wink, and while playing Roblox, could have as many as 180 potential victims who have not been identified.

The 27-year-old victimised vulnerable teens in particular with many left with psychological trauma, feeling broken and their innocence stolen, a court heard.

He twice leaked indecent images online, leaving the young victims suicidal.



The vile predator told a 13-year-old girl that he was preparing her to have sex with him, and told others that sending naked images is what people did for each other if they were in love.

Kazi met another teen victim on an app called Wizz, before grooming her on Snapchat.

Some of her friends logged into her account and saw a video she had sent to ‘Reece’, which was shared around her school and others, and she said her “whole world fell apart”.

In a victim impact statement, she said: “I was young and I didn’t know any better. I became a joke overnight, like I had done something wrong. I was just a kid.”

It was heard the girl lost all her friends, was bullied, fell into severe depression, and took an overdose.



Kazi hacked the Snapchat account of another girl and publicly posted on her profile the indecent video she had sent him, which was viewed by 93 users.

The girl’s mother found the messages from ‘Reece’ in May 2022 and alerted police.

Kazi, a chemical engineering PhD student originally from Mumbai, was traced, living in Chester but had left the country.

He was then arrested at Heathrow Airport in July 2023, when he came back from visiting family in Kuwait and his mobile phone was seized.

The paedophile, at the time living in Birmingham, continued to target teenage girls while released on bail.



Kazi was finally rearrested and remanded into custody in August 2025 and police found hundreds of category A child sex abuse videos involving teenage girls, along with 9,000 messages exchanged with one girl alone in the space of three weeks.

Cheshire Police said their investigation into Kazi became the force’s largest ever online child sexual abuse case as 70 victims, aged between 10 and 17 at the time of offending, were identified across 28 of the UK’s police force areas.

Judge Steven Everett, Recorder of Chester, jailed the defendant for 30 years, with an extended sentence of eight years on licence, saying: “That’s the sad feature. He’s taken away their childhoods.

“You took advantage of what appears to me a lack of proper security on social media sites which should have been there to prevent young persons being taken advantage of by sexual predators like you.

“It is incomprehensible why any person would do what you did to these 19 different young girls and we have no idea how many others.



“We will never know how many victims have fallen prey to you. You are a very dangerous person.”

Detective Sergeant Ross Peel said: “Victims should never feel ashamed of what they have experienced. The responsibility for these offences lies solely with the offender, and we want anyone who has been subjected to this kind of abuse to know that they will be listened to, supported and taken seriously.

“Our message to parents is to speak to your children and take an interest in the apps and platforms they are using. The potential for online offending is vast, and offenders can target children from anywhere in the world.

“By educating yourselves and your children about online safety and the risks associated with communicating with people they do not know online, you can help protect them from becoming victims of crime – the impact of which can be profound and long-lasting.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I hope this case demonstrates our commitment to protecting vulnerable people and bringing an end to the sexual exploitation of children. It should also serve as a warning to those who, like Kazi, believe that hiding behind a screen makes them anonymous and untouchable.



“No matter where you are or how you choose to offend, those who target children and vulnerable people will be identified and brought to justice.”

News.title: Small boat migrant raped woman twice after dragging her into tent beneath London bridge
News.content:
Next

A SMALL boat migrant who dragged a woman into his tent in a homeless encampment and repeatedly raped her is facing years in jail.

Moustafa Elbohy targeted his victim after she had been out drinking with work colleagues on September 20 last year.



She stopped to chat to the 32-year-old Egyptian and his friends near Embankment tube station in Central London because she lived near “a lovely Middle Eastern community” and enjoyed listening to them speak Arabic, a court heard.

But Elbohy pulled her into his tent and used Google Translate to threaten her.



He then forced the woman to the ground and raped her twice.

Prosecutor Richard Milne told Southwark crown court that she thought Elbohy might kill her in the tarpaulin encampment under Hungerford Bridge.



He said: “She was scared and fearful, and told him she needed to get home to her husband and children.”

When the woman got away, she contacted an actor friend who had just finished in a play.

He arrived within 15 minutes and took her to Charing Cross police station to report the attack.

The woman told police: “I was really scared. It was dark and there was no one else around.



“He was a really volatile, angry man.

“I felt fear and scaredness. I felt disgusting.”

Speaking with her head in her hands, she told police officers: “He was really rough.”

Elbohy, whose address was formerly given as the Doubletree by Hilton Reading in Wokingham, Berkshire, claimed his victim consented to sex.

But he was convicted of two counts of rape yesterday by a jury after seven hours and 57 minutes of deliberation.



Elbohy — who entered the country on a small boat three months before the attack and was housed in a hotel where he made an unsuccessful asylum claim — will be sentenced on Tuesday.

News.title: US soldier suspected of spying for Russia served alongside SAS in Afghanistan before arrest in Britain
News.content:
Next

A US soldier suspected of spying for Russia served with the SAS in Afghanistan, The Sun can reveal.

Lt Col Brandon Tyner spent a year with a special forces task force that included SBS, Navy Seals and Delta Force.



The married dad-of-two, 41, was arrested on Tuesday at his four-bed home in Innsworth, Gloucs.

He was one of around 30 US personnel at Nato’s Allied Rapid Reaction Corps (ARRC) at nearby Imjin barracks.



In 2013 he served with the elite Special Operations Joint Task Force in Kabul.

As deputy head of its personnel branch, he was never a “badged” special forces operator and did not go out on missions.

But he would have had access to Special Forces soldiers’ names, roles and units.

The taskforce was led by Delta Force Gen Scott Miller, a hero of 1993’s Battle of Mogadishu which inspired the book and film Black Hawk Down.

Sources close to the Tyner investigation are “confident” he didn’t share anything with any genuine Russians.

One said: “He was intercepted before any damage could be done.”



Counter Terrorism Police said he was arrested under the National Security Act 2023.

He can be held for up to 14 days but is expected to be charged within days.

News.title: British CNN war reporter who dodged bombs & gun ordeal sues for £1.6m after breaking ankle outside restaurant in London
News.content:
Next

A WAR reporter who survived guns, bombs and grenades is suing for £1.6million after breaking his ankle outside a restaurant.

Brit telly newsman Matthew Chance, 56, claims his career was torpedoed by a patch of grease.



The CNN correspondent, on £425,000 a year, fell over in Christmas 2022, slipping on “greasy and oily” food waste at a stall in Borough Market, London Bridge.

Mr Chance, who was heading to the nearby Roast Restaurant to book a table, suffered a “Bosworth Fracture”, where ligaments are torn from the bone.



He claims he was forced to move back to the UK from Moscow, raising his tax bill and hitting earnings.

He is suing the Borough Market Trustees at London’s High Court for his injuries and lost past and future income.



Barrister James Byrne said it “has caused a substantial loss to him”.

The trustees have admitted liability, but are set to contest the amount of damages.

Mr Chance has had several brushes with death, including being held at gunpoint in Libya.

He also interviewed Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky in his Kyiv bunker as Russian bombs landed.



Live from Ukraine in another report, he saw he was crouching next to a grenade by a road, telling viewers: “Let’s move away from that.”

Barrister James Hogg, for the trustees, said he must prove “incidence, causation, nature and extent of the pain, injury, loss and damage alleged”.

He said “credibility was an issue” as Mr Chance was able to return to report from Ukraine in 2023.

The case is scheduled for a five-day trial in early 2028.

News.title: Brit flight to America cancelled after FAA grounds planes with weekend journeys likely to be affected
News.content:
Next

BRITS travelling to America have seen their flights cancelled after the US grounded all planes on Friday night.

The US’s Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) halted all flights nationwide “due to extraordinary circumstances”, sparking fears it will cause travel chaos this weekend.



British Airways cancelled a flight to New York which had been due to take off from London Heathrow at 10.30pm on Friday.

A spokesman for Manchester Airport confirmed three US-bound flights scheduled to leave on Saturday morning – all operated by Virgin Atlantic – are likely to be affected if the issue is not resolved soon.



A Virgin Atlantic spokesperson said: “We’re aware of the ground stop order issued by the Federal Aviation Administration for all US airports.

“We’re closely monitoring the situation and assessing any impact to our flights. We advise any customers due to travel to check their flight status at virginatlantic.com.”



US transportation secretary Sean Duffy said the FAA is investigating a communications issue affecting regional air traffic control centres – the incident has left millions of US passengers stranded.

It is only the second time flights have been grounded across the US since the September 11 terror attacks in 2001.



Flights were halted by the FAA in January 2023 because of a system error.

US homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin said: “There is no reason for the public to be afraid or scared for your loved ones.

“This isn’t another 9/11… This is a telecommunications outage.

“Throughout FAA, out of abundant of caution, we have grounded all the flights, and all the flights are accounted for.

“As incoming flights, either internationally or the flights that are currently still in the air, we’ll be dealing with those case by case.



“As you can imagine, there will be a priority list as they start coming in.”

He added: “Everybody is safe. There is no reason to be concerned about your loved ones if they’re flying or anything like that. I just want to make sure everybody’s at ease about that.”

He went on: “There is no indication as of yet that this was a nefarious attack against us. It’s just a telecommunication outage as of right now.”

A spokesperson for American Airlines said: “The FAA has temporarily paused departures nationwide.

“Flights already in the air can continue to their destinations.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We expect disruption to our schedule for the rest of the day, depending on the length of the FAA’s nationwide ground stop.

“It will be all hands-on deck across American to get customers on their way as soon as possible when the FAA lifts this ground stop.

News.title: Blithering Burnham is out of his depth – he’s off begging in Brussels while Trump, Putin and Xi decide the world’s fate
News.content:
Next

A SINGLE flap of a butterfly’s wings can unleash a storm on the other side of the world – or so chaos theory goes.

Some actions have a world-changing impact. Others go completely unnoticed.



So guess how Andy ­Burnham’s latest flap of the eyelashes on the world stage went this week?

Yes, that’s right, it wouldn’t be a gathering of the global B-team without our foreign- policy rookie and all- round wing-and-a-prayer PM turning up.



Britain was the only G7 country to bother sending its leader to the latest COP ­summit — that annual circlejerk of climate hypocrisy, hot air and hysteria.

Given the cost of ­similar trips on the prime-ministerial jet, his seven-hour, 4,000-mile round schlep to Turkey would have cost the taxpayer at least £100,000.

Forget about the carbon, that’s £131 per word for the six-minute, 764-word boreathon he delivered to a near-empty hall.

“The message I carry here at my first COP as UK Prime Minister is this: we’re committed to meeting our 2050 Net Zero target” . . . yada-yada-yada.

It was the ­definition of a meeting that could have been an email.

If emails were working, that is, and not knocked out by the latest mysteriously timed internet chaos that came just days after we were warned cybergeddon is on the way.



Why, if a British Prime Minister gives a speech in a faraway land and no one is there to hear it, are we paying for it?

But, after saving the world in Turkey, it was then on to Dublin for Burnham the Brexit Betrayer — pitching up cap-in-hand to the Brussels elites for a scrap from their increasingly bare table.

And, once again, the PM was absolutely all over the shop — out of his depth, babbling one minute about rejoining the EU and the next about “delivering what voters wanted in 2016”.

It’s all building up to the joint UK/EU Summit in six days’ time that Burnham declared just a few months ago would be the moment he would “lay out to the country what I believe the different options are for Britain’s long-term relationship with our European partners.”

Now that speech is being quietly shelved, as it becomes increasingly clear that Burnham doesn’t have the first clue about what he actually believes.



Forget talk of publishing a Ten-Year Plan, this guy would struggle to build a bear at a Build-a-Bear Workshop.

Meanwhile the Europeans are sniggering into macchiatos as they salami slice away Britain’s post-Leave freedoms, luring us all back into ensnarement in their web of red tape — just as they always planned to do.

Only now they’ve got a doormat of a British PM to bamboozle to make the job easy.



Just this week, Burnham’s Government insisted he had “no plans to align with the EU AI Act” — just days after his ­ministers signed off Northern Ireland to do just that.

I fear we are about to watch the first recorded case in history of a kipper stitching up itself.

Whatever the outcome of next week’s summit, we know for certain that it will not be the most important gathering of leaders in the next seven days.

No airmiles for Andy at this one, though, as Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and President Xi meet in China at a crossroads in history.

While the 33rd annual Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen sounds pretty dry, it’s the action on the fringes of the summit that is causing a stir.



America, Russia and China are still locked in talks about the talks, as they haggle over the terms of a potential tri- lateral chinwag of mega-importance.

It’s being breathlessly compared by some to the 1945 meeting between the US, ­Britain and Soviets at Yalta — the doomed summit designed to stabilise the globe after World War Two, which ended in the decades-long Cold War. But sadly there’s no Churchill at the table for us any more.

No, Burnham will be nose pressed to the diplomatic shop window as the international strongmen gather to carve up the modern world.

The mood music ahead of such a momentous meeting could not be more ­dramatic as America reels from its No1 firm, AI giant Nvidia, imploding in a sex-and-spy scandal — accused of illegally smuggling its pioneering chips to China.

The US economy is over-exposed to the $4trillion firm’s runaway success, with ousted CEO Jensen Huang’s bedroom antics potentially sending the world into recession if they pricks the AI bubble.



The timing of the implosion could not work more in favour of Beijing as they seek to turn the screws on an embattled Trump in their new “arms race” for global technological domination.

And that’s before we get to the world’s three largest nuclear powers meeting behind closed doors to talk about the rest of us.

Shamefully, I fear it will be Ukraine on the chopping block, as Russia increases its insane demands for breaking up Nato, carving up the Donbas and demilitarising half of Eastern Europe as its price for peace.

Decisions could be made this week that will leave Burnham’s diplomatic blithering and tinkering looking very small indeed. But, hey, at least we know his views on climate change now.

LAST week I wrote of the great battle shaping up to replace Donald Trump, with the two big beasts of his government, Marco Rubio and JD Vance, heading toward a clash of destiny.



Now both of them have been hit by an outbreak of coyness.

Multiple well-sourced briefings this week suggested Vice President Vance – who has been fundraising and scheming for two years – has not yet decided if he will run in 2028.

That’s despite having a pretty advanced operation already up and running and endorsements flowing in.

Meanwhile, Secretary of State Rubio is sticking to his line that he’s just not thinking about it.

While you can take Vance’s teasing act with a hefty truckload of salt, Rubio’s supporters genuinely believe he will sit out the 2028 race.



One well-placed figure in the administration is even suggesting that Rubio is “broke”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

His 14 years in the Senate on an annual salary of $174,000, and two years on $250,600 as America’s top diplomat, pales in comparison to the billions sloshing around Trump world.

“He could be making ten or 20 million dollars a year for a decade with his eyes shut and come back to politics another day”, whispers one “helpful” opponent.

News.title: Thousands of young Europeans coming to UK risks worsening youth unemployment, fear ministers
News.content:
Next

AN expected surge of young European migrants risks worsening the youth unemployment crisis in the UK, ministers fear.

Several of Andy Burnham’s top team are understood to fear the Youth Mobility Scheme will undermine the attempt to get Brits into work.



His bid to give visas to tens of thousands of EU youngsters coincides with the drive to reduce the UK’s one million Neets — 16 to 24-year-olds not in employment, education or training.

A government source said: “Several of the Cabinet are privately baffled that at the very moment we’re trying to get youngsters into jobs, the PM is making that harder by forcing them to compete with loads of Europeans.”



Shadow Chancellor Andrew Griffith said: “It’s weird any government would want to make a bad situation worse.”

It comes days before Labour grandee Alan Milburn unveils a review into Neets.



The former Health Secretary is expected to recommend cutting sickness and disability benefits for some under-25s to fund greater support to get youngsters into work.

His review has warned Britain spends £25 on benefits for young people for every £1 spent helping them into jobs.

Labour is currently in talks with Brussels about the scale of the Youth Mobility Scheme and will continue negotiations at next week’s EU-UK summit.

The programme would let young Europeans live and work in Britain for a limited number of years, with reciprocal arrangements for UK youngsters.



The Government insists the scheme will be capped but has yet to agree a figure, with reports suggesting Britain had sought a limit of fewer than 50,000 arrivals a year.

News.title: Shocking moment ‘drunk Brit tourist’ parades stolen golden Jesus statue before smashing it on ground and fleeing
News.content:
Next

THIS is the outrageous moment two suspected drunk Brits chuckle while posing for a photo with a stolen statue of Jesus before smashing it.

Shocking CCTV footage showed one man hauling the gilded icon away from a 15th-century church while laughing as the other filmed the stunt.



The two men are believed to be from the UK, but authorities have not confirmed their nationalities and have appealed to the public for information on their identities.

In the gob-smacking clip, one man can be seen sitting on a bench before another stumbles into frame holding the sacred figure.



The suspect sitting down begins to record using his phone while the other struggles to keep his footing while man-handling the child-sized statue.

Seconds after horsing around, the figure’s arms suddenly break off.



The gilded sculpture then crashes to the ground before shattering into several small pieces.

With a dumbstruck expression on his face and two gold arms in each of his palms, the reportedly British man runs off while the man filming also walks away in the same direction.



The man who dropped the figure appeared to be intoxicated, though this has not been confirmed.

Police launched a probe into the appalling ordeal.

The idol was taken from the Shrine of Divine Mercy church in the Old Town of Vilnius, Lithuania‘s capital.



Reports say the man is British due to his accent heard in the CCTV clip.

He was seen wearing a checkered scarf and a long grey coat.

The other man filming wore a blue beanie and black jacket.



The clip was shared to social media by the church’s priest, Fr. Elijas Anatolijus Markauskas.

It is believed to have been taken from a nearby shop.

The priest appealed with viewers to share the video in order to gain more attention.

He added that the statue was taken from a wooden cross in a courtyard close to the street where the duo were recorded.

Local cops said: “On November 11, at about 9pm in Vilnius, Dominikonų St., from the inner courtyard of the church, an unidentified person broke a golden sculpture of Jesus hanging on a wooden cross.



“The damage is being assessed.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“A pre-trial investigation has been initiated under Article 284 of the Criminal Code of the Republic of Lithuania.”

The Shrine of Divine Mercy church is home to the famed 1934 painting of the Divine Mercy.

News.title: Paedo jailed for 30 years over 'incomprehensible' crimes while posing as child
News.content:
Paedo jailed for 30 years over 'incomprehensible' crimes while posing as child

Bilal Kazi, 27, posed as a 14-year-old boy called 'Reece' to manipulate more than 70 young girls into sending him sexually explicit videos and images of themselves

View 2 Images Bilal Kazi (Image: Cheshire Constabulary/Press Association)

A paedophile who groomed more than 70 young girls while posing as a 14-year-old boy online has been jailed for 30 years.

‌



‌



Bilal Kazi, 27, used a fake photo and online alias 'Reece' to manipulate the girls into sending him sexually explicit videos and images of themselves.

‌



Kazi's victims were aged between 10 and 17, and were targeted through apps including Snapchat, Wink and Roblox across a four-year period from August 2021 to August 2025.

‌



A trial at Chester Crown Court heard the defendant made his victims believe they were in a relationship with him before pressuring them - even while they were at school - to send naked photos and videos on Snapchat.

He would then threaten to leak the images online, so victims sent more indecent images out of fear, the court heard.

Kazi, originally from India, was studying at the University of Chester. Police have said he could have as many as 180 potential victims who have not yet been identified.

‌



View 2 Images The case was heard at Chester Crown Court (Image: MEN Media)

Many of his teenage victims were left with psychological damage, feeling "broken", their innocence taken and teenage years ruined, the court heard. Twice indecent images were leaked online, leaving the young victims suicidal.

‌



Kazi admitted at an earlier hearing to 33 child sex offences relating to 19 victims, including causing a child to engage in penetrative sexual activity, making indecent images of children and six counts of blackmail, between 2021 and 2025.

He was today jailed for 30 years with an extended sentence of eight years on licence as a judge told him: "You are a very dangerous person."

‌



"Thats the sad feature. He's taken away their childhoods," Judge Steven Everett, Recorder of Chester, told the court.

Addressing Kazi, he added: "You took advantage of what appears to me a lack of proper security on social media sites which should have been there to prevent young persons being taken advantage of by sexual predators like you.

‌



"It is incomprehensible why any person would do what you did to these 19 different young girls and we have no idea how many others.

"We will never know how many victims have fallen prey to you. You are a very dangerous person."

‌



Kazi told one of his 13-year-old victims that he was preparing her for sex with him, while he told others that sending naked images is what people did for each other if they were in love.

The defendant met another teenager on an app called Wizz before grooming her on Snapchat.

‌



Another girl said her " whole world fell apart" when her friends logged into her Snapchat account and found a video she had sent to "Reece", which was shared around her school.

The girl lost all her friends, was bullied, fell into severe depression, and took an overdose.

‌



Kazi hacked the Snapchat account of another girl and publicly posted on her profile the indecent video she had sent him, which was seen by 93 of her friends. "Before she took it down the damage had been done," Myles Wilson, prosecuting, told the court.

The girl's mother found the messages from "Reece" and police were called in, in May 2022.

‌



Kazi, a chemical engineering student originally from Mumbai, was traced, living in Chester but had left the country. He was then arrested at Heathrow Airport in July 2023, when he came back from visiting family in Kuwait and his mobile phone seized.

He had been living in Hubert Croft, Birmingham, at the time, and continued targeting teenage girls in the same way while on bail and under investigation.

‌



Cheshire Police said their investigation into Kazi became the force's largest ever online child sexual abuse case, with as many as 180 girls potentially involved, with victims across the UK including in Scotland, Devon, Cornwall, Avon and Somerset.

Police say 70 victims, aged between 10 and 17 at the time of Kazi's offending, were identified across 28 of the UK's 45 police force areas.

‌



Kazi was finally rearrested and remanded into custody in August 2025 and police found hundreds of category A child sex abuse videos involving teenage girls, along with 9,000 messages exchanged with one girl alone in the space of three weeks.

Detective Constable Georgia Hughes, of the Online Child Abuse Investigation Team at Cheshire Police, said: "The scale of Kazi’s offending meant this was a truly mammoth investigation, requiring significant resources and close collaboration across the force.

‌



She added: "The girls targeted by Kazi were young and vulnerable. For many, their interactions with him were their first experience of what they believed to be a romantic relationship.

"His offending has had a profound and lasting impact on the victims. Many lived in constant fear of what he would do if they failed to comply with his demands, and some have carried that fear with them for years."

Article continues below

Detective Sergeant Ross Peel said: "I hope this case demonstrates our commitment to protecting vulnerable people and bringing an end to the sexual exploitation of children.

"It should also serve as a warning to those who, like Kazi, believe that hiding behind a screen makes them anonymous and untouchable."

News.title: Microsoft outage updates: Outlook and Teams issues continue amid 'improvements'
News.content:
Thousands of people across the UK faced problems accessing Microsoft services such as Outlook, Teams and Copilot today amid a global outage affecting millions of users

NHS GP practices, pharmacies, police forces and schools were hit by a major Microsoft outage that has disrupted services for millions of people around the world today.

The tech giant has been battling widespread disruption to Outlook, Teams, its AI assistant Copilot and its cloud-based subscription service Microsoft 365, among other services, since yesterday evening. Thousands of UK users reported being unable to access their emails and carry out their work and daily tasks this morning. GMB Union claimed the Microsoft outage is preventing 111 and 999 services from referring patient details as they normally would, creating a "massive backlog".

Microsoft says the disruption has been caused by a "technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents". It is restoring services gradually due to the "scale of demand" and it will provide a full post-incident report once its review is complete, the spokesperson adds

News.title: BBC Weather issues ‘unprecedented’ polar vortex verdict as snow forecast for UK
News.content:
BBC Weather issues ‘unprecedented’ polar vortex verdict as snow forecast for UK

While snow and freezing temperatures are on the cards this weekend, weather forecasters say we have now seen the 'earliest major sudden stratospheric warming on record'

What is the bizarre weather phenomenon Sudden Stratospheric Warming?

Following a summer of record-breaking temperatures and heatwaves, experts say another weather record has now tumbled.

‌



‌



BBC Weather says winds in the polar vortex have switched from their typical westerly direction to easterly, marking the “earliest major sudden stratospheric warming on record”.

‌



Temperatures rising in the stratosphere can cause shifts in the polar vortex, a ring of powerful winds that keeps freezing air near the North Pole. When these winds weaken, Arctic air rushes downwards and often impacts the jet stream.

‌



The previous earliest SSW on record came on November 28 in both 1969 and 2025. The same process led to the infamous 'Beast from the East' in 2018, a historic weather system which brought 22 inches of snow to some parts of the country.

View 2 Images The polar vortex is a ring of powerful winds that keeps freezing air near the North Pole (Image: weathershot)

Met Office weather maps show 20 counties face snow on Monday and Tuesday – list READ MORE :

However, as there are “very few historical examples of early season major SSWs to compare with”, BBC Weather says it remains unclear just how the current SSW will impact our weather. “This event happening so early in autumn is unprecedented in modern observations,” forecasters explain.

‌



Temperatures have dropped below freezing this week, reaching -7C in some rural areas overnight, while snow is expected in some regions this weekend. However, this isn’t a result of SSW.

“We do know that it is definitely not connected to the cold spell right now,” BBC Weather said. The Met Office previously linked the current conditions to developments in the troposphere, the lowest layer of the atmosphere.

‌



View 2 Images SSW can lead to snow falling in the UK (stock) (Image: PA)

The world is also in the grips of a strengthening El Nino, set to be the most powerful in decades. El Ninos have previously been linked with SSW events in the latter half of winter, but BBC Weather says “further research” is needed to draw any links between the current El Nino and the SSW event this week.

‌



Met Office forecasts snow for UK

Met Office Deputy Chief Forecaster Steven Keates has said “spells of rain, sleet and some hill snow” are on the cards this weekend.

In Scotland, “there is an increasing chance of snow developing later in the day”. While most of the snow will be confined to higher ground, he added some “could fall to lower levels too”.

Article continues below

“Into next week, unsettled and cold conditions remain with rain, sleet and (mainly hill) snow key features,” the Met Office said.

News.title: Washington DC shooting: Dr Matt Lambert named as suspect in fatal gun spree
News.content:
Matt Lambert, the gunman who took his own life after shooting five people in Washington DC, was a doctor who had reportedly been involved in a long-running feud with his homeowners association

Three weapons have been recovered from the flat where a doctor fatally shot himself after shooting five people in Washington DC, killing one of them.

Matt Wade Lambert, 55, opened fire inside the Vida Logan Circle gym in the Logan Circle neighbourhood on Thursday morning local time, killing 46-year-old James Stuart. He then made his way back to his flat in the area and shot four other people from his balcony, police said. The shootings took place about a mile north of the White House.

Police said one person is in a critical condition, while the other three suffered non-life-threatening injuries. The injured victims are two women and two men, but their identities have not been revealed.

Police chief Jeffery W Carroll said Mr Stuart was the building manager of the property where Lambert lived. Officers believe the shooting was related to an ongoing dispute between Lambert and the homeowners association management.

The attacker had reportedly been involved in a long-running feud with the Metropole Condominium Association, which operates the luxury residential tower on 15th Street near Logan Circle. An X account believed to be linked to Lambert complained of water damage and mould in the property. Its last post came at 8.06am local time, around the same time as the shooting, and said: "My manifesto is an engineering report."

The emergency room doctor filed a lawsuit last year, alleging that he had been unable to use his $1.1m (around £831,000) penthouse since 2024 because of black mould and humidity problems. He then sued the Metropole Condominium Association in March 2025.

News.title: Former NSW MP Rory Amon found guilty of sexually assaulting 13-year-old boy
News.content:
Former NSW MP Rory Amon found guilty of sexually assaulting 13-year-old boy

Former NSW Liberal MP Rory Amon, 37, has been found guilty by a jury of sexually assaulting a 13-year-old boy after claiming he believed the boy was over the age of 16

View 2 Images Former NSW Liberal MP Rory Amon (Image: 7NEWS)

A former NSW Liberal MP could face a lengthy jail term after a jury found him guilty of sexually assaulting a 13-year-old boy.

Rory Amon was found guilty on Friday of one count of sexual intercourse with a person aged between 10 and 14, and of indecently assaulting a child. The jury reached a verdict after around four hours of deliberations.

The 37-year-old was standing trial for a second time at the New South Wales Supreme Court after a previous jury cleared him of eight separate child sex offences in March, but failed to reach a verdict on the other two.

The case centred on Amon's contact with a 13-year-old boy, who he met through an adults-only website, the court heard.

Amon had consistently denied the allegations, claiming he genuinely believed the boy was over 16. His original trial heard the boy had given a false age when signing up to the gay dating app and repeated it during conversations with Amon.

The pair exchanged explicit images before arranging to meet in 2017 in the car park of the boy's apartment block, the court heard.

View 2 Images Amon has maintained that he believed the boy was over 16 (Image: 7NEWS)

At the time, Amon was working full-time for Jason Falinski, a federal MP representing the Australian constituency of Mackellar. He later served two terms on the Northern Beaches council before being elected as the Liberal MP for Pittwater in 2023.

But the charges brought his fledging political career to an abrupt end, with Amon expelled from the Liberal Party and forced to resign just months after his election in March 2023.

His departure triggered a by-election, in which the Liberals lost the previously safe seat to an independent candidate.

Amon remains on bail and is due back in court for a sentencing hearing on November 27. He is the third former NSW MP to be convicted of sexual offences in recent years.

Former Kiama MP and Coalition minister Gareth Ward was jailed in 2025 for sexually abusing two young men, including a political staffer who was drunk following an event at NSW Parliament House.

His minimum prison term of three years and nine months is due to expire in April 2029.

Former NSW minister Milton Orkopoulos was convicted in 2023 of sexually abusing teenage boys while serving as a state Labor MP.

The 65-year-old was found guilty of 26 offences involving four underage boys, as well as supplying them with drugs over a decade-long period ending in 2003.

He had previously served more than a decade in prison for separate offences, including the sexual assault of a minor, indecent assault and supplying heroin and cannabis.

News.title: Microsoft outage could leave people in hospital for longer and others low on medication, warns top pharmacist
News.content:
Microsoft outage could leave people in hospital for longer and others low on medication, warns top pharmacist

EXCLUSIVE: The chair of a community pharmacy association revealed the impact Microsoft outages have had on chemists, leaving some driving to hospitals to pick up paper and drop medication

View 3 Images The chair of the NPA, Olivier Picard, revealed the impact faced from the Microsoft outage (Image: Supplied)

Some patients could be kept in hospitals longer while some people could run low on medication amid the Microsoft outage that has impacted pharmacies and the NHS, a top pharmacist has warned.

‌



‌



The UK Government and its counterparts worldwide have been forced to put in place contingency measures due to the outage, which has seen Microsoft scramble to restore email, Teams and other services since they went down yesterday around 6pm.

‌



Olivier Picard, the chair of the National Pharmacy Association, shared the impact of Friday's tech disruptions as pharmacists have been left to "work around the system". Pharmacies were unable to access their NHS emails meaning they could not contact hospitals or GPs for information on patients.

‌



Mr Picard, a Berkshire based pharmacist, revealed some chemists were forced to revert to contingency plans, and have people drive to hospitals to collect paper and come back to prepare medication to take back for patients.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images Key public services across the UK - including the NHS, police and councils - faced disruptions amid the outage (Image: Yui Mok/Press Association)

‌



Microsoft outage live: Outlook and Teams issues continue as Claude AI goes down READ MORE :

The NPA chair, who represents 6,000 members, shared the difficulties he faced this morning. He told the Mirror that dispensing or receiving prescriptions was not impacted as this is not done through an NHS email.

Mr Picard said: "Where there's been a problem is, for example, in local surgeries, sometimes they only allow patients to request repeats either through the NHS App or via NHS email for security reasons." He added that patients have come in to request prescriptions but pharmacists have been unable to do this due to the outage.

‌



He added: "Some patients are telling me, 'Well, I'm running out of medication over the weekend.' There could be an argument around when it is reasonable to ask for a repeat prescription, but at the same time, these patients could be in a position where they have to wait for their repeat until next week."

View 3 Images Mr Picard said 'today we've gone back 20 years', due to the outage (Image: Supplied)

‌



The NPA chair added that some pharmacies, including his, offer a service to hospitals where they can request medication to allow patients to be discharged from hospitals. Picard said: "Now, if we can't receive the email, we can't prepare the medication.

"If we don't prepare the medication, the patient is staying in hospital until they receive the medication, and that can have a ripple effect for patients who might have to stay in hospital until we are able to receive and prepare those packs for them."

‌



On being forced to revert to driving between a hospital and pharmacy with papers and medication, Mr Picard said: "Basically today... we've gone back 20 years just because of that, in the way we work."

The NPS chair however shared that all pharmacies should have contingency plans in place to ensure services are not majorly impacted, and praised pharmacists for how they responded to Friday's unexpected challenge.

‌



Mr Picard however shared his concerns over tech disruptions as this has not been the first one pharmacists have had to face, adding the extra concern for community pharmacies entering the festive period - which is the busiest time of the year for chemists.

He said: "Pharmacies have gone through wars and pandemics over the last two centuries and have been able to continue providing NHS care to their patients. But we can't be let down by a system."

‌



Earlier today, in a statement, the NPA said: "Please bear with your pharmacy teams today, where waits may be longer than normal and there may be delays to some prescriptions."

This comes as NHS England said health service staff were "enacting long-standing measures" to overcome IT outages, including using paper records, but asked patients to continue contacting services such as 999 and 111 as necessary, and attend appointments as usual.

‌



Professor Victoria Tzortziou Brown, President of the Royal College of GPs, said practices were continuing to provide care despite the disruptions.

However, Professor Brown said: "We understand that the disruption is primarily affecting email communications, although there have also been reports of difficulties accessing some online consultation systems. The full extent of the impact is still being established."

‌



Other key services in the UK impacted by the tech disruption included some police forces, schools, and councils.

Monitoring website Downdetector first showed a spike in users reporting problems with Microsoft Teams in the UK at about 6.15pm on Thursday, with more than 130,000 reporting Outlook issues in the US at its peak last night.

‌



Millions of its customers have been unable to send and receive emails through Outlook, with Teams has also been affected for many, and the tech giant's Copilot AI assistant and other Microsoft 365 services are also disrupted.

Other AI chat services have also been disrupted, such as OpenAI's Chat GPT and Anthropic's Claude.

Article continues below

Microsoft executive vice-president Charles Lamanna said the outages did not appear to be the result of a cyber attack.

News.title: Myleene Klass 'told off' by King Charles' staff after mistake at his home
News.content:
Myleene Klass 'told off' by King Charles' staff after mistake at his home

Loose Women panellist Myleene Klass reflected on her several encounters with King Charles, including a visit to his home in Scotland

View 3 Images King Charles III

Myleene Klass has revealed the unusual reason she was given a dressing-down while visiting one of King Charles’ Scottish residences. The singer and Loose Women panellist has performed for the monarch on several occasions and was presented with an MBE by him last year in recognition of her services to women’s health, miscarriage awareness and charity work.

‌



‌



Reflecting on her several meetings with the monarch, she joked she may have left him wondering when he'd seen the last of her.

‌



Speaking about her encounters with the King on the At Home With Vanessa podcast, Myleene told Vanessa Feltz: "There was definitely a two-month period where I'm sure he was rolling his eyes, like 'Her again'.

‌



"He's a cellist, he's an amazing cellist, I find him fascinating. There's been a few times that I have performed for him, like at his castle, that's such a surreal line [to say]," she continued.

The former Hearsay star then recalled one particularly memorable visit to the King's Dumfries residence in Scotland, where she had been invited to perform on the harp.

Describing the experience, she said: "I went up to Scotland and they asked me to play the harp for him at his Dumfries house and you just sort of see him roaming around the gardens and why wouldn't you?"

‌



View 3 Images Myleene shared why she was told off at Charles' Dumfries home (Image: Getty)

However, Myleene insisted her relaxed approach to getting ready landed her in trouble after she used one of the bedrooms.

‌



"It's his house but it just feels so surreal and they've got these Chippendale beds, which I put all my stuff out on, and I thought oh you know I'll get ready in this room and then somebody popped in and said, 'Don't put anything on the bed'."

Myleene appeared to suggest that the warning was prompted by fears she could damage the valuable furnishings.

‌



Previously opening up about receiving her MBE from the King, she told Express.co.uk, she said: "He was incredible. I have been lucky to meet him on a few occasions now and have performed for him many times however, this felt very different. It really was a huge moment."

Their conversation also turned to a cause particularly close to Myleene's heart, with the pair speaking "at length" about her campaign to improve miscarriage care across the UK and challenge long-standing medical practices.

‌



View 3 Images Myleene Klass said she found King Charles 'fascinating' (Image: Getty)

For years, women in the UK were required to experience three consecutive miscarriages before being offered certain forms of NHS medical intervention or tailored support.

‌



Myleene's campaigning helped push for changes designed to ensure women could receive support much earlier, including GP signposting and mental health support following a first or second loss.

She said the King was surprised by some of the issues she raised, explaining: "HRH was surprised to hear that there's no official figure on the amount of women suffering miscarriages, as no official stat exists, as well as the fact that women have to endure three consecutive miscarriages before receiving medical intervention.

Article continues below

"I mooted, 'You wouldn't wait for two more heart attacks before seeking out care' at which he vehemently agreed."

News.title: Police investigating David Walliams over reports alleging serious sexual offences
News.content:
The Metropolitan Police has launched an investigation into David Walliams over reports of "alleged serious sexual offences".

It comes after ITV News and the Guardian published reports alleging that Walliams had been accused of sexual misconduct by several women.

The Met said that the allegations being investigated are separate from those reported by ITV and the Guardian, but as "part of their investigation, detectives are also proactively reviewing that reporting to establish whether there is any evidence of offences".

When those allegations were first reported, Walliams said he was "not a sexual predator" and had not "broken the law".

In a statement released on Friday, the Met said it had "received a number of allegations of non-recent serious sexual offences involving a man now in his 50s".

"Those who have come forward are being supported by specialist officers," the statement added.

Detective Superintendent Mike Cagney said: "We would encourage anyone who has been the victim of a sexual offence to come forward and speak to us, no matter when it happened.

"We know reporting allegations of this nature can be daunting, but specialist officers are on hand to provide support, answer questions and guide you through the process."

Allegations against the entertainer and children's author were published after he lost a legal bid to stop claims against him being made public by the media.

Some of the women in the investigation accused Walliams of "grooming" them when they were teenagers.

One now characterises her alleged encounter with Walliams at 15 years old as a "sexual assault". Walliams strongly denied he had any sexual contact with the girl.

He said he rejected any allegations of criminal activity and that he has never engaged in the grooming of young women.

The Guardian and ITV News said that several of the women, who do not know one another, allege they were targets of unwanted sexual advances from Walliams.

The investigation also claimed Walliams had a sexual relationship with at least one junior employee at publisher HarperCollins, and pursued another.

Other women alleged inappropriate behaviour at ITV's Britain's Got Talent, such as inviting girls and young women to his dressing room.

In a letter addressed to journalists working on the ITV and Guardian investigation, Walliams wrote: "Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with.

"I realise I did not always take people's feelings properly into account. That is something I regret.

"And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did."

He added: "I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me."

Walliams shot to fame in the early 2000s with BBC sketch comedy Little Britain, served as a judge on ITV's Britain's Got Talent and launched a best-selling series of children's books.

News.title: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All rescued after cruise ship hit by tanker in New Orleans
News.content:
Some 130 people on a cruise ship docked in New Orleans have been rescued after it was struck by a tanker.

The cruise ship, American Heritage, was left lying on its side in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel, Atlantic Asphalt.

The collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for. Officials hailed it as a "miracle on the Mississippi".

The exact cause of the crash remains under investigation, but US Coast Guard Captain Melanie Burnham said: "There seems to be some type of a loss of steering."

New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference that all credit in the rescue effort went to first responders who "literally jumped right in to help".

"We have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," Moreno said.

Calls about the collision came in around 13:30 EST (18:30 GMT) on Friday when people began trying to help passengers escape the boat as it took on water, Port of New Orleans Chief Melanie Montroll told the news conference.

There were about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, on the American Heritage at the time of the collision, according to Port of New Orleans.

Passengers began disembarking from the paddlewheeler vessel, operated by American Cruise Lines, as it started listing before tipping on to its side, Mayor Moreno said.

Tugboat operators, police and other rescuers rushed to help and officials shut down the Mississippi River for the search effort.

The American Heritage was finishing an eight-day cruise to Mississippi River destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi.

President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that the rescue was an "incredible job".

Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said the US Coast Guard also supported local rescue operations.

Governor Jeff Landry also hailed the rescue as a "miracle on the Mississippi" given the "sheer number of people who were on that cruise ship" who were rescued.

Ships have operated safely on the Mississippi River for years, Landry said, pledging to investigate what happened.

Jamie Holford, a witness to the crash, told the BBC's US partner CBS that he saw the cruise ship hit the dock following the collision.

"It sounded like a war movie. Just imagine tons of steel crunching. That's what it sounded like," he said. "It looked like something off the Titanic."

Holford added that he saw passengers and crew members "hollering" and "crying" as they tried to get off the ship while it was sinking.

The American Heritage can carry up to 150 guests and features a glass-enclosed restaurant, fitness centre and three guest lounges, according to its website.

Built in 2015, the vessel has at least four decks.

News.title: US Air Force says it responded to 'suspected drones' over RAF Lakenheath
News.content:
The US Air Force said it responded to "suspected unauthorised drone activity" over RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk on Friday evening.

No personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected, a spokesperson for the US Air Force said.

It comes after unconfirmed reports that sirens were sounded at the base, which residents reported hearing from a nearby village.

A Ministry of Defence spokesperson told the BBC it was "coordinating with all relevant parties", adding that US Air Force security personnel responded to the reports and the situation was resolved.

"We are working closely with them to establish the facts," they added.

West Suffolk MP Nick Timothy said he had been in touch with authorities at the base, and was told "there is no threat to the public, and the incident is now resolved".

"Given the raised threat level, I continue to encourage everyone to report anything suspicious or out of the ordinary to the authorities," he added in a social media post.

Earlier this week, at least 12 US Air Force aircraft departed the nearby RAF Mildenhall base.

They included two Boeing Stratotanker KC-135 refuelling aircraft, with one apparently headed towards Germany and another seen landing at Prestwick Airport near Glasgow.

News.title: Goalkeeper involved in fatal collision gets 12-game ban
News.content:
FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been given a 12-match suspension by the Spanish football federation's disciplinary committee after his challenge which resulted in the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.

Owono, 25, was sent off after colliding with De Miguel during the closing stages of the second-tier match between their two respective sides on 2 November.

De Miguel died the following day, aged 30.

The disciplinary committee said it had to base its decision "on the facts expressly recorded in the referee's report", which stated the player "was sent off for 'violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play'.

"The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge."

The committee added the "nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances" means that "the maximum sanction, a 12-match suspension, is justified".

Separately, the federation has decided the game between the two sides, which was abandoned seven minutes into stoppage time when the incident occurred, will not be replayed.

"This avoids having to resume play from the precise moment at which the tragic incident occurred," it said.

The teams were drawing 2-2 at the time and that result will now stand, with a federation committee saying that was the "most respectful course of action, given the extraordinary and tragic circumstances of this case".

Owono's club issued a statement on the goalkeeper's behalf on 4 November, in which he said he was experiencing "the most difficult days" of his life and felt "enormous pain" about De Miguel's death.

On Thursday, FC Andorra manager Carles Manso said Equatorial Guinea international Owono is yet to decide whether he will return to football following the incident.

Manso said Owono is currently spending time with his family and is "completely free to make any decision" with regard to a potential return, adding: "What we have to do is support him in every way and be close to âhim.

"We will âgive him space so that he feels completely free to make âany â decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

"When he feels it is appropriate and when âhe feels genuinely ready to take a âdecision â like that [he will do so]."

News.title: Former Hamas bodyguard guilty of UK knife attack
News.content:
A former Hamas bodyguard, wanted in Germany over an alleged plot to murder Jewish people, has been found guilty of a knife attack on a bailiff outside his UK home.

Mohammed Alfatih, previously known as Mohammed Naim, was regularly seen acting as a bodyguard for a former leader of Hamas in 2006. He was granted asylum in the UK in 2015 and British citizenship in 2021.

The 40-year-old was found guilty by majority verdict of unlawfully wounding a bailiff who had come to repossess his wife's car, possession of two knives and criminal damage. He was cleared of wounding with intent.

Alfatih was under surveillance by a counter-terror unit at the moment he attacked the bailiff in Birmingham last year.

The son of a senior Hamas official, he could not be named during his trial due to reporting restrictions.

During the trial, footage was shown of Alfatih brandishing two large kitchen knives outside his home in the suburb of Kings Heath and trying to stab the bailiff as he drove away.

He told the court he chased the victim across the street to scare him away after his wife was asked to settle her debts of more than Â£2,250 linked to unpaid parking fines.

Her car had been clamped by the enforcement officer, who was involved in a struggle inside Alfatih's terraced home.

News.title: New campaign against EU membership launches ahead of UK-EU summit
News.content:
A new campaign against the UK rejoining the European Union has been launched ahead of a UK-EU summit next week.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham is exploring closer ties with the bloc and is expected to sign new agreements on food, energy and youth mobility on 20 November, arguing a "win-win" deal can be struck.

But Stay Out has warned any future attempt to rejoin the EU could prove costly to taxpayers and the UK should "move on and spend our money on our own priorities".

The group has received support from Lord Gove, chairman of the Vote Leave campaign during the 2016 EU referendum, who warned reopening the Brexit question would "commit the country to another decade of fractious negotiations".

He said: "Rejoining would mean handing back control of our laws, borders, money and trade, and paying a good deal more for membership than we did before."

He added people are "desperate for Westminster to get on with delivering on their priorities" rather than looking to rejoin the EU.

Stay Out is chaired by Oliver Lewis, who also worked for Vote Leave, and acted as deputy chief negotiator for the UK government in trade negotiations with the bloc.

Lewis said: "The country has had enough of arguing about Europe, and it is time to move on and spend our money on our own priorities."

News.title: Man jailed for grooming at least 70 girls online
News.content:
A man who groomed at least 70 girls and manipulated them into sending sexually explicit videos and images of themselves has been sentenced to 30 years in prison.

Bilal Kazi, 27, targeted his victims - aged between 10 and 17 - using apps including Snapchat, Wink and Roblox between August 2021 and August 2025.

Kazi, a student from India who was studying at the University of Chester, posed as a 14-year-old white British teenage boy and made his victims believe they were in a relationship with him.

He was jailed after pleading guilty to 37 charges including making indecent images, blackmail and inciting a child to engage in sexual activity.

Warning: This article contains distressing information

Kazi must serve a minimum of 20 years in prison before being eligible for parole and will be on the sex offenders register for life.

Once eligible for parole he will be on licence for eight years.

In a personal impact statement read out at Chester Crown Court earlier, one victim said she had struggled with anxiety as Kazi, who later moved to Birmingham, had "taken away a sense of privacy and security".

"I am doing my best to move forward but the effects are still with me," she said.

"The harm caused is not limited to the time events took place - they continue to affect my daily life."

The court heard that some of the victims had attempted suicide, struggled with anxiety and developed eating disorders.

One victim, who was 13 years old when Kazi first contacted her, said he took her "innocence away".

"I hope one day I can get on with my life," she said.

News.title: Widespread frost and freezing fog forecast as cold health alerts continue
News.content:
Arctic air will maintain its grip on the UK to start the weekend, as cold health alerts remain in place for a large swathe of England.

Saturday will dawn with another sharp and widespread frost with the coldest conditions expected in England and Wales.

Patches of freezing fog could also be a hazard, reducing visibility and bringing a risk of very slippery surfaces in southern and eastern England.

Then it is all change by Sunday with most areas having a frost-free start, but heavy bursts of rain and brisk winds will sweep across the country later.

News.title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage
News.content:
Key services across the UK, including the NHS, GPs and schools, have been affected by a global Microsoft outage.

Pharmacies and businesses have also been hit after email and messaging services went down.

NHS England said patients should still attend appointments unless told otherwise, while several large police forces are urging the public to call if they want to report a crime.

Microsoft said services were now gradually being restored globally after a problem caused by a higher-than-usual stress on its servers, but users could still experience disruption.

The government said it was working closely with the firm to assess any impact on its services, while local authorities warned that some council services were being affected.

The full extent of the impact of the outage - which is affecting Outlook, Teams and Copilot - and the time it will take to restore the systems remains unclear hours after users first reported issues.

Some 430 million people use the online tools worldwide.

The chief executive of the NHS Alliance, which represents the healthcare system in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, said the outage was affecting some services including emails.

NHS trusts in England were enacting measures to minimise disruption to critical services, a spokesperson said.

Patients have been told to continue to use 999 in an emergency and otherwise contact 111 by phone or online, or their local pharmacy.

Some GP surgeries have urged patients not to submit messages via their website while the problem remains. Practices in Hampshire and Shropshire have told patients to phone them or come into the surgery if they have an urgent need.

News.title: Reform and Tory spokesmen in angry clash over immigration at Piddington
News.content:
A press conference led by Piddington Parish Council chairman Tim McNally took place on Friday after Housing Secretary Angela Rayner approved the Home Office's application to change the use of the site for asylum accommodation.

The Home Office said this would allow it to continue developing the plan but that no final decision on the site had been taken.

There has been significant local opposition to the proposal and a legal challenge to the planning decision is expected from the parish council.

In September, Piddington symbolically voted to leave the UK over the planned use for the site in Oxfordshire.

Politicians from the Conservatives and Reform have made several visits to Piddington, a village of about 350 people, to show their support for campaigners.

Speaking on Friday, Philp said a future Conservative government would shut the asylum accommodation "straight away" if it was opened by Labour.

Yusuf made clear Reform's opposition to the plans before his focus switched to the Conservatives.

He said: "It's obviously true that we would not be gathered here today and 1,200 men would not be being dumped into this beautiful village were it not for the actions of the Conservative government.

"So I actually want to ask you Chris, would you actually like to apologise for the things you did in government to bring hundreds of thousands of people into this country illegally?"

Philp, a former immigration minister, described Yusuf's remarks as "disingenuous" and argued the migrants who could be housed near Piddington will have arrived in the country while Labour has been in power.

He said the Conservatives are under new leadership and he hoped the politicians could "stand in solidarity with the residents" rather than "engage in point scoring".

Philp added: "Zia, read the room, listen to the people clapping and read the room."

Yusuf countered that it was "important that we hold everybody accountable for this situation" and said Philp had been "heavily involved in immigration and borders policy" for the Conservatives in government.

Philp repeated his "read the room" suggestion, adding: "The public here want you to pipe down on the cheap politics."

Yusuf dismissed the suggestion that he was engaging in "cheap politics" and repeated his criticism of the Conservatives' record, saying they "refused" to secure the country's borders when in power.

As Yusuf spoke, Philp could be heard saying: "Buddy, I'm not here to give you comms advice, mate, you're in a hole stop digging."

Philp told Yusuf he should "calm down", with the Reform politician repeating his request for the Conservative MP to "apologise to the British people".

McNally thanked the pair for attending the press conference, adding: "I understand this is a passionate discussion and I respect you both for what you've got to do and what you represent."

While the two parties are on the right of politics, it is unusual for them to share a platform to campaign and both are keen to stress their differences to voters.

Reform leader Nigel Farage has pitched the party as replacing the "old, fuddy-duddy" Conservatives, and Tory leader Kemi Badenoch has said she would rather have another general election than do a deal with Reform to secure power.

News.title: Probation officers to take industrial action over pay and early release scheme
News.content:
Probation officers have voted to reject a 5% pay rise and take industrial action, citing growing pressure created by the government's prisoner early release scheme.

Members of Napo, the probation service union, voted to refuse overtime from 23 November - and could take strike action should the union "deem that option to be necessary".

Its general secretary Ian Lawrence said the service was "already in crisis" before the early release scheme came into force, which relies on probation staff monitoring freed prisoners in the community.

A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said the government had put forward a "strong offer" and was recruiting an extra "1,300 officers to significantly cut workloads".

They added that the government has "robust contingency plans in place" to ensure offenders "are still subject to the same rigorous supervision" in the event of industrial action.

Probation service unions have warned that officers have too many cases and the rate at which staff are leaving the profession has increased.

The service has come under renewed pressure in recent months as a result of the early release scheme, the union said, which the government introduced as prisons were dangerously close to capacity.

Seven-hundred eligible offenders originally sentenced to up to 19 months were released on 1 October, with another two groups of 650 prisoners released on 13 October and 10 November.

Another nine groups are expected to leave prison in the next seven months, with inmates who received longer sentences included in the later cohorts.

Some 250 prisoners serving more than 12 years are expected to be released on 9 June.

Napo's leader said staff had tried "desperately" to implement early release schemes introduced by the Labour government and previous Conservative government, but had been asked to do so with "inadequate staff and a lack of resources".

The government has said electronic tags and probation intervention will help to manage prisoners freed early.

The Probation Service uses electronic monitoring to track curfews and conditions of a court or prison order, with most of those eligible for early release now requiring tagging.

But a September report by His Majesty's Inspectorate of Probation (HMIP) found that almost half of electronic tags used to track offenders' movements were not fitted on time.

News.title: 'Hardest challenge of my life' - Owain Wyn Evans completes Children in Need ride
News.content:
Presenter Owain Wyn Evans has completed his challenge of cycling through all four UK nations to raise money for BBC Children in Need.

The Welsh host of BBC Radio 2's Early Breakfast Show rode almost 400 miles, setting off from Glasgow and finishing in Cardiff on Friday.

The challenge started on 9 November in Scotland and over the next five days, Owain rode through Northern Ireland, England and Wales and raised Â£3,853,530 in the process.

Reflecting on his journey, he said: "This has been the hardest challenge of my life, 100%.

"I can't believe I'm here. It's overwhelming, all the love and passion and commitment people have shown."

The BBC said Owain's challenge would be the "greatest-ever distance" covered in a Radio 2 endeavour for the charity.

He crossed the finish line in Cardiff's Central Square just after 11:00 GMT, and was greeted by a crowd cheering him on before he was met by his husband, Arran Rees.

Owain, 42, whose bike was named Shania Chain, and decked out in Children in Need colours - Pudsey's favourite yellow with coloured spots - said: "Thank you so much everyone, from me and Shania.

"Honestly, this has felt so far away for such a long time. I can't believe that I'm here with this welcome and the sun's out."

Hollywood actor Luke Evans announced the route to Owain each day on BBC Radio 2.

During the 640km feat, he was also surprised with the premiere of Steps' brand-new version of their debut hit 5, 6, 7, 8, retitled 5, 6, 7, donate, which featured new lyrics and extra vocals.

It was recorded to help boost Owain's spirits on the longest day of his challenge.

News.title: Eleanor Donaldson given supervision order and placed on sex offenders' register
News.content:
The wife of former Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) leader and convicted child sex offender Jeffrey Donaldson has been placed under a supervision order for three years.

Appearing before Newry Crown Court, via video link, for the first time since 2025, a tearful Eleanor Donaldson was also told she would be placed on the sex offenders' register for five years.

When Judge Paul Ramsey asked if she understood that she would be subjected to a supervision treatment order (STO), she nodded her head and said "yes".

Eleanor Donaldson could not be given a prison sentence as she faced a 'trial of the facts' as it was determined she was medically unfit for a criminal trial.

She was found to have done the acts in relation to five charges, including four of aiding and abetting her husband's offending.

Last month Jeffrey Donaldson was sentenced to 15 years in prison for a series of child sex offences against two victims, including one count of rape, which took place between 1985 and 2008. He is seeking to appeal against his convictions.

His wife has also applied to appeal the verdict from her trial of the facts.

News.title: Tories pay artist for Burnham images after legal threat
News.content:
The Conservatives have agreed to pay an artist who threatened to sue the party after it used his illustration of Andy Burnham to mock the prime minister.

Stanley Chow posted on Facebook that the party had used the picture - which Burnham has used on social media - without permission.

He had sought legal advice and threatened to take action against the party. It is understood the Tories agreed to pay a Â£1,000 fee for use of the image - and contributed an unknown sum to Chow's legal fees.

The Conservatives had distributed water bottles with the image on them - accusing Burnham of being a "bottler".

Chow posted on Facebook: "The Conservative Party have settled after their recent indiscretion of using my image without my permission."

He added: "Maybe ask firstâ¦ admittedly I would have said no, but it would have been a damn sight cheaper for the Tory Party if they just hired any illustrator to do their take on a cartoon of Burnhamâ¦ hopefully this a lesson learned. Copyright matters."

A Conservative spokesman said: "The Conservative Party values the importance of intellectual property in the creative industries. We consider this matter closed."

News.title: Dept Q crew member dies after being  injured at Edinburgh film studio
News.content:
A member of the crew for the Netflix series Dept Q has died after being seriously injured at a film studio in Edinburgh.

Emergency crews were called to FirstStage studio in Leith at about 15:00 on Thursday and the man was pronounced dead a short time later.

Left Bank Pictures, which is involved in making Dept Q, later said it was "shocked and saddened" by the death of a crew member.

Police Scotland said the death was not being treated as suspicious but inquiries into the circumstances were ongoing. The Health and Safety Executive said it was "aware" of the incident.

A Left Bank Pictures spokesperson said: "We are deeply shocked and saddened by the tragic death of a member of our Dept Q crew.

"Our thoughts are with their family, friends and colleagues at this incredibly difficult time, and we are offering support for those affected."

News.title: Mother whose newborn died after failed hospital checks was 'terrified and alone'
News.content:
A mother whose newborn baby died after hospital staff failed to wake her for checks before he was born told an inquest she felt "terrified and alone".

Eve Taylor, 29, was admitted to Ysbyty Gwynedd, Bangor, after her waters broke early at 36 weeks and was identified as having signs of potential infection.

She was due to be monitored again later that night, but a midwife decided not to wake her up. Taylor awoke hours later and was rushed for an emergency C-section.

Sonny Taylor died of a brain injury three days after being born on 3 October 2022, with a coroner saying his death was preventable.

Betsi Cadwaladwr University Health Board has apologised and admitted failings in care.

During a full inquest hearing at Caernarfon, the coroner's court heard how initial monitoring showed both mother and child were well, with antibiotics given in case of an infection.

In a statement read out in the hearing, the mother said she later woke up "feeling an intense fear".

"Instinctively, I felt that something was wrong and I needed help," she said.

Taylor told a midwife that her baby did not appear to be moving as usual.

The maternity team discovered the baby's heartbeat was very low, and an emergency C-section was carried out.

"Everything seemed rushed and out of control. I felt that the staff were frantic with little organisation," she said.

The hospital then moved the mother to the labour ward rather than directly to an operating theatre, leading to a further delay in delivering the infant.

Taylor said there was "panic" with staff arguing with each other and her son was born in "poor condition" just after 02:00 in the morning.

She was told he was very unwell with a possible brain injury.

Sonny was then transferred to the special care baby unit at Glan Clwyd Hospital, but despite intensive care, he died three days later.

News.title: ‘Miracle on the Mississippi’: All passengers accounted for after New Orleans riverboat crash, officials say
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A nearly 500-foot tanker collided with a paddlewheel riverboat carrying more than 100 tourists and crew members along the Mississippi River in New Orleans, sending dozens into the water and sparking massive rescue efforts - ending with no loss of life.

In what New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno called a “miracle on the Mississippi,” all passengers and crew members on the American Cruise Lines vessel have been accounted for. At least 32 people were hospitalized among the 180 to 190 passengers and crew members who were on the riverboat at the time. No deaths or critical injuries were reported.

It remains unclear what caused the tanker to “lose control,” Moreno said.

“The passengers began disembarking, but while that was happening, the cruise ship began to sink and then eventually the cruise ship toppled over and flipped,” the mayor said during a press conference Friday afternoon.

“When that occurred, we started to have people in the water,” Moreno added. “It was an all hands on deck approach.”

open image in gallery This image, taken from a video provided by Devon Flanagan, shows people being helped out of the water after a tanker crashed into a river cruise in New Orleans on November 13 ( AP )

open image in gallery Footage from the scene shows a much-larger tanker striking the docked paddlewheel cruise ship, which began sinking into the Mississippi River as passengers in life jackets gathered along its railing or jumped into the water ( AP )

The crash unfolded along a heavily trafficked stretch of the riverfront just outside the French Quarter, near the Ernest N. Morial Convention Center between the Central Business District and Warehouse District.

American Cruise Lines’ paddlewheelers are a familiar fixture along the riverwalk, which is surrounded by hotels, restaurants, a shopping mall, a riverfront park and the Audubon Aquarium.

At roughly 12:30 p.m. local time, in a stretch of the river under the Crescent City Connection bridge, the riverboat was preparing to disembark passengers when the tanker careened toward the docked vessel.
