Video footage from the scene shows the tanker moving perpendicular to the riverboat before making contact, creating a massive crashing noise that crackled along the riverwalk.

Evacuations began when the boat started to sink with passengers still aboard.

“Unfortunately, we were not able to get everyone off before the boat started to take on water, and, eventually, it would capsize,” Harbor Police Chief Melanie Montroll told reporters Friday afternoon.

Passengers clung to the rails and screamed as the boat tilted toward the tanker, then flipped upside down and sank into the water. Videos also show people bobbing in the water wearing orange inflatable rings while passersby try to toss ropes into the river to pull them up.

'Zero people unaccounted for' after New Orleans boat crash, officials say

The Mississippi River in that corridor reaches depths of up to 200 feet and is notorious for powerful currents and whirlpools capable of quickly pulling swimmers under — a hazard so severe that signage along unprotected stretches of the shoreline warns pedestrians never to wade into the water.

Emergency crews began pulling people out of the water by 2:10 p.m. local time. Passengers were brought into the Port of New Orleans Administration Building to receive shelter and assistance, port officials said. Louisiana Lt. Gov. Billy Nungesser told WWL-TV that initial estimates indicated 85 people had been rescued and treated alongside the dock.

In a statement to The Independent on Friday evening, LCMC Health confirmed that University Medical Center New Orleans and other network hospitals had “received an estimated two dozen patients following the reported maritime incident.”

“Our medical teams are currently evaluating patients and providing appropriate care while coordinating with emergency responders,” a spokesperson added. “As this remains an active situation, we will provide additional information as appropriate.”

open image in gallery Emergency personnel and crews arrived on the scene shortly after a tanker crashed into the boat, which quickly capsized and sank into the river ( AP )

New Orleans officials also confirmed that a riverboat pilot from the New Orleans-Baton Rouge Steamship Pilots Association was aboard the tanker at the time of the crash.

Specialized pilots routinely board foreign-flagged vessels to help navigate the treacherous stretch of the Mississippi River from the Gulf of Mexico into Louisiana.

Investigators are expected to interview the pilot to determine what went wrong and why the vessel “lost control,” as the mayor described the incident.

U.S. Coast Guard Captain Melanie Burnham told reporters that the tanker may have lost control of its steering, but the cause of the collision is still under investigation.

Louisiana Rep. Troy Carter told New Orleans news outlet WDSU-TV that a national airlines ground stop delayed a forensic team from the federal National Transportation Safety Board from getting to the scene.

The Atlantic Asphalt tanker, at roughly 520 feet, typically carries asphalt and bitumen, which is often used in road and roof construction. Ships carrying those materials are typically heated above 250 degrees Fahrenheit to prevent asphalt from solidifying, though it’s unclear whether the tanker was carrying anything at the time of the crash.

The crash could mark the most serious maritime accident along that stretch of the Mississippi River since 1996, when a cargo ship collided with the Riverwalk Marketplace shopping mall, injuring 66 people.

Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry said officials are working to connect riverboat passengers with their families to get them home; many of the people onboard were not from the New Orleans area.

“As long as they want to stay in New Orleans, and as difficult as it may be getting home, we want to make them very comfortable,” Landry said Friday. “It may take us a couple of days to get them back home.”

News.title: New poll reveals Northern Ireland’s Brexit regret as Burnham eyes ‘win-win’ EU deal
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A decade on from the Brexit referendum, more than half of voters in Northern Ireland favour the UK rejoining the European Union, according to a new public opinion survey.

The latest poll from Queen’s University Belfast also reveals that over three-quarters of respondents would welcome an agreement at an upcoming UK-EU summit to ease controls and checks on goods moving into Northern Ireland from Great Britain.

Conducted on behalf of the university by polling firm LucidTalk, the survey highlights a continuing decline in support for the Windsor Framework, with only 45% viewing it as "on balance a good thing for Northern Ireland" – its lowest rating since June 2021.

Just 44% of participants currently consider the Windsor Framework an effective mechanism for managing the consequences of Brexit in the region, reflecting a sharp drop from 60% recorded in February 2024.

Researchers responsible for the study noted that the data points to persistent fragmentation surrounding post-Brexit arrangements, alongside mounting anxieties over their economic, political, and constitutional ramifications.

The Windsor Framework represents the post-Brexit treaty agreed between London and Brussels to alleviate trade friction between Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham will travel to Brussell next week for a UK-EU summit (PA) ( PA Wire )

The findings come ahead of next week, when Andy Burnham is scheduled to travel to Brussels for a UK-EU summit to sign new accords on food and energy. The prime minister declared on Thursday that he believes a “win-win” deal can be struck with the EU that is closer to the Brexit that was promised a decade ago.

The Queen’s University study is the 16th publication in the Testing The Temperature project, which examines public sentiment regarding Brexit and the Northern Ireland Protocol/Windsor Framework, directed by Professor David Phinnemore and Professor Katy Hayward.

The research was carried out by LucidTalk between October 23 and 26, gathering a weighted sample of 1,050 participants across Northern Ireland.

Findings show that 77% of respondents consider there to be a clear need for a "serious dialogue" concerning the UK’s long-term relationship with the EU.

However, 69% of participants indicated that there is currently insufficient information available to enable an informed public discussion regarding potential UK-EU options.

Almost two-thirds of those surveyed (63%) believe that Brexit has caused far more disruption than they had anticipated back in 2016.

The survey indicates that 52% of Northern Ireland electors agree the UK ought to rejoin the EU under standard member obligations, whereas 38% remain opposed.

Favourability towards rejoining the EU is highest among SDLP (88%), Sinn Féin (86%) and Alliance (83%) voters.

Opposition is led by TUV voters (92%), followed by DUP voters (84%) and UUP voters (63%).

Additionally, the findings reveal that respondents continue to view the Windsor Framework’s impact on political stability in Northern Ireland as predominantly negative (49%), compared to 28% who view it positively.

A larger proportion of voters also continue to perceive the Framework’s effect on Northern Ireland’s position within the UK internal market as negative (44%) rather than positive (27%).

open image in gallery It has been a decade since the UK decided to leave the EU following a referendum ( PA )

Prof Phinnemore said: "Voters in Northern Ireland generally welcome the prospect of the UK having a closer relationship with the EU.

"But with the UK Prime Minister keen to have a ‘serious dialogue’ on where next, it is striking how few, 16%, believe that politicians will be able to debate options in an informed manner.

"Most respondents do not regard Brexit as having been good for the UK. It certainly appears that it has done little to improve trust in politics."

Professor Katy Hayward said: "Our findings suggest that opposition to the Windsor Framework is driven less by resistance to practical cooperation with the EU than by concerns about Northern Ireland’s place in the UK.

"Reducing GB-NI trade barriers through UK-EU agreement attracts support even among those who remain firmly pro-Brexit.

"As the UK Government seeks closer cooperation with the EU that brings tangible benefits, it will be hoping pragmatism outweighs Brexit purism among Leave voters."

News.title: Immigrant families detained in cold and sunless rooms beyond 72-hour limit, advocates say
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Immigrant children are spending up to a month in cold, sunless rooms meant to house them for no more than three days, according to legal advocates charged with ensuring the government abides by a court agreement.

The Center for Human Rights and Constitutional Law, the National Center for Youth Law, and Children's Rights filed a motion Friday afternoon asking a judge to clarify the children’s right to counsel as part of a longstanding court agreement between them and the federal government.

The Justice Department and the U.S. Department of Homeland Security did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Multiple parents held in CBP stations this year in Del Rio, Texas, Laredo, Texas and San Diego, California, reported either no access to a phone call with attorneys or calls that lasted less than five minutes.

Immigrant children in federal custody are protected under the Flores Settlement, a court agreement between the federal government and legal advocates representing immigrant children. It created standards to ensure safe and sanitary conditions in federal custody. It also allows CBP to detain children in their facilities for up to 72 hours. The federal government has a pending appeal with an appellate court to terminate the agreement.

Typically, immigrant children arrested alone or with their families by Border Patrol are processed in temporary stations and then transferred to another agency where they could be placed in long-term detention centers or released with ankle monitors.

Despite a record low number of border arrests, an annual report filed with the court by CBP found that officials took more than the recommended time to process families from March through June, the last month reported. Legal advocates found many children spent weeks and up to a month at these temporary facilities not designed for long-term stays.

Immigrant parents described being held with their children in cold rooms with cement floors and windows that only faced indoors. Lights are kept on all day and night, and many reported losing their sense of time.

“In the morning they bring us a burrito and that’s the way we learn that it is the morning,” one parent held with her teenage daughter in Laredo, Texas, in November said in her declaration. Others said they tried to steal glimpses of wristwatches as agents walked by.

Thin mats and Mylar blankets are provided at night, but one parent said the mats gave her child a rash. She came up with a solution: “At night I lie on my back and I tell him not to touch the mat but to lie on top of me, to sleep on my chest. His rash has gone down since we began sleeping this way, with me as his bed, protecting him.”

Families with young children reported being held in detention pods with no books, toys or television. One mother who was allowed to stay with her four-year-old daughter by her side said they were able to step outside the pod for an hour a day. "That is not enough for a child, to be locked in a cell 23 hours a day,” she said.

Parents were also concerned for their children's well-being. The mother of the four-year-old said her child lost weight in the two weeks of her detention and developed a stutter that only worsened after witnessing a man, handcuffed and chained at the legs and waist, walking out of the facility to be deported.

“She started crying, asking if they would chain her and take us from here the same way. Her stutter increased after that. Every time she thinks of it, she starts to cry again,” the mother said.

News.title: Noel Fielding ‘appalled’ at ‘horrible jokes’ he made with Russell Brand
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Noel Fielding has said he is “appalled” by the “horrible” jokes he had made alongside Russell Brand in the past.

The Great British Bake Off presenter expressed his regret days after Brand, 51, was jailed for 10-and-a-half years after he was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

In a statement to The Sun, Fielding said he was “horrified” by Brand’s crimes and had only ever considered their relationship to be a professional one.

Fielding has not been accused of any wrongdoing and was not linked to Brand’s trial and conviction in any way.

The 53-year-old said: “I was horrified and deeply disturbed to learn of Russell Brand’s crimes, which I was completely unaware of until they became public knowledge. My thoughts are with the women whose courage brought him to justice.

open image in gallery Noel Fielding says he regrets the inappropriate jokes he made alongside Russell Brand ( Getty )

“I appeared on TV, radio and live charity shows with him, and whilst we played it up for the cameras and in the media, I considered it a professional relationship, rather than a personal one. I have had no contact with him for many years.

“Looking back at some of the jokes I made alongside him I was appalled. They were horrible and inappropriate, and I very much regret them.”

A clip of Brand and Fielding joking about rape on the Big Fat Quiz of the Year resurfaced following Brand’s conviction.

The episode, which aired in 2007, saw host Jimmy Carr welcome Rob Brydon, David Mitchell, Jonathan Ross, Fielding and Brand onto the panel alongside singer Lily Allen, who was 21 at the time and the only woman on the show.

“I’m a bit concerned because look where you’ve put us,” Ross tells Carr in the clip: “You’ve put the only sexually attractive young lady – well, the only young lady full stop, she happens to be very attractive as well – near two of the best known cocksmen of the business.” Ross was referring to Brand and Fielding, who were seated to the left of Allen.

open image in gallery The Great British Bake Off presenter said his relationship with Brand was only ‘professional’ ( Channel 4 )

“I’m going to insist as a sort of uncle figure in Lily’s life that she moves over there because obviously that’s the sexless zone,” Ross continues, pointing to Brydon and Mitchell, who looked at one another and nodded in agreement. “And then, Lily might go home with her dress still on.”

Fielding then replies: “How dare you? We’re not rapists.”

Allen later spoke about the uncomfortable moment in an interview 16 years later. “I was on a chat show with Russell Brand and Noel Fielding and Jonathan Ross. And there are comments, I think, about me being raped or something,” she told Grazia in 2023.

“And I laugh along with it. In retrospect, that’s really horrendous. It makes me uncomfortable, but I don’t think I felt that at the time, because it was the culture.”

News.title: UK airports face major disruption as United States grounds all flights
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Air travellers using UK airports are facing widespread disruption following a complete grounding of departures across the United States.

America's Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a nationwide order halting flights "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety".

The knock-on effects are already being felt in Britain, where British Airways cancelled a New York-bound service that had been scheduled to depart London Heathrow at 10.30pm on Friday.

Meanwhile, a Manchester Airport representative stated that three Saturday morning flights heading to the US – all operated by Virgin Atlantic – could face disruption unless the situation is rectified quickly.

A Virgin Atlantic spokesperson said: "We’re aware of the ground stop order issued by the Federal Aviation Administration for all US airports.

"We’re closely monitoring the situation and assessing any impact to our flights. We advise any customers due to travel to check their flight status at virginatlantic.com."

US transportation secretary Sean Duffy confirmed the FAA is currently looking into a communications failure that impacted regional air traffic control facilities, as reported by the Associated Press.

( Reuters )

A nationwide freeze on American flights of this scale has only occurred once before since the September 11 terror attacks in 2001.

Flights were previously halted nationwide by the FAA in January 2023 following a system error.

Reassuring the public, US homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin said: "There is no reason for the public to be afraid or scared for your loved ones. This isn’t another 9/11… This is a telecommunications outage.

"Throughout FAA, out of abundant of caution, we have grounded all the flights, and all the flights are accounted for.

"As incoming flights, either internationally or the flights that are currently still in the air, we’ll be dealing with those case by case.

"As you can imagine, there will be a priority list as they start coming in."

He added: "Everybody is safe. There is no reason to be concerned about your loved ones if they’re flying or anything like that. I just want to make sure everybody’s at ease about that."

He went on: "There is no indication as of yet that this was a nefarious attack against us. It’s just a telecommunication outage as of right now."

A spokesperson for American Airlines said: "The FAA has temporarily paused departures nationwide.

"Flights already in the air can continue to their destinations.

"We expect disruption to our schedule for the rest of the day, depending on the length of the FAA’s nationwide ground stop.

"It will be all hands-on deck across American to get customers on their way as soon as possible when the FAA lifts this ground stop."

News.title: Woman arrested on outstanding warrants moments after she unexpectedly gave birth at home
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A Pennsylvania woman was arrested on outstanding warrants shortly after emergency responders found her newborn inside a toilet bowl following an unexpected home delivery.

She is now facing felony assault and child endangerment charges, according to court documents.

Alyssa Katich, of West Mifflin, was charged with multiple counts of aggravated assault, endangering the welfare of children and prohibited acts, as reported by CBS News.

The incident began on the morning of October 24, when West Mifflin police and Baldwin Emergency Medical Services responded to a medical emergency at a residence on Sylvan Avenue. During the 911 call, Katich told dispatchers she had gone to the bathroom and delivered a baby without knowing she was pregnant.

Katich reported that the infant was crying and covered in blood inside the toilet, adding that she was in shock and unable to pick the child up, according to police audio reviewed during the investigation.

open image in gallery Police arrested a Pennsylvania woman on outstanding warrants after emergency crews pulled her newborn from a toilet following an unexpected home delivery, court documents show (file photo) ( Getty Images )

Responding officers and paramedics removed the newborn from the bowl, administered first aid and unwrapped an umbilical cord that was loosely coiled around the infant’s neck.

Paramedics transported the baby to UPMC Children’s Hospital, where the newborn required intubation and later tested positive for cocaine and cannabinoids, the criminal complaint states. The infant’s condition eventually improved, and doctors removed the breathing tube.

Katich was taken to a separate hospital for treatment. While investigating the incident, police discovered she had two active arrest warrants for failing to appear in court on prior charges in West Mifflin and Munhall and took her into custody.

When officers interviewed Katich at the hospital, she admitted to smoking marijuana and using cocaine, claiming she had found the cocaine while cleaning her bedroom, as reported by CBS News.

Police later executed a search warrant at the Sylvan Avenue home, where they recovered drug paraphernalia, a vial containing brown residue and several marijuana blunts.

Investigators filed the additional charges after completing their review of the case.

News.title: A sudden FAA ground stop strands teams and throws the sports weekend into chaos
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The Federal Aviation Administration's decision to ground all flights nationwide Friday threw the sports world into chaos, leaving NBA, NHL and college teams stranded as they tried to reach their destinations, and NFL teams were left to wonder whether the issue would be resolved in time for them to travel to their games this weekend.

The FAA issued a notice that said the ground stop was “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety."

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy later said there was a communications issue affecting the 22 regional air traffic control centers that direct planes en route between airports nationwide, and that FAA technicians were investigating.

“There’s no reason to be concerned about your loved ones if they’re flying,” Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said.

Most college football teams playing Saturday travel the day before their game, and the stoppage left many schools — including No. 2 Utah, eighth-ranked Texas and No. 9 Tennessee — at a standstill as they departed for road games. The Utes play at No. 22 Arizona, the Longhorns visit No. 24 LSU and the Vols are traveling to Texas A&M in three of the bigger games of the weekend.

In the case of the Longhorns, they posted on social media a short video of them boarding their plane before the stoppage. If they end up taking a bus to Baton Rouge, the trip for the 6:30 p.m. CT kickoff Saturday takes about seven hours.

"We are grounded and waiting to see when we can leave,” a team spokesman said.

Other schools affected by the stoppage included No. 19 Ole Miss, Baylor, Kansas State, Washington and Minnesota.

It also was unclear whether referees, who typically fly to their assignments the day before games, would make it on time.

Several teams were able to take off before the stoppage went into effect, including Missouri, which was flying to No. 1 Georgia; Duke, which was traveling to No. 5 Miami; and No. 10 Texas Tech, which was on the way to Oklahoma State.

Meanwhile, the Nets were among five NBA teams scheduled to fly Friday for games on Saturday. They had just boarded the team plane in New Orleans after playing the Pelicans earlier this week when their flight to Memphis was halted in place.

The Pistons flew earlier in the day to Miami. The Cavaliers, Bulls and Grizzlies play Friday night and were due to fly afterward.

There are 14 scheduled games in the NHL on Saturday. And while the Panthers made it to St. Louis for their game before the stoppage began, the Sharks were among those that were left waiting to leave for their game in Utah.

The FAA did not provide a timeline for restarting flights, leaving sporting events taking place beyond Saturday in limbo. That includes most of the Week 10 schedule in the NFL along with numerous college sporting events.

___

AP Sports Writers Jim Vertuno, Aaron Beard and Tim Reynolds contributed to this report.

Sports.title: Kevin De Bruyne’s wife reveals star will QUIT Napoli ‘the sooner the better’ after rows with boss, team-mates and fans
Sports.content:
Next

KEVIN DE BRUYNE’s wife has revealed he will QUIT Napoli and move back to Belgium.

Michelle, 32, has been with the former Manchester City star since 2014 and got married in 2017.



De Bruyne, 35, made the move to Napoli in 2025 following the end of his iconic time at the Etihad Stadium.

But his time in Italy has not offered him the romantic ending to his career so far.



In his first season, the Belgian has struggled with fitness problems and clash with former manager Antonio Conte.

The arrival of Max Allegri has not seen an improvement in fortune for De Bruyne.

Reports have emerged that he was in a dressing-room bust-up with team-mates.

Michelle has been interviewed by Belgian magazine NINA and revealed that they often speak about returning home.

She said: “Of course, we think about the future together.

“And increasingly often, we say to each other We are going to live here in Limburg.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“The sooner we get here, the better.”

Michelle has claimed that life in Naples has proved difficult for the family.

She added: “Kevin leads a very restricted life in Napoli.

“It’s not much fun for him. Besides, we can’t do anything together as a family in the city. That’s the other side of the coin, isn’t it?

“In Manchester, it was different. Where we lived, people had seen us so often that it wasn’t special anymore.



“We could walk out the door there without a single photo being taken. In Naples, that is impossible.’

“At a certain point, football is no longer the priority.

“You have achieved everything, done everything. Why would you then turn your children’s lives upside down?”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

De Bruyne put pen to paper on a two-year deal at Napoli when he joined last year.

He was made one of the highest-paid players in Italy but his contract is set to expire next summer.

Sports.title: Max Dowman hailed as ‘outstanding’ as Arsenal prodigy breaks Jude Bellingham record for England U21s
Sports.content:
Next

MAX DOWMAN became the youngest-ever England Under-21 player as he made his debut aged just 16.

The teenager’s second-half introduction elicited the loudest cheer of the night at Ashton Gate as Lee Carsley’s side were sunk 1-0 by Portugal.



Dowman’s cameo – hailed as “outstanding” by Carsley – means he has broken the previous record held by Jude Bellingham by almost FOUR MONTHS.

The Arsenal prospect was unable to help turn the tide in England’s favour after being introduced at the hour mark, but still impressed with some classy touches.



England boss Carsley had stressed pre-match that this fixture was a chance to test his side of youngsters against a top side ahead of next summer’s U21 Euros.

It was certainly a test for the Young Lions, facing a Portugal team littered with top-flight players from the Portuguese Primeira, Ligue 1 and further afield.

Divin Mubama tried his luck early on, attempting to lob Portugal goalkeeper Joao Carvalho from 30 yards out after intercepting a wayward pass from Goncalo Oliveira.

But the Southampton loanee misjudged his distance effort and watched it sail well wide of the upright.

And Portugal took advantage before the half-hour mark when Bayer Leverkusen ace Alfonso Moreira wriggled into the box and flashed a venomous effort at Tommy Setford, which the Arsenal prospect effectively turned into his own net in a moment he will want to quickly forget.

It was always going to be an uphill battle from there for England, with Portugal boasting an incredible defence that conceded just TWO GOALS during their 10 European qualification games.

Speaking after the match, Carsley said of Dowman: “We’ve only got three games left before the Euros [next summer].

Former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino was announced as the Red Devils’ new manager on Friday, with the US National team confirming he would be departing for pastures new after taking charge of his final two games over this international break.

Sports.title: Jesus Owono slapped with maximum 12-MATCH ban by Spanish FA over tragic Jesus de Miguel incident
Sports.content:
Next

JESUS OWONO has been slapped with a 12-match ban following the tragic death of Jesus de Miguel.

The Tenerife striker passed away at the age of 30 following a sickening collision with the FC Andorra keeper earlier this month.



And the Disciplinary Committee of the Royal Spanish Football Federation has handed Owono, 25, the maximum suspension.

Article 102 of the disciplinary code, which covers violent conduct during play resulting in injuries or serious consequences, was applied.



But Owono is still considering retiring following his involvement in the horrific incident.

The shot-stopper was sent off after his knee collided with Jesus’ head and chest as he rushed to clear a long ball in stoppage time.



Medics rushed to the Tenerife frontman’s aid following the X-rated challenge in the Segunda Division showdown, which was locked at 2-2.

But Jesus’ condition deteriorated after being transported to hospital and he tragically died less than 24 hours later.

Owono broke his silence by releasing a heartbreaking statement via FC Andorra.

The Equatorial Guinea international said: “These are the most difficult days of my life.



“I am struggling to find the words, and it is very hard for me to process anything that has happened.

“I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I am thinking of him, his family, and all the people who loved him.

“I know there will be many matters to address, and I will face whatever comes with complete respect.



“But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything other than Jesus and the grief we are experiencing.

“Rest in peace, Jesus.”

After linking up for the international break, Spain’s big-name stars paid an emotional tribute to Jesus before their first training session.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino is £10m gamble for Man Utd.. he must take sledgehammer to toxic culture and follow Arsenal blueprint
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED have taken a £10million gamble in appointing Mauricio Pochettino — and it will be fascinating to watch.

This is one last shot for Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada, who have cocked up almost every big call they have made without being held to account by the owners.



Pochettino departs America, where I am based, with very little outcry from fans here that he is leaving.

But as he heads over the Atlantic on his jet in the next few days, picking over the squad with his staff there will be one overriding thought: ‘Holy f***, we’ve got a lot of work to do’.



I played against Pochettino’s Tottenham team, one of the hardest games each year for us in the Premier League. They had quality in bundles, but also togetherness, depth and — above all — intensity.

Getting that out of this Manchester United squad feels nearly impossible, which is why the biggest question is whether Pochettino and United are actually a good fit.

The Argentine is known across football for working his players hard, right to the edge — getting them fit as a fiddle but sometimes making them physically sick.

And here he is faced with a group who cannot seem to stay fit.

Carlos Baleba has arrived and broken down, Harry Maguire comes off constantly and Luke Shaw — who Pochettino was like a father to at Southampton — can no longer be relied upon. That relationship will be different now he’s plagued by injuries.

Even further forward, big signings like Benjamin Sesko — he is never around and has knees as reliable as mine!



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

These players are about to get the biggest volley up the backside they have ever experienced — and I doubt they will be able to handle it.

You look at the team he built at Spurs, with Moussa Dembele, Dele Alli and Christian Eriksen. Can anyone in this United squad match or replicate their skill set? No.

But beyond a huge squad rebuild and a lack of quality, we all know the underlying problem at Old Trafford.

We have enough evidence now to know Jose Mourinho cannot be wrong, Louis van Gaal cannot be wrong. Ralf Rangnick, Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim all saw it.

Poch must go in and take a huge sledgehammer to the toxic Carrington culture, accepting that things are not good enough.



Managers and those above need to stop fiddling around the edges and tackle the big problem, otherwise there will be no progress.

United supporters might not like it, but Arsenal have shown the way and offered the blueprint. Rather than repeating what has failed, they must make a brave change. Someone big has to go, even if it means short-term pain.

Mesut Ozil, Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Alexandre Lacazette were pushed out for the benefit of everyone.



They were good players but carried a stink with them around the place.

Cut them out and everyone else can breathe, focus in training and start growing.

For the Red Devils, that has to be someone like skipper Bruno Fernandes or, once again, Marcus Rashford.

They cannot move on players like Jadon Sancho or Tyrell Malacia any more — no one really cares about them.

I can guarantee it now, Rashford will suddenly be fit for the Liverpool game. He will see a new manager who likes energy and pace, he will think he can do all that.



He might even start well, get a few games, but then Pochettino will ask for more and he will not like it.

Then all the bad traits will come back — he’ll be out and about and late for training all over again. The cycle begins and the damage returns.

Pochettino must make a statement, give these players until January to prove they are on board or get rid.

LIVE REACTION AS POCH ANNOUNCED AS NEW BOSS

He has to set standards for everyone else to follow. The big challenge is, he must win alongside doing that.



The former Chelsea chief feels like a halfway house between the two other standout candidates, Eddie Howe and Antonio Conte.

He has the tactical acumen and man-management of Howe, with the edge of Conte, without the risk that he will bring the house of cards down with a tantrum.

That feels like a smart route for United to go down in one sense, but he remains a gamble, seven years since he saw real success in the Premier League.

It will, as always at Old Trafford, be quite the ride.

Sports.title: Chelsea have new owner, Ukraine is still at war.. Roman Abramovich’s £2.5bn sale money still sitting in bank is disgrace
Sports.content:
Next

THERE is an extraordinary postscript to Roman Abramovich’s ownership of Chelsea Football Club.

He has gone, the club has been sold, the new owners have spent a fortune trying to make their mark, players have come and gone, managers too, and yet one thing remains stubbornly stuck in the past.



The £2.5billion from the sale is still sitting in a UK bank account, unable to reach the people it was supposed to help.

Four years. That is how long it has taken for a promise to become an exercise in bureaucracy, legal wrangling and political buck-passing.



And the people who are paying the price are not lawyers, bankers or billionaires — they are the victims of the war in Ukraine.

When Abramovich was forced to sell Chelsea in 2022, following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and the sanctions imposed on him by the British government, he said the proceeds would be donated to a charitable foundation to help victims of the war.



A gesture that could make a genuine difference to thousands of lives. Yet here we are and the money has still not been handed over.

I was told at the time by someone very senior at Chelsea that Abramovich’s private jet was permanently positioned on the runway, ready for a possible escape.

It was an image of a man whose world was changing very quickly. But where does he go now?

Russia is perhaps the obvious destination, although it is not somewhere I can visit.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

I am, for reasons I have never quite understood, on the Russian government’s list of people banned from entering the country.

I can only assume I must have said something they didn’t like.

Abramovich, though, has not disappeared from the diplomatic picture. Earlier this year Volodymyr Zelensky reportedly invited him to Kyiv to carry a message to Vladimir Putin about direct peace talks.

He may have a genuine desire to help end the conflict. One might also observe that having billions of pounds of assets frozen gives a man a fairly compelling personal interest in a change.

Whatever his motivation, his involvement raises an obvious question: if he can help broker conversations about peace, why has he not managed to resolve the much simpler matter of the money?



The issue was raised again in the House of Lords this week.

The government confirmed that it had issued a licence in December last year providing a legal route for the £2.5bn to be transferred to a foundation for humanitarian purposes in Ukraine.

But the Charity Commission is still considering the foundation’s application and the government says it is prepared to go to court if necessary. After four years.

There is also a dispute over £1.4bn in loans allegedly owed to offshore companies linked to Abramovich.

The government maintains the full proceeds should go towards humanitarian purposes in Ukraine.



That is precisely why the money needs proper scrutiny — but scrutiny cannot become an excuse for paralysis. And while the lawyers argue, the bank account is doing rather nicely.

The money is understood to have generated at least £175MILLION in interest while sat in Barclays.

But what exactly is taking so long? If the government has a legal route, why has it not been used to bring this saga to an end?



If Abramovich has made a commitment, why has he not honoured it?

And if there are genuine legal obstacles, why can’t the public be given a clearer explanation?

At some point, somebody has to stop passing the parcel and take responsibility.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Chelsea have a new owner. Abramovich has a new life under sanctions. Ukraine still has a war.

The one thing that hasn’t changed is the money. It is still sitting there.

And that, more than anything, is a disgrace.

Sports.title: McGinn double seals win for ragged Scotland
Sports.content:
Match report as John McGinn scores twice in Scotland's win over North Macedonia at Hampden; Aston Villa midfielder gives hosts lead after McTominay and Gilmour go close; Rastoder's header levels scoring; McGinn penalty seals win after Gannon-Doak fouled; Scotland face Switzerland next

John McGinn's double rescued Scotland as they toiled to a 2-1 win over North Macedonia to keep their Nations League promotion hopes alive.

The hosts were booed off at half-time with the game goalless but there was a sense of relief - rather than joy - at the final whistle after McGinn's penalty secured the three points after Elmin Rastoder's header cancelled out the Aston Villa midfielder's opener.

The win means Scotland can still finish second in Group B1 after Slovenia were held by Switzerland, but will have to win in St Gallen on Monday and hope North Macedonia do them a favour in their final game.

Image: Andy Robertson equalled Sir Kenny Dalglish's appearance record

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli secured his first win at Hampden on a night when skipper Andy Robertson earned his 102nd cap to equal the appearance record held by Sir Kenny Dalglish.

The returning Scott McTominay nearly grabbed an opener after 16 minutes but he was denied by Stole Dimitrievski in the North Macedonia goal after turning and shooting sharply. The keeper then denied Che Adams and McTominay again before the Napoli midfielder attempted to recreate his famous Denmark overhead kick to no avail.

Boos rang around Hampden as the players trudged off at the interval and Billy Gilmour did little to lift the collective mood straight after the break when he fired over with the goal gaping following good work by Adams.

Image: Scotland's Scott McTominay goes close

Scotland did take the lead soon after, however, Adams outmuscling his North Macedonian counterpart to set the onrushing McGinn away into the box before he curled his effort into the net.

Rastoder stunned Hampden less than three minutes later, leaping highest to glance his header past Angus Gunn from a corner, but Dimitrievski went from hero to villain with a little over 15 minutes remaining, bringing down Ben Gannon-Doak when the winger seemed to be running the ball out of play.

Image: North Macedonia's Elmin Rastoder scored to make it 1-1 against Scotland

A VAR review followed, allowing McGinn to step up and deliver a first win in Glasgow for Pocognoli, but it is a performance that will raise more questions than answers.

The key moments from Hampden Park

16: BIG SAVE! Scott McTominay controls the ball with his back to the goal, then turns sharply and shoots but Stole Dimitrievski gets down well to his left and keeps it out.

22: OVER! Andy Robertson delivers a free-kick into the box but Kieran Tierney's header loops over the bar.

27: SAVE! John McGinn's corner is met by Che Adams at the front post before his header takes a big deflection. It looks like it's heading in but Dimitrievski is equal to it again.

35: OVER! McTominay tries an acrobatic effort with an overhead kick but it sails over the bar and out of play.

39: MCTOMINAY DENIED! The ball is threaded into the feet of McTominay and he shoots from a tight angle but the goalkeeper makes another save to keep it level!

46: HOW HAS HE MISSED?! Adams capitalises on a loose back pass and squares the ball to Billy Gilmour. All he has to do is guide it on target and it is a goal but he skies it over the bar!

54: GOAL! Adams outmuscles the defender before poking the ball forward allowing McGinn to race onto it before curling the opener into the back of the net.

57: GOAL! North Macedonia shock Scotland with a quickfire equaliser. The corner is whipped into the box and Rastoder is there to glance it into the bottom corner.

75: GOAL! McGinn scores from the spot to restore Scotland's lead

Pocognoli 'satisfied' with first home win

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sebastien Pocognoli was pleased after his first home win with Scotland against North Macedonia in the Nations League, hoping that it will 'helps build a winning culture'.

Scotland head coach Sebastian Pocognoli:

"I'm happy to get the first win at home. It's important and we knew before the game that it will help to build a winning culture.

"In terms of what we produced on the pitch, I know exactly what we worked on this week. I'm quite satisfied about what I saw in some moments of the game, the work on the ball and off the ball.

"It was not always perfect, but I know that what we worked on in the last two days happened many times on the pitch. And for me that's very important. On top of that, we created a lot of chances that we should score.

"Off the ball, I think we were quite aggressive. We recovered a number of balls that we managed well in some moments of transition. We created a big chance for Billy (Gilmour) from this also. So that's a new approach of the game. Not everything was perfect, but there was a lot to take to move forward.

Image: Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli was satisfied with the win over North Macedonia

"After the first goal, I think we need to learn to not drop the intensity. Because after the first goal, for five minutes, I really feel like we dropped the intensity and the focus. And we conceded a goal from a set-piece. And I had the same feeling after the second goal. So, it's something that we need to fix."

Robertson: We have to be patient with new style

Scotland captain Andy Robertson speaking to BBC Sport:

"I thought we showed glimpses of good stuff. We tried to be patient on the ball, tried to keep the ball, I think we did that well at times, but also at times it broke down because the quality wasn't there at times so we're still trying to piece it all together.

Image: Andy Robertson says Scotland are adapting to a new style

"It's a different way of playing and that's what we are working on in the training ground. It wasn't always perfect, but no international game is easy and we're all delighted in the changing room to get that win and hopefully other people have a smile on their face too.

"Every formation can be played differently, there are so many different variations of this formation. We're trying to implement what the manager and coaches want us to do on the training ground and we're working really hard.

"Yes, it's not going to be perfect right away but everything is working towards us going into the qualifiers for the Euros. We're still trying to learn it and we believe in what the manager is trying to teach us to do and we have to be patient with that.

"I know people don't see us train and see the work we're doing in the background, so I can get why people are frustrated but there is an idea behind what we are doing and like you say at times we lacked that quality.

Image: Andy Robertson applauds the fans after Scotland's win over North Macedonia

"Obviously the Slovenia at home game made it unrealistic, or tougher [to qualify]. We'll go over to Monday and we'll give everything we can to win that game. We're in a position where we have to rely on other results."

On equaling Dalglish's appearance record: "It feels amazing for me and my family, it's an amazing achievement. I've been around here for a long time. I've had highs, I've had lows, I've sometimes had praise and had criticism."

McGinn praises 'amazing' Robertson

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player John McGinn hails Andy Robertson after he matched Kenny Dalglish’s caps record against North Macedonia.

John McGinn to Sky Sports on Andy Robertson's record-equalling night:

"Amazing - he deserves everything that is coming his way. The biggest credit I can give him is that he is always available, always willing to help his country. Whether he is at 60, 70, 80 per cent, or 100.

"I'm sure Monday will be a special occasion for him but he'll give the boring answer that it will only be special if we get three points."

Analysis: McGinn takes centre stage on record-equalling night for Robertson

It will be a night that Andy Robertson never forgets but a game most Scotland fans will blank from their collective memories fairly quickly.

Image: Andy Robertson and John McGinn celebrate after Scotland's win

The skipper equalled Sir Kenny Dalglish's record of 102 caps but it was fellow Scotland stalwart John McGinn who spared the home side's blushes on a drab evening in Glasgow.

Scotland looked slow in their build-up, even if there were first-half chances, but when the goal finally did come the floodgates did not open. Instead, North Macedonia, who hadn't scored since November 18, 2025, equalised and could have gone in front.

The natives were understandably restless but were ultimately relieved when Stole Dimitrievski clumsily brought down Gannon-Doak, allowing McGinn to be the hero again.

Image: Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli celebrates

The Aston Villa captain was quick to remind everyone that a new style takes time to bed in and that is true. Scotland are moving away from the comforts and success of the Steve Clarke era, but questions will be asked of Pocognoli's insistence on using wing-backs and one upfront at home with a comfortable win expected.

Scotland have something to play for when they travel to Switzerland for their final Group B1 game, with promotion still up for grabs. Robertson should play on Monday to become Scotland's most-capped player outright. How sweet it would be if his 103rd appearance for his country was a winning one.

Sports.title: France put injuries behind them to stun Springboks
Sports.content:
Nations Championship - France 21-19 South Africa: Les Bleus put injuries behind them to hold on and stun Springboks in Paris

Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang was among the try-scorers as France pulled off an epic victory over South Africa

France put a raft of injuries behind them to withstand huge pressure and defeat South Africa 21-19 in a stunning Nations Championship victory in Paris.

The win is only the second for Les Bleus over the Springboks in the last 11 contests, with the hosts playing sensationally in the first half and digging in to survive and get over the line in the second.

Back-three Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, Théo Attissogbe and Louis Bielle-Biarrey each scored tries in the opening half, with France belying the fact they had to play Antoine Dupont at 10 due to four fly-halves being out injured (Matthieu Jalibert, Romain Ntamack, Thomas Ramos, Antoine Hastoy).

All three tries were converted by Maxime Lucu, with France 21-7 ahead at the half-time break, but the second half proved entirely different.

France 21-19 South Africa - Score summary France - Tries: Grandidier-Nkanang (15), Attissogbe (24), Bielle-Biarrey (32). Cons: Lucu (16,24,33). South Africa - Tries: Wessels (30), Reinach (51), Marx (72). Cons: Feinberg-Mngomezulu (31,52).

Though South Africa were shown a 20-minute red card to back-row Cobus Wiese for an illegal ruck clear-out, France coughed up sin-bins to Lucu, Grandidier-Nkanang and Régis Montagne - the latter as a result of scrum penalties which kept flowing the visitors' way.

Scrum-half Cobus Reinach and hooker Malcom Marx scored tries in the second half for South Africa - adding to a first-half Jan-Hendrik Wessels effort - but Manie Libbok crucially missed the third conversion and the chance to draw level.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

South Africa's wholesale front-row changes less than an hour before kick-off - swapping their starting front-row for their replacements - had ​little impact on France's fast start, with Dupont floating between fly-half and scrum-half from the off in a marvellous individual performance.

The match was considered a potential preview of the final at Twickenham in two weeks, but while France are closing in on representing the northern hemisphere - England and Ireland are now six points behind with two games to play - South Africa may not make it.

The Springboks will be overtaken atop the southern hemisphere standings and lose their No 1 world ranking if undefeated New Zealand beat Wales on Saturday in Cardiff, as expected.

On Friday, the Springboks closed to 21-14 with 30 minutes to go, revving up their power game for a grandstand finish.

France were bleeding penalties - nine in the scrum alone - but desperate scramble defence roused a packed Stade de France.

South Africa's Pieter-Steph du Toit was held up over the try-line late on, while Lucu - France's goalkicker with an 85 per cent success rate - ramped up the tension when he missed a straightforward penalty attempt that would have given France a 10-point lead.

Springboks hooker Marx inevitably scored from a rolling maul but Libbok, on for Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, botched the conversion attempt that would have levelled the score with eight minutes left.

The Boks had one last chance in the final minute, but Bielle-Biarrey stopped the charge and Dupont jumped on the loose ball, earning Lucu the chance to kick out and end a gripping Test match.

Dupont: We kept intensity up the whole match - 'That's huge for us'

France fly-half Antoine Dupont told ITV:

"I feel tired! They [South Africa] are really intense during the 80 minutes.

"It was so hard today with the yellow cards. We kept the intensity the whole game, and that's a huge thing for us today.

"We tried to adapt [Dupont at fly-half], we just had one day of training this week.

"I tried with Max [Lucu] to have the best combination possible. In attack and defence.

"With the energy of the entire team, it worked."

What's next?

For France, they next face Argentina in their third Nations Championship Test of the autumn at the Stade de France in Paris on Saturday, November 21 (8.10pm kick-off).

South Africa travel to face Ireland at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin for their next Test, also on Saturday November 21 (4.40pm kick-off).

Sports.title: Choi pushing for first LPGA win at The Annika as Korda drops back
Sports.content:
Hye-Jin Choi opened with two bogeys, made up ground with a 15-foot eagle putt late and finished with a three-under 67 on Friday that gave her part of a three-way share of the lead at The Annika.

It was far more effective than the bogey-free round of Nelly Korda, the No. 1 player who could only laugh at her clean card because it was cleaner than she would have preferred - 15 straight pars, one birdie, two closing pars for a 69.

That left Korda four shots behind going into the weekend at Pelican Golf Club, where a victory would make the 28-year-old American eligible for the LPGA Hall of Fame.

"I had a lot of chances," said Korda, competing for the first time in two months. "But you can just tell that from yesterday morning to today afternoon with the wind, that's what the defence of this golf course is. It's as fast as Bermuda as I've putted on throughout my career."

It wasn't a problem for Solheim Cup star Carlota Ciganda, who birdied her last four holes for a 63 to join Choi and Lindy Duncan (66) atop the leaderboard at 12-under 128.

Image: Nelly Korda has dropped further behind the leaders. (AP Photo/Chris O'Meara)

The Japanese duo of Mao Saigo (65) and Minami Katsu (69) were two shots behind.

Choi has been an LPGA member for five years and it has been a curious chase for that first LPGA victory, particularly since she was 17 when she had a late lead in the 2017 US Women's Open and wound up as a runner-up.

She also had two good chances at winning during the recent Asia swing, where she was runner-up in Shanghai and South Korea.

Choi was playing in the group with Korda for the opening two rounds, which she believes has tested her enough to calm her nerves on the weekend. She wasn't rattled by the bogey-bogey start, or the bogey on the par-five 14th, her fifth hole of the round.

She pieced together enough birdies to regain some momentum, then hit an approach that got a nice kick around the green and rolled out to just under 15 feet for eagle on the par-five seventh.

"I have two rounds left, but I have recently played in a champion group on the tournament before, so I have that experience and I'm going just try my best and concentrate on my game," Choi said.

Scoring was low enough in the opening round that one-under 139 made the cut. This is the final regular-season event of the year, and the top 60 in the Race to CME Globe advance to the finale next week in Naples, where the winner gets $2 million.

Julia Lopez Ramirez of Spain, who defeated Yealimi Noh in a crucial singles match in her Solheim Cup debut, was among those at nine-under 131. That was important for the Spaniard, who came into the week at No. 66 in the Race to the CME Globe.

Image: Charley Hull was five shots off the leaders on seven-under. (AP Photo/Chris O'Meara)

Duncan, the 35-year-old Floridian, has yet to win on the LPGA Tour and this was the first time she had at least a share of the lead through 36 holes. She went 2-1 in her Solheim Cup debut.

"The week has gone by really fast, which is sometimes a good thing," Duncan said. "Because if you're playing a lot and you get some momentum going, that's kind of a nice way to play. So it's just been kind of rolling with it."

Charley Hull was five shots off the leaders on seven-under after shooting 67 on Friday. England's Lottie Woad finished the second round level with Hull on seven-under.

Sports.title: England respond to Jones' mind games ahead of Japan match
Sports.content:
England have hit back at Eddie Jones' claim they could be vulnerable to an upset by Japan on Saturday because they have one eye on their upcoming game with New Zealand.

Jones is aiming to disrupt Steve Borthwick's side by hitting them with the unexpected in the belief they will be "a little bit distracted" by the All Blacks' visit to Allianz Stadium on November 21.

New Zealand are the box-office fixture of the campaign ahead of finals weekend but England deny they are looking beyond Japan.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Japan head coach Eddie Jones fired England a warning to 'expect the unorthodox' ahead of the reunion with their former coach

"That's nowhere near the case because we understand how important this game is," scrum coach Tom Harrison said.

"We understand the challenge Japan can throw at us and we have to be alive in every single moment to the type of rugby they play.

"We understand that there might be unorthodox things coming our way but our need is to be alive.

"I've never worked with Eddie but I've met him a few times and he's a rugby genius, the way he thinks about the game and the way the players talk about him."

Murley: My best rugby will get me in the mix

Image: Cadan Murley is aiming to make an impression on Steve Borthwick

Cadan Murley wins his eighth cap but first at Twickenham after coming in for the injured Immanuel Feyi-Waboso on the left wing as one of 10 changes made for Japan.

Murley, Max Ojomoh and Will Joseph are aiming to make an impression on Borthwick after the head coach signalled that places in next year's World Cup squad are up for grabs.

"I just want go out there and play my best rugby," Murley said. "I'll focus on what I can do, control the controllables, and hopefully that will get me in the mix further down the line.

"But my sole focus is on this game and putting my best foot forward. It's my first game at Twickenham and that's what's on my mind at the moment."

Sports.title: Tearful Pochettino admits he 'couldn't say no to Man Utd'
Sports.content:
An emotional Mauricio Pochettino said that leaving his role with the United States was the "toughest decision of his career" but admitted he couldn't turn down the chance to become head coach of Manchester United.

Pochettino has been appointed as Michael Carrick's replacement at Old Trafford having signed a deal until the summer of 2029. It comes mere months after extending his stay with the USMNT until the 2030 World Cup.

The Argentine will begin his new role on November 18, after taking charge of the USA's two fixtures against Haiti.

Speaking in his pre-match press conference before his penultimate game, Pochettino broke down in tears as he explained his decision.

"In some part, this is a very sad decision. In another part, we are professionals. This is the next step to try and make your dreams come true," the former Spurs and Chelsea boss said.

"It all happened so quickly. By Sunday afternoon there was contact. You always were transparent and always tried to build something together. We learned a lot from you all, this amazing country and you amazing people. This is one of the most difficult decisions of my career. Thank you so much."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Rob Dorsett explains why Pochettino could be set for a busy January transfer window

Pochettino last held a club role in Europe during his one-season stint at Chelsea, which came to an end in 2024. When asked why he had opted to leave his post to return to the Premier League, Pochettino didn't hide the fact that taking the Old Trafford hot seat was a once in a lifetime opportunity.

"It's obvious," Pochettino added. "They [US Soccer Federation] know that not many opportunities can happen in your career like a side the size of Manchester United.

"When that arrives, it's difficult to turn down."

Liverpool

Manchester United Sunday 22nd November 4:00pm Kick off 4:30pm

Pochettino explains why he is staying for two more games

Pochettino will start life at Carrington following the international break, and will have three training sessions with the players before the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

The new head coach admitted that he would have started sooner if asked to, but explained why he wanted to see out the remainder of this camp.

"I am a professional person and the emotional link between us we have built in this two years is to show the commitment and respect and care and love," Pochettino said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports's Rob Dorsett explains why Pochettino has a VERY busy few days ahead of him

"Even if we take a decision which is not the best for one part, we've always been open. We have the respect of the players and staff, they understand the situation.

"Of course, if Manchester United and the federation agreed different terms, I would have respected between both. But this happened and of course, all the games are important.

"The last four games were important. We gave debuts to 13 players, before the cup I thought everyone had different ideas about it but we believe in the programme and are brave enough to go ahead. We're always optimistic and positive.

"After this camp, with four victories, we've been consistent in the same way, win or lose. We believe in the programme. It's an honour for us to be here, defend our patch and our players.

"We need to play tomorrow and the next game. We're not thinking in the future, it's about performing. We're very optimistic and it's a natural way to finish our partnership."

Emotional Poch rediscovered motivation in USA

Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol:

"We've always known Mauricio Pochettino is an emotional person. He wears his heart on his sleeve. But I don't think you would normally expect a manager to break down and be so emotional in a press conference when he was leaving the USA to manage Manchester United.

"But that just tells you about the kind of guy he is because he's all about personal relationships. And obviously, he's made some very good friends in the US.

"He also said: 'We recovered our motivation here'. He was quite hurt and bruised by what happened to him at PSG and at Chelsea. It's almost like he's rediscovered his motivation by working in the US. And now he's ready to come back to the Premier League."

Carrick’s unintentional advice to Pochettino

In the wake of the announcement of Pochettino as the new head coach at Old Trafford, his predecessor Michael Carrick penned an emotional farewell off the back of his sacking on Wednesday.

Carrick took to social media to thank supporters saying, “you've shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way".

In his post, the former Red Devils midfielder also lent an inadvertent word of advice for his replacement, giving an insight into what life is like at the club.

Sports.title: Riley determined to prove himself a world champion in waiting
Sports.content:
Viddal Riley will put himself on a path to a cruiserweight world title shot, if he can defend the European championship against Seydi Coupe on Saturday.

Only 14 fights into his pro career, Riley is already rated as the IBF's No. 2 contender for their world championship.

The Londoner wants to showcase himself as a world champion in waiting against Coupe.

"I think I'm the most well-rounded cruiserweight in the world," Riley told Sky Sports.

"I think we've trained for that because we want to cover every aspect of the game. We don't want to be lacking any area when it comes to movement, speed, IQ. All these things, I have them."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look back at Viddal Riley's best knockouts.

The IBF belt is currently vacant with Riley and New Zealand's David Nyika ranked one and two. Sooner or later a world title fight would surely lie ahead of Riley, if he's victorious.

"He's in the way. We can't worry about the other side of the door until we get past the doorman," Riley said of Coupe.

"I'm trying to get in the club, Seydi's asking for my ID at the door, I have to show him my ID or pull him out the way and get into the club."

It's a fight Riley is determined to dominate.

"I believe this will be a stoppage victory," the Londoner said. "You can't stop everybody, I'm aware of that as well. I won't be disappointed per se if I don't stop him. I'll be disappointed if I don't batter him.

"I just want to show for 12 rounds at least, it's not the level. We're completely different levels and I do, contrary to belief, possess good punch power."

Sports.title: Tearful Pochettino says United job was ‘difficult to turn down’ in USMNT farewell
Sports.content:
There were always going to be tears at Mauricio Pochettino’s news conference at US Soccer’s national training center on Friday. It was only a matter of when. Pochettino is famously emotional, and nobody in attendance had to wait long for the waterworks – they came during his introductory remarks, as he thanked the US Soccer executives flanking him for the opportunity to guide the US men. He grew emotional again as he addressed his impending departure for Manchester United, one announced just hours earlier.

“I think [the decision was],” Pochettino said, pausing to compose himself, “one of the most difficult decisions of our careers. Thank you guys. Thank you so much.”

The news conference read very much as a farewell to Pochettino, but there is still work to be done. The Argentinian will guide the USMNT through a pair of Concacaf Nations League quarter-final matches against Haiti on Saturday and Tuesday. In the meantime, the future United coach did his best to address questions about his departure and what comes next.

“These moments are not easy decisions,” a reflective Pochettino told the media. “Normally it’s the opposite. Normally you get sacked and you cry because you want to stay and you’re sacked by [the club]. It’s a tough decision but at the same time we are excited for the next step forward.”

Pochettino characterized United’s interest and negotiations as having come together at the last minute, essentially, with contact between the two sides first made Sunday.

“We cannot underestimate the staff and the players. When things became big and big and big, the players are very sensitive and the staff are too – they start to feel things as well. [Everything] was so quick, because we arrived here last Friday and Sunday afternoon this situation started to appear and some contact. We were very transparent, we were talking with [US Soccer CEO] JT [Batson] and the federation.”

Details were quickly ironed out between the sides, with the club and federation agreeing Pochettino would remain with the US through the upcoming matches.

“[Thursday], when things were positive in the way the agreement was, we had a meeting and I communicated to the players and the whole staff. I want to say thank you because they were very supportive and they really understand the situation and they know us – how committed we are for the next two games. The decision between the federation and Manchester United, to agree that we’ll continue with our job in the camp; [nothing] can change our commitment and how important the next two games are.”

Pochettino bids tearful farewell to USA after Manchester United appointment – video

Pochettino and the US federation touted his contract renewal in August as the start of something new and significant, with the coach given a larger role in the overall direction of the US men at every level. That went by the wayside when United came knocking.

“They know that there are not too many opportunities that can happen in your career like [this one with Manchester United],” Pochettino said. “When they arrive, it’s difficult to turn down. But I want to make it clear, when we decided together to [stay another four years], it was always the commitment for the federation, too. Maybe the four games [in the September/October window] if we lose them, maybe you start to put pressure [on me]. And maybe something can be in a different way.

“Or even in the future,” he continued, “Things can happen. The federation and maybe new people arrive or don’t, or maybe have different ideas and you say, ‘We are thinking in different directions’ and maybe they say ‘Mauricio, maybe you need to go home.’ We cannot think in these extremes – I think we were very committed and never thought this would happen so quickly.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Pochettino was joined by Batson and US Soccer president Cindy Parlow Cone on Friday. Batson was pressed on what will happen with the approximately $10m (£7.5m) Manchester United paid out for Pochettino’s services. A significant portion of Pochettino’s $6m salary was subsidized by billionaire hedge fund manager and US Soccer donor Ken Griffin. It’s unclear whether that generosity will extend towards Pochettino’s successor.

“The agreement with Manchester United, those funds – as you all know, US Soccer is a nonprofit and those funds are used to help us hire great coaches,” Batson said. “They help us do youth national team programs, coaching education … those funds are available for us to invest in order for us to make the biggest impact on our goals. Our supporters, our sponsors, our donors, are fans are very supportive around making sure that we have the resources that we need to achieve our goals, including having a world-class coach. We are appreciative of that support and look forward to our way of winning going forwards.”

Pochettino’s legacy, of course, is still to be defined. He was by no means a generational influence on the state of soccer in the US but he will be remembered fondly, by many, for a handful of standout performances and for guiding the US to a respectable, albeit disappointing, last-16 finish at this summer’s World Cup.

Pochettino was reluctant at first to define his own legacy, telling reporters he was “not arrogant” before jokingly conceding that he is “well, a little bit arrogant, but not too much.”

“We don’t take a project to be remembered forever,” Pochettino said, “and to have a picture here at the training center. It’s the impact on the human being. It’s for us to be a good partner and, through the vision of the federation, to add our quality and knowledge of the game and to be part of this family. I hope, in Manchester United, to do the same. That is what we can do – add our expertise about soccer … The key factor, though, that can have a key influence is the human being.”

Sports.title: ‘United is broken’: Guardian readers react to Michael Carrick’s sacking
Sports.content:
“As a United fan who was around for the early 90s seeing Carrick go is a sad end to a horrible situation. He was the only likable thing about the club … I took my eight-year-old lad to Old Trafford for the Brighton game in the FA Cup in January and I’ve never experienced a more toxic atmosphere at a football ground. The fans deserve better … Better owners, better attitudes, better standards. Nothing will change with the setup of the club today and we are in this macabre holding pattern of failure, hope, anger and disappointment” – Chris

“Wilcox, [Berada] and [Jim] Ratcliffe should have fired themselves. They are the common denominator of all this failure. [Mauricio] Pochettino will last 12 months if he’s lucky” – Deb

“I have been a United supporter for over 60 years and this sacking just depresses me. Everyone knows the problem lies elsewhere … We were in desperate need of a left-back and centre-half. What did they do? Recruit several midfielders. So it starts again. Does anyone really believe changing manager will make any difference?” – Barry

“This feels sadder than every other time it’s happened since Alex Ferguson retired. Each of the previous managers had to go, as in large part the underperformance felt like it was their fault. This doesn’t feel like that … But, because the owners and executives aren’t going to sack themselves, and because you can’t fire the players, you change the only thing you can: the manager. And then repeat the cycle” – John

“I think it was Jonathan Liew who made the eminently sensible suggestion of a positional switch for Michael Carrick – by having him replace Jason Wilcox as director of football. That would have made sense” – Geoff

View image in fullscreen Manchester United minority shareholder Sir Jim Ratcliffe (left), CEO Omar Berrada (centre) and technical director Jason Wilcox. Photograph: Jacob King/PA

“Just waiting for Mr Mediocrity Wilcox to do the honourable thing and admit he is out of his depth and responsible in part for the situation and resign” – Andrew

“Since Fergie left there have been 12 managers at United, including interims, with little reward. Can all of these have been wrong? Surely they could not have been? It highlights the systemic failures of the club at all levels” – Simon

“Carrick remains a Manchester United legend, he will always be. Without corresponding changes in the club’s recruitment process and the people driving it, we will be back here after 12-18 months” – Wale

“There are many problems at United but the biggest is short-termism. Carrick, like Ole Gunnar Solskjær, was given the permanent job because he did a good job as caretaker, but those roles are very different. Building for the long term, even at a well-run club with solid foundations, is different from getting the best from the hand you’ve been dealt over a few months. Since Fergie retired managers have been sacked because results have taken a downturn, and those who’ve suggested things might need to get worse before they get better (Ralf Rangnick and Ruben Amorim) have been shown the door. There are no reasons to think it will be any different for Pochettino” – Jason

“Is Pochettino a good manager? He did well at Spurs – albeit without winning anything – and in a short spell at Southampton but that was a long time ago. Since then his record has been pretty underwhelming, up to and including an uninspiring time in charge of the US men’s team. He just seems to have a reputation as a good manager but I’m not really sure what it’s based on any more” – Jon

“The similarities between ENIC’s ownership of Tottenham and the Glazers stewardship of United are striking. It doesn’t bode well for United given Tottenham’s unprecedented two-and-a-half decades of underachievement since then. The main difference, further bad news for United, is that Tottenham’s perilous debt load primarily funded a new stadium rather than facilitating the owners’ stake in the company and subsequent dividends to themselves. Football clubs can’t withstand money being extracted – it all has to be re-invested to keep the wheels turning” – Paul
