World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: 32 passengers taken to hospital after tanker hits river cruise boat in US
World.content:
Officials have not said if anyone was hurt after American Heritage was partially submerged with 129 passengers on board.

Share 32 passengers taken to hospital after tanker hits river cruise boat in US on social media

Dozens of passengers have been taken to hospital after a tanker struck a river cruise boat carrying 129 passengers in New Orleans, partially submerging the vessel, according to authorities.

The Atlantic Asphalt tanker hit the American Heritage paddleboat on the Mississippi River on Friday at about 12:30pm local time (18:30 GMT), the Port of New Orleans said.

The cruise boat had docked about two hours earlier to begin letting passengers off.

New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference on Friday evening that all passengers on board the American Heritage were accounted for and that 32 were in local hospitals, none with critical injuries.

The Atlantic Asphalt tanker “lost control and collided into the cruise ship”, she said.

Passengers were disembarking when the boat “began to sink, and then eventually toppled over and flipped”, sending people into the water, she said.

Video from the scene showed the much larger tanker hitting the paddlewheel cruise boat as metal and glass crashed and crunched, according to The Associated Press news agency.

More than a dozen people in life jackets were dragged from the river, where the water temperature was 19 degrees Celsius (66 degrees Fahrenheit), onto nearby ships, while others stood near the railing as the boat listed further into the water.

“Surreal, that’s what that was,” one witness, Jamie Holford, told local television. “Fifteen minutes from impact to where it rolled over.”

Port police, the fire department, the coastguard and emergency medical staff are on the scene, and a triage area was set up inside the port’s administration building. The river was closed to vessel traffic.



American Cruise Lines, which operates the boat, said guests and crew had been evacuated and that it was “deeply concerned for everyone involved”.

The five-deck American Heritage, built in 2015, holds up to 150 passengers and was finishing an eight-day cruise to destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi.

The 160-metre (520-foot) tanker was flying the flag of the Marshall Islands and was bound for New Orleans, according to the MarineTraffic tracker. It specialises in carrying asphalt and bitumen, according to the maritime periodical Marine Insights.

The cause of the collision, as well as whether the ship was carrying cargo, remains unknown.

World.title: FAA grounds US flights nationwide after ‘communication issue’
World.content:
US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says federal aviation agency is ‘investigating the issue’.

The United States has grounded flights across the country after a “communication issue” impacted traffic control centres, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said.

“FAA [Federal Aviation Administration] technicians are investigating the issue. We will provide immediate updates as we have them,” Duffy wrote on social media.

The FAA said in a post on X that there had been a “temporary telecommunications outage” and that, as a precaution, all flights were being halted. International flights would be handled case by case, it added.

About 7,000 flights have been either delayed or cancelled due to the stop, according to FlightAware.

Some 4,042 flights were in the air, heading to US airports, when the ground stop was ordered, according to the tracking site Flightradar24.

The communication issue affects all 22 air route traffic control centres, which guide aircraft.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters there was no indication that the ground stop was triggered by a threat to the US. “Everybody’s safe. The flights are accounted for,” he said. “This is not another 9/11.”

President Donald Trump had been briefed, he added.

Asked whether a planned rollout of a new AI tool meant to help air traffic controllers could be to blame, Mullin said officials had not ruled it out. “You just can’t rule out anything at this point. We are going through that process,” he said.

The FBI does not believe a cyberattack or criminal activity caused the failure, Bloomberg reported, citing an official familiar with the matter.



The cited official said investigators were examining whether a software update could have caused the outage, though the cause had not been determined.

The disruption is the latest sign of strain on the US air traffic control system, which has ⁠been beset by equipment failures, communications problems and ⁠shortages of controllers, as the FAA tries to replace ageing infrastructure.

Congress approved $12.5bn for the overhaul last year, and the Department of Transportation and the White House asked lawmakers on Friday for ⁠another $30.1bn.

This is the first nationwide US ground stop since January 2023, when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned. Before that, the last time had been after the September 11, 2001, attacks.

The FAA has not provided any indication of when the ground stop might be lifted.

World.title: Pope thanks crowds on emotional return to ‘second home’ in Peru’s Chiclayo
World.content:
The Chicago-born pope was welcomed by huge crowds in the coastal city, on the final leg of his South America tour.

Share Pope thanks crowds on emotional return to ‘second home’ in Peru’s Chiclayo on social media

Pope Leo has made an emotional return to his former diocese of Chiclayo in Peru, where large crowds welcomed their former bishop exactly one month after he had lung cancer surgery, and he thanked them for their support during his recovery.

“As I look at your faces, a prayer of thanksgiving to the Lord arises in my heart for the blessing you have been and continue to be in my life,” he said.

About 500,000 people gathered for Mass at Pampas de Pimentel, a desert park just outside of Peru’s fourth-largest city, according to estimates from the Vatican, while another million lined his motorcade route.

Before he was elected pope, Leo had spent about two decades working in Peru as a missionary priest and served as bishop of Chiclayo, where he is still known as “Padre Roberto” and where his image is ubiquitous, from 2015 to 2023.

In Chiclayo, a coastal city of about 620,000, Leo earned a reputation for staying close to poor communities during times of crisis, including when the region was hit with devastating floods and the COVID-19 pandemic.

Some had camped overnight to see him, while others walked in the hot sun to avoid bumper-to-bumper traffic to get to the open-air Mass.

As he rode in his popemobile, people in the crowd waved yellow and white Vatican flags and shouted, “The pope is from Chiclayo.”

“What a joy it is to return to Chiclayo,” said Leo at the start of his homily.

Originally from Chicago and formerly known as Robert Francis Prevost, Leo also holds Peruvian citizenship and declared the country his homeland on Wednesday.



Peru is the final stop of his 12-day, three-country South America tour, coming after visits to Argentina and Uruguay. Approximately 12 million people have come to see him at public events so far.

Last month, he underwent surgery for lung cancer, amid fears that the trip would have to be cancelled. But doctors have said the cancer was localised, had not spread, and would not require further treatment.

Leo will stay in the Chiclayo area until Sunday, leading eight events, including a private dinner with the priests he oversaw during his time as bishop.

World.title: Paraguay’s ex-president Pena faces new charge over Ueno bank collapse
World.content:
The criminal association charge over his alleged role in the collapse of the bank comes a week after his removal.

Paraguayan prosecutors have charged former president Santiago Pena with criminal association over his alleged role in the collapse of the digital bank Ueno, a week after Congress removed him from office.

The prosecutor’s office announced the new charge on Friday, adding to the breach of trust and self-dealing charges already facing Pena, who is being held in pretrial detention at a military facility.

The 47-year-old former leader is accused of using his position to direct millions in government funds to Ueno and concealing or downplaying its financial troubles, despite warnings of risky lending practices, while having financial ties to the bank.

He denies all charges.

Pena, who entered office in 2023, held a stake in the bank’s holding company until last year.

On Thursday, investigators raided his official residence in the capital, Asuncion. The prosecutor’s office said agents from the economic crimes unit were extracting data and gathering relevant information for the investigation.

Last week, Pena tried to step down as president, but Congress rejected his resignation, instead removing him from office through impeachment. Pena was arrested shortly after his removal.

The collapse of Ueno left customers locked out of their accounts, prompting huge protests across the country as thousands demanded accountability and their money back.

Prosecutors had been looking for missing funds and said on Friday that assets had been located abroad, although they did not specify in which countries. They had previously asked the United States, Luxembourg and Argentina for help locating the missing money.



“The necessary steps are under way to request that they be frozen,” prosecutor Francisco Cabrera told reporters.

Three former central bank officials were also arrested on Friday, accused of having known about Ueno’s issues since late last year.

The bank, which held more than $800m in public funds, grew quickly under Pena’s presidency from a financial technology company into a large firm handling state pensions and the accounts of several government entities.

The credit ratings agency Fitch has placed Paraguay’s sovereign rating on watch for a possible downgrade, which would make it more expensive for the government to borrow money.

On Thursday, the Central Bank said it had returned savings to more than 1.8 million people who had deposited money at the bank.

World.title: Eisenkot Accuses Netanyahu of Fueling ‘Racist’ Hostility Against Arabs
World.content:
Gadi Eisenkot, the former military chief who is trying to form the next Israeli government, accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday of fueling a “racist” campaign against the country’s Arab citizens, in some of the strongest public criticism of his rival’s attacks on the community.

The comments were made days after Mr. Netanyahu delivered a divisive speech to the opening session of Parliament, or the Knesset, in which he referred to Arab lawmakers as “terror supporters” and “haters of Israel.” Diplomats and analysts condemned the remarks as a brazen display of hatred and incitement against Arab citizens, who make up about 20 percent of the overall population, and voted in massive numbers in inconclusive elections last month.

“Since the beginning of the election campaign, they have been subjected to a racist and aggressive campaign of delegitimization, fueled by the outgoing prime minister and those around him for political purposes,” Mr. Eisenkot said in a statement on social media.

“Arab citizens of Israel are an integral part of the Israeli story,” he said, adding that it was wrong to malign an entire community.

World.title: Caught Between Killers: Ebola on One Side, Islamic State on the Other
World.content:
Six months on, Ebola continues to hack a deadly trail across eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

When the outbreak was first detected in May, it resembled a single, giant blaze, with infections concentrated in a handful of towns in one province.

It has since morphed into a far bigger, more elusive foe, creeping into eight provinces and splintering into numerous hot spots as it moves through one of the world’s great rainforests.

Instead of one big fire, there are many now, scattered across a vast area about the size of Britain.

Health workers have corralled the virus where it was first detected, but infections are soaring elsewhere. Biakato, a small town deep in the rainforest, suddenly accounted for as many as one-quarter of new cases nationally. Yet its beleaguered residents were left almost entirely on their own, with dangerously little to defend themselves against the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history.

“We see the same mistakes as before,” said Dr. Jean-Jacques Muyembe, who helped discover Ebola in 1976 and now heads Congo’s National Institute for Biomedical Research. “It’s as if we were starting from zero. It’s very disappointing.”

And if that were not enough, the campaign to contain the epidemic has run into a terrifying new threat: the Islamic State.

World.title: The U.S.-Israel Relationship Is Broken. Here’s How Eisenkot Could Fix It.
World.content:
Gadi Eisenkot, the former military chief who has been given a chance to form Israel’s new governing coalition and replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, is by no means assured of success.

But if he does take power, another hugely daunting challenge would immediately confront him: how to undo the vast damage done to Israel’s relationship with the United States, its closest and most important ally.

It’s hard to imagine things getting much worse.

Many Americans have turned against Israel over its devastating military campaign in Gaza, and even more so over its role in pressing for war with Iran, which led to soaring gas prices.

President Trump announced this month that he would cut off billions of dollars in annual U.S. military aid to Israel by the end of the year and blamed Israel in part for Republican losses in the midterm elections. Democratic control of Congress could quickly lead to sanctions on violent Israeli settlers and on new settlement construction in the occupied West Bank, as well as to new conditions on arms sales.

World.title: Study Hard, Get a Career and Get Ahead? It’s Not What It Used to Be.
World.content:
Protest movements have long relied on students as some of the most ardent foot soldiers. Young people have been on the front lines of protests against war, climate change and racial inequality. But in huge protests that have shaken India and France this fall, students have revolted against the failed promises of education itself.

In India, students took to the streets after the government abruptly canceled the results of a medical-school admissions exam because test questions had been leaked online. Aspiring doctors had to take the test again, after many spent years studying for up to 12 hours a day in hopes of winning one of the coveted spots — and the chance of upward mobility. Young people across the country saw the scandal as emblematic of a broken education system and were furious.

In France, students in poor suburbs outside Paris began protesting the decrepit physical condition of their schools, an opaque university admissions system and absent teachers. French education had long promised to serve as a “social elevator” enabling young people to advance in society, but had fallen into disrepair. Soon, demonstrations spread across the country and, in some cities, spiraled into rioting.

In both countries, the anger of the students shows no signs of abating. And while in many ways France and India could hardly be more different, their unrest was sparked by a similar source of outrage: the breakdown of a foundational social contract that one could call the meritocratic bargain.

World.title: Europe Agrees on a Team to Represent It in Talks With Russia
World.content:
European leaders have waited on the margins of negotiations to end Russia’s war in Ukraine for months, eyeing a seat at the table. They learned this week that they would get one, and simply needed to decide which official should sit in that chair.

Instead, they decided on six.

European Union leaders concluded in Dublin on Friday that they will tap a group of major nations — Britain, France, Germany, Poland, and Italy — along with a representative from the E.U’s leadership arms, the European Council and European Commission.

In some ways, the choice of a crowd plays into jibes Americans have made about the continent’s indecisiveness: “If Europe could identify one person to speak on their behalf, that would be a bigger achievement than getting the Russians to include them in the negotiation,” Jared Kushner, President Trump’s son-in-law and a U.S. envoy, said earlier this week.

Europe’s failure to pick one negotiator leaves open the possibility that its fragmentation will diminish its influence. Even so, Europeans have underscored that they are a democracy of many nations and that many voices must be represented.

World.title: After Xi Purges China’s Generals, a Military Inquisitor Rises
World.content:
When China’s leader, Xi Jinping, endorsed the expulsion of dozens of disgraced officials at a recent Communist Party meeting in Beijing, one man stood out as a clear winner.

Taking his new place at the front of the meeting was Gen. Zhang Shengmin, the somber-faced enforcer of Mr. Xi’s purges inside the military. He had been promoted to the Politburo, the party’s top leadership council, the latest step in his improbable rise from low-profile inspector to a position second only to Mr. Xi in China’s military hierarchy.

General Zhang has been the principal overseer of Mr. Xi’s campaign to purify the People’s Liberation Army. His latest elevation signaled that the investigations, indoctrination drives and loyalty tests could continue for years, as Mr. Xi searches for officers he believes are irreproachably loyal, experts and officials said.

“Twist the blade inward, with strict measures to cure disorder,” China’s main military newspaper said after the party meeting that was held late last month, referring to the continued discipline campaign.

World.title: Border Crossings Have Plummeted. Stephen Miller Isn’t Satisfied.
World.content:
Since President Trump resumed office, the number of illegal crossings at the U.S.-Mexico border has dropped to the lowest point in decades.

For one of Mr. Trump’s top policy advisers, that is not enough.

In conversations with both American and Mexican officials over the last several months, Stephen Miller has insisted that illegal border crossings must be reduced, according to officials in both countries familiar with the private conversations but not authorized to discuss them.

Mr. Miller’s goal, they said, is zero crossings. Mexican officials have said that, with a nearly 2,000-mile border, that is simply not possible.

In his new role as chief of staff, Mr. Miller is expected to continue driving that agenda.

One of the main forums for Mr. Miller’s demands has been his near daily calls with the U.S. ambassador to Mexico, Ronald ​Johnson, some of the officials said. On calls with staff, Mr. Miller, previously the deputy chief of staff, frequently rails about the number of border crossings, despite their low figures, the officials said.

World.title: One of France’s Most Popular Athletes Is Running for President
World.content:
When Teddy Riner, a judo champion and one of France’s most popular athletes, announced this week that he would run for president, it was less a game changer than a welcome diversion. For all of his appeal, Mr. Riner, 37, is unlikely to win the race to replace President Emmanuel Macron next spring.

Yet his quixotic candidacy reveals a hard truth about France’s presidential campaign. Five months before voters go to the polls, many are eager, even desperate, for a fresh face to upend a race that looks increasingly as if it’s on a glide path to the election of France’s first far-right government since World War II.

The main far-right candidate, Marine Le Pen, has held a commanding lead over all her rivals for months — a lead that has only been reinforced by weeks of protests, marred by violence, that have shaken France. The most prominent center-right candidate, Édouard Philippe, has faded in the polls as the unrest has sharpened the appeal of far-right calls for law and order and left-wing calls for social justice.

Another beneficiary of the upheaval is a far-left firebrand, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, who now appears to be the likeliest candidate to advance into a second round against Ms. Le Pen in France’s two-round system. As things currently stand, French voters would be confronted with a choice between two poles of the political spectrum.

World.title: Microsoft 'deeply sorry' for global outage after almost 24 hours of disruption
World.content:
Microsoft has said it is "deeply sorry" for the service outage to its products, including Outlook and Teams, which has caused disruption around the world.

Services were broadly recovering by Friday afternoon, nearly 24 hours after issues began. Microsoft said it was making "encouraging progress", but added it does not know when services will fully recover.

The outage hit more than 70 countries, disrupting everything from business operations to government services and personal users. More than 430 million people use the affected products worldwide.

Microsoft said it was a technical issue introduced during a "network capacity upgrade" and not related to cyber or artificial intelligence agents.

Experts said the event was a "stark reminder" of how heavily businesses and vital services rely on a small group of big tech providers.

Users began reporting they were having trouble accessing Microsoft 365 products on Thursday.

By Friday, the far-reaching issue was affecting institutions from the Japanese government and the Philippines Supreme Court to the Australian spy agency, and trains, hospitals and courts in North America.

World.title: Why is Microsoft's outage lasting so long and will emails be lost?
World.content:
Although email service Outlook appears to be resuming, the outage has so far lasted for more than 20 hours - in outage terms that is considered a long time.

Prof James Ferryman from the University of Reading's department of computer science said the details the company has disclosed provide some clues.

"What Microsoft has told us is that the part of its servers that sets up secure connections is getting swamped, and once that happens the server just stops answering," he said.

"The trouble is that this kind of failure snowballs.

"One server falls over, its work gets passed to the next one, and meanwhile huge numbers of phones and laptops keep trying to get back in.

"You can't just turn it all back on at once. You have to bring it back bit by bit."

The challenge is therefore not just fixing the fault, but managing the huge surge of devices trying to reconnect once services start coming back online.

Gergely Orosz, a former leading software engineer at several major tech companies including Skype and Uber, said this could be the "most disruptive" business email outage "of all time".

He said it was still difficult to know just how many people have been affected by the disruption, but added he "cannot recall" an outage over business email ever taking this long to return to normal.

Australian cyber-security expert Troy Hunt told the BBC the outage could have far-reaching consequences.

"Microsoft is a massive part of the internet backbone and reminds us how critical email still is.

"Not only does this outage affect many people's ability to work but also things like the ability to communicate about appointments, purchase things that need verification, create or access accounts and services," he said.

In a statement, Microsoft said it was "deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners.

"We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services."

World.title: Watch: How a server outage took down Microsoft Teams and Outlook
World.content:
A Microsoft outage is affecting services including Teams, Outlook and AI software Copilot.

Microsoft has said the problem was caused by a higher-than-usual stress on its servers but that systems were now showing "early signs of stabilisation" as work continued on a fix.

The BBC's technology reporter Shiona McCallum explains what we know.

Read more about the Microsoft outage.

World.title: SpaceX to attempt double catch of huge Starship rocket
World.content:
The 124m-tall rocket is scheduled to blast off from the Starbase launchpad in Texas at 1645 local time (2245 GMT) with a 75-minute-long launch window.

After six and a half minutes, the first planned catch will be attempted when the bottom part of the rocket - the Super Heavy booster - returns to the launch tower.

The top part of the rocket, called the Ship, will continue its journey to space and deploy 26 satellites. These will form part of the Starlink constellation that provides high speed internet from space.

The Ship is then due to complete 14 orbits around the Earth before returning for the second catch attempt about 22 and a half hours after taking off.

Until now, SpaceX has managed to catch the Super Heavy Booster on three earlier test flights.

But the upper stage of the rocket, which only reached orbit for the first time in September, has never been grabbed by the chopsticks. Instead it's splashed down in the ocean.

SpaceX said it would only decide to try to catch the Ship after carefully assessing the vehicle while it's in space.

If any problems are detected there are various points during the flight when the rocket stage can be brought down in the ocean.

World.title: Rosenberg: Uncompromising Putin ups demands for peace with Ukraine
World.content:
Russia's President Vladimir Putin says he wishes "eternal peace" for Ukraine.

That is the same Russian president who ordered the full-scale invasion of Russia's neighbour nearly five years ago and who continues to reject the idea of a comprehensive ceasefire.

And what, in Moscow's view, is a prerequisite for peace?

The Kremlin spelt it out after talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner: "A new, long-term architecture of indivisible security and peace."

Translated from Kremlin-speak, it means Moscow wants to change the security set-up of Europe in a way that benefits Russia.

What Russia is pushing for is, potentially, the biggest change to European security arrangements since the end of the Cold War.

The Kremlin has put back on the table its controversial proposal from December 2021 â the "draft treaties" with the US and Nato which would not only have put the brakes on the alliance's eastward enlargement by giving Moscow cast-iron guarantees that, for instance, Ukraine and Georgia would never be allowed to join, but also rolled back Nato military infrastructure from countries of central and eastern Europe which became Nato members following the dissolution of the Soviet Union.

Western leaders dismissed such demands as an unacceptable Russian ultimatum. Two months later Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

The "draft treaties" were put away. Now they are out of the geopolitical filing cabinet, and being quoted again by the Kremlin.

What is more, Yuri Ushakov, Putin's foreign policy aide, has suggested that Moscow is about to "add certain new considerations" to its list of demands in light of Western efforts "to inflict a strategic defeat on Russia".

That does not mean, of course, that Western governments will accept them.

But the fact that the question of European security is featuring now in discussions on Ukraine is viewed here as a victory for Moscow.

"In December 2021 Russia actively proposed that Nato rethink the security system in Europe," wrote newspaper Komsomolskaya Pravda earlier this week.

"Our proposals were almost laughed at.

"Having secured one victory by forcing the West to think about security, our diplomats need a second by making the West heed Russia's concerns about Nato enlargement."

The EU's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, has called Russia's demands for a new European security architecture a "trap" designed to "shift attention away from a ceasefire".

"The sequencing of Ukraine-Russia talks is important," Kallas wrote on social media. "The priority should be securing a ceasefire, followed by a peace agreement. Only then can there be discussions on Europe's wider security architecture."

Europe's problem is that, right now, it is not at the table.

Moscow has had no desire to give it a chair. It has slammed European leaders for their military support for Kyiv and tough stance on Russia.

This week's peace talks in Abu Dhabi involved Ukraine, Russia and the US.

After his discussions in Moscow, Witkoff indicated that Putin had agreed to the idea of European representatives joining the next round of Ukraine peace talks.

But on Friday the Kremlin indicated a final decision on European participation had not been taken.

"Once we understand their true intentions and their readiness to facilitate the peace process, then it will be possible to take a decision about dialogue on Ukraine in a wider format," said Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov.

World.title: Nvidia scandal fallout widens as Trump's treasury secretary blames cabinet colleague
World.content:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has blamed Howard Lutnick's Commerce Department for failing to properly oversee the export of high-spec AI chips, as the fallout from the Nvidia scandal widens to President Donald Trump's cabinet.

Pressure is building on Lutnick from across the political spectrum to explain his department's actions.

Jensen Huang was ousted as Nvidia CEO after revelations he had an affair with a businesswoman who was also allegedly a Chinese spy.

Megaspeed, the firm she worked for, had been probed by US government agencies over suspicions it was smuggling Nvidia chips into China, reports said, but it is not on a list of firms US companies are prevented from working with.

Bessent told CNBC several agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months".

"But Commerce has the pen... and you will have to ask them about their internal process," he added.

Bessent's comments come after Lutnick was called to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month over the Commerce Department's role in allowing Nvidia to export its advanced chips.

Other congressional committees have asked both Lutnick and his department to retain all records relating to Nvidia and Huang.

World.title: The Peruvian city that has embraced Pope Leo as one of its own
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV has celebrated Mass near the Peruvian city where he made his name as a compassionate bishop who worked closely with poor and migrant communities.

The ceremony was held on Friday at a park in Pimentel, about 10km (six miles) from Chiclayo in northern Peru as part of his tour of Latin America.

The Vatican estimates more than 1.5 million people gathered to welcome the pontiff.

"Thank you for your affection, support and prayers," the Pope told followers.

"Especially for my health during this time of trial which, with God's help, I am overcoming," he added, referencing the surgery he had for lung cancer which took place just weeks ago.

Some of the crowd arrived 12 hours in advance to wait in vigil before the Mass began.

"We spent the night praying, alongside family, excited to welcome the Pope from Chiclayo," said Isa Orderique.

World.title: German spies handed new powers to tackle 'hybrid threats' from abroad
World.content:
Germany's foreign and domestic intelligence services are to be given greater powers to combat espionage, terrorism and sabotage after the country's parliament, the Bundestag, approved a major overhaul of its legislation.

Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, who championed the bill, has called it a "reform of the century", necessary because of the increasing threats from foreign powers.

But the Left Party's security spokeswoman, Clara BÃ¼nger, said Dobrindt was creating a new German secret police.

The legislation gives numerous new powers to Germany's BND federal intelligence service, and its BfV domestic service, the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution.

In the Bundestag, 309 MPs voted in favour of the new law on intelligence services, while 190 voted against and 71 abstained.

For historical reasons, German intelligence has mainly focused on gathering information rather than acting on it.

In future, German spies working for the BND, which is responsible for foreign intelligence, will be able to conduct covert operations abroad, including sabotage.

This could include paralysing the servers of state-sponsored hacker groups, disrupting disinformation networks, or even disrupting supply chains for weapons.

Agents for the domestic intelligence service, the BfV, will no longer to be limited to gathering information. For the first time they will be able to take protective action against property and IT systems, if specific threats are identified.

That means they will be allowed to dismantle or break explosives or weapons, divert or block data flows during cyber-attacks, delete or falsify data stored for malicious purposes, and plant false information on those involved.

World.title: Zamfara stands still as Gov Lawal hosts First Lady, Remi Tinubu for mega rally
World.content:
The First Lady of Nigeria, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, received a rousing welcome from thousands of residents and supporters during her visit to Zamfara State.

On Tuesday, the Zamfara State Government hosted the APC North-West Women’s Mega Rally and Empowerment Programme at the Trade Fair Complex in Gusau.

The event, led by Zamfara First Lady Huriyya Dauda Lawal, brought together former Zamfara governors, the first ladies of the North-West, ministers and other key All Progressives Congress stakeholders.

Before the rally, Senator Tinubu met with the Zamfara State traditional rulers to seek their blessings.

In her remarks, Mrs Tinubu described her visit as a powerful expression of solidarity and compassion, as well as a commitment to women’s welfare and advancement, especially for those facing insecurity, poverty and limited economic opportunities.

She said, “This is the happiest day of my life. Except for Zamfara, I have been in all 36 states of Nigeria, including the FCT. I have always wanted to come to Zamfara, and today I have fulfilled that. Because it is now easy to come, this is just the beginning; I am coming back again. Mr President is also coming.

“Before I start, I want to commiserate with you all for all the lives that were lost; they are very precious to us. May God forgive them, grant them Al-Jannatul Firdaus, and continue to be with us.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Today is Juma’at; we have to be fast; we have empowerment to give to women. This is the only party that empowers during the campaign, and it is not about the campaign; we have been empowering from day one. And that is why it is not politics.

“Earlier, I was also given a title in Zamfara, the ‘Jagaban Matan Arewa’ by the Chairman of the Zamfara State Council of Chiefs and Emir of Anka, Alhaji Attahiru Muhammad Ahmad. I thanked all the Emirs.

“I love Zamfara. I am happy to be here. Mr President said I should tell you he will continue working for you. Nigeria will continue to prosper, in sha Allah.”

Earlier, Governor Dauda Lawal thanked Senator Tinubu for her continued support through the Renewed Hope Initiative, including its Food Outreach Programme.

“Your Excellency, Mother of the Nation, your presence today represents more than an official visit. You have set a record in the history of our dear Zamfara State.

“Your Excellency, Distinguished ladies and gentlemen, in Zamfara State, we firmly believe that empowering women is not only our responsibility as a government; it is a needed and bankable investment in social and societal morality, economic prosperity, family stability, and sustainable peace.

“I assure Your Excellency that Zamfara’s government and people unwaveringly support Mr President’s second term. With the women here and the men supporting them, Zamfara and the North West will deliver for Mr President come January 2027.”

World.title: Finance must break developing countries from ‘debt and disaster’ loop – UN climate chief
World.content:
The executive secretary of UN Climate Change, Simon Stiell, told the ministers at COP31 that climate finance must be redesigned to lift developing countries out of a cycle of debt and disaster, adding that meeting a headline figure will not do it.

“Meeting a financial target does not always meet countries’ needs. To do that, we need to look at how finance is delivered,” Mr Stiell said on Friday at the opening of a high-level ministerial dialogue on climate finance in Antalya, Turkey.

Countries agreed at COP29 that developed nations would lead in providing $300 billion a year by 2035, as part of a wider effort to raise $1.3 trillion annually from all sources.

Mr Stiell said the roadmap for reaching those sums “must become reality”, but that the terms of the money mattered as much as the amount.

“Many developing countries are trapped in a downward loop of debt, disaster, and devastating capital costs,” he said. “The threat of floods, fires, storms and droughts hangs over them, pushing up the price of borrowing even before disaster strikes.”

He stated that the terms of finance should reflect each country’s debt position.

“Private finance, loans and guarantees are essential to achieving our collective goals. But grant-based and highly concessional finance will remain critical, particularly for Least Developed Countries, Small Island Developing States and other very vulnerable economies,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, broader action on debt is also needed to prevent countries from being forced to choose between repayments and resilience.

International climate finance for developing countries reached about $137 billion in 2024, and almost 70 per cent of it came in the form of loans, according to a UN Women flagship report released on Tuesday in Antalya.

Countries in sub-Saharan Africa paid more than twice as much in external debt service between 2021 and 2023 as they received in climate finance, according to an analysis published by the Heinrich Böll Foundation.

The analysis found that interest payments consumed more than 10 per cent of government revenue in 27 African countries in 2024.

The chair of the African Group of Negotiators, Nana Antwi-Boasiako Amoah, has said that a transition could not be called just if poorer countries have to “mortgage their futures” to pay for it.

The group lost a bid on Monday for a separate agenda item on tripling adaptation finance. It now wants the target prioritised in the summit’s cover decision.

Nigeria is not on the UN’s list of least developed countries, which places it among the states the UN climate chief expects to rely more on loans, guarantees and private capital.

It needs about $337 billion between 2026 and 2035 to implement its climate commitments, according to the National Council on Climate Change.

Omotenioye Majekodunmi, the agency’s director-general, said more than 80 per cent of that will have to come from private investment, commercial debt, and international carbon finance.

About $2.5 billion a year went to climate action in Nigeria in 2021 and 2022, counting domestic and international sources, according to the Climate Policy Initiative’s tracking.

The dialogue was the last in a series that began in 2013, and its conclusions will go to COP32 in Ethiopia next year, Mr Stiell said.

World.title: North accounts for most of Nigeria’s recorded maternal deaths – Report
World.content:
Women in northern Nigeria continue to bear a disproportionate burden of maternal deaths, with the Northwest and Northeast geopolitical zones accounting for about three-quarters of reported fatalities in health facilities, according to the 2026 Joint Annual Review (JAR) Statistical Book.

The report also highlights significant disparities in maternal health outcomes between rural and urban areas, with rural women recording a maternal mortality ratio of 656 deaths per 100,000 live births, compared with 444 deaths per 100,000 live births in urban areas.

Produced by the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the report reviews the third year of implementation of the Health Sector Strategic Blueprint. It was presented at the third Nigeria Health Sector Joint Annual Review in Abuja on 10 November.

The findings highlight persistent inequalities in maternal healthcare access and outcomes, despite a reported decline in maternal deaths across health facilities nationally.

According to the report, Nigeria recorded thousands of maternal deaths in health facilities between January and September 2026, although the figures represent only deaths captured by the facility reporting system.

The ministry acknowledged that the figures could be underreported or overreported but described the data as reliable for monitoring trends in the health sector.

Maternal mortality remains high

Maternal mortality refers to the death of a woman during pregnancy, childbirth or within 42 days of the termination of pregnancy from causes related to or aggravated by the pregnancy or its management.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Most maternal deaths are preventable through timely access to quality antenatal care, skilled birth attendance, emergency obstetric services and appropriate postnatal care.

Despite the reported improvements, Nigeria’s maternal mortality ratio remains a major public health concern.

The JAR Statistical Book puts the country’s maternal mortality ratio at 572 deaths per 100,000 live births, significantly above the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) target of fewer than 70 deaths per 100,000 live births by 2030.

The burden is particularly concerning given Nigeria’s contribution to global maternal deaths.

In its 2023 report, titled “Improving Maternal and Newborn Health and Survival and Reducing Stillbirths: Progress Report 2023”, the World Health Organisation (WHO) estimated that Nigeria recorded 82,000 maternal deaths, 181,000 stillbirths and 277,000 neonatal deaths in 2020.

The combined 540,000 deaths accounted for 12 per cent of global maternal, stillbirth and neonatal deaths, despite Nigeria contributing only six per cent of global live births.

The report ranked Nigeria second after India among countries with the highest combined burden of maternal deaths, stillbirths and neonatal deaths.

Reported maternal deaths decline

The JAR data indicate a downward trend in facility-reported maternal deaths over the review period.

The country recorded 5,391 maternal deaths in health facilities in 2024, compared with 4,455 in 2025.

The figure declined further in 2026, although the exact total requires confirmation against the final statistical table. The quarterly data also indicate improvements.

Following a peak in the second quarter of 2024, maternal deaths and the maternal mortality ratio generally declined. By the third quarter of 2026, the maternal mortality ratio had fallen to 128 deaths per 100,000 live births, representing a reduction of about 46 per cent from the earlier peak.

Maternal deaths during the same period also declined by approximately 40 per cent to 947.

However, these improvements have not been evenly distributed across the country.

Northern states bear the burden

According to the report, maternal deaths over the past three years were heavily concentrated in the Northwest and Northeast geopolitical zones.

By 2026, the two zones together accounted for approximately three-quarters of all documented maternal deaths in health facilities.

The five northern states with the highest maternal mortality burden were Kano, Borno, Jigawa, Yobe and Katsina.

While the national figures showed a downward trend, maternal deaths reportedly increased across the two northern zones, contrasting with reductions recorded in southern parts of the country.

In most southern states, fewer than 50 maternal deaths were reported. The states with the lowest recorded numbers included Osun (four deaths), Abia (five), Enugu (eight), Ekiti (nine), and Bayelsa (nine).

Maternal morbidity

Beyond deaths, the report also highlights the burden of maternal morbidity, including complications that can have lasting effects on women’s health, wellbeing and livelihoods. In 2026, approximately 3,060 women were diagnosed with vesicovaginal fistula (VVF), compared with 4,350 in 2025.

VVF is an abnormal opening between the bladder and vagina that can result in continuous, involuntary leakage of urine, often following prolonged or obstructed labour.

Of the women diagnosed in 2026, 1,737 underwent surgical repair, representing 56.8 per cent of those diagnosed. This was lower than in 2025, when 2,564 women (59 per cent) underwent repairs.

The Northwest and Northeast again recorded the highest burden, with 1,420 and 982 cases, respectively, in 2026. The figures underscore the need to strengthen access to emergency obstetric care, timely referrals and surgical treatment, particularly in underserved communities.

World.title: COP31: White paper urges governments to invest in water-based energy storage
World.content:
A new international white paper launched at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, has urged governments to prioritise pumped-storage hydropower as strategic infrastructure to strengthen energy security and support the expansion of renewable electricity.

The paper, developed with input from more than 60 governments and international agencies through the Global Alliance for Pumped Storage (GAPS), outlines seven policy recommendations for accelerating investment in the technology, which can store electricity for extended periods and release it when demand increases.

It was presented at a high-level roundtable organised by GAPS, as countries consider how to strengthen electricity systems amid growing energy demand and the expansion of renewable energy.

Pumped-storage hydropower uses surplus electricity to pump water from a lower reservoir to an upper reservoir. When electricity demand rises, the system releases stored water through turbines to generate electricity.

Unlike conventional battery technologies, the system can store large amounts of energy for extended periods, while also providing services that help maintain electricity grid stability.

The white paper argues that the technology could help countries reduce dependence on imported energy resources and strengthen domestic energy systems because it relies primarily on water, suitable geographical locations, and local labour, rather than imported or processed critical minerals.

It also notes that projects can be developed using existing reservoirs, lakes, hydropower infrastructure and former mining sites.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Seven recommendations for governments

The paper identifies seven priority areas for governments seeking to accelerate pumped-storage development.

These include assessing national energy-storage needs and incorporating them into electricity planning, recognising pumped storage as strategic national security infrastructure and establishing clear legal definitions for energy storage.

It also recommends identifying and preparing suitable sites, simplifying permitting and licensing procedures, creating an enabling investment environment and ensuring that pumped-storage operators are adequately remunerated for the services they provide to electricity systems.

According to the paper, significant upfront investment, lengthy development timelines and site-specific preparation requirements have continued to limit the development of pumped-storage projects despite their established capabilities.

It argues that governments must create the necessary policy, regulatory and market conditions to attract investment while ensuring that projects meet environmental and social sustainability standards.

Energy security, renewable expansion

The launch comes amid efforts to expand electricity access and increase the share of electricity in global energy consumption.

Under the COP31 Global Electrification Pledge, countries are seeking to increase electricity’s share of final energy consumption from about 23 per cent currently to 35 per cent by 2035.

Achieving this target will require electricity systems that can accommodate growing renewable energy generation while maintaining a reliable supply, the paper states.

It identifies pumped storage as one of the established technologies that can provide long-duration energy storage alongside other grid services, including frequency and voltage control, operating reserves, and black-start capabilities, which allow electricity systems to restart after a major outage.

President of the International Hydropower Association (IHA), Malcolm Turnbull, said countries seeking greater energy security and faster electrification could not afford to overlook the infrastructure required to support reliable electricity systems.

Mr Turnbull said pumped storage represented a long-term investment in national energy security and sovereignty, adding that the white paper provided governments with recommendations to translate the technology’s potential into projects, investment and more resilient electricity systems.

“As countries seek to become energy secure and accelerate electrification, we cannot afford to overlook the infrastructure that makes these systems work,” he said.

The paper also highlights the potential economic benefits of pumped-storage projects, including employment opportunities through domestic resources and local labour.

It argues that their long operational lifespans could make them important infrastructure investments for countries seeking to strengthen their electricity systems over generations.

World.title: Prophet who claimed he could resurrect Toluwanisings remanded
World.content:
A court has remanded a self-styled prophet, Moses Idowu, following allegations that he filmed the remains of gospel singer Olayemi “Toluwanisings” Bolaji while claiming he could resurrect him.

The Oyo State Police Command also arraigned content creator Oladapo Dunminimnun in a separate case over videos containing unsubstantiated allegations about the singer’s death and members of his family.

The command’s spokesperson, Ayanlade Olayinka, disclosed the developments in a statement on Friday. He said the two defendants were arraigned before courts of competent jurisdiction over separate publications linked to the controversy that followed Toluwanisings’ death.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that the gospel singer slumped and died at his Ibadan residence in October. His death subsequently triggered disagreements among his relatives, wife and associates over the circumstances surrounding it and where he should be buried.

The dispute intensified after his paternal family opposed plans by his wife, Elizabeth, and some associates to bury him in a cemetery. Following police intervention, the parties reached an agreement, and the singer was buried at his residence on 9 November.

Alleged resurrection attempt

Mr Olayinka said Mr Idowu visited the morgue where Toluwanisings’ body was kept and claimed to possess the spiritual power to resurrect the dead.

During the visit, the police alleged he recorded the singer’s remains and circulated the footage on social media without obtaining permission from the family.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“In the course of the incident, the suspect recorded a video of the deceased’s body and subsequently circulated the footage on social media without the consent or authorisation of the deceased’s family, thereby subjecting the remains to indignity and causing further distress to the bereaved family,” the police spokesperson said.

The police further accused Mr Idowu of publishing claims that implicated the singer’s widow and personal assistant, Babadunmi Gbolabo, in his death without providing evidence.

He was consequently arraigned on four counts relating to the alleged unlawful recording and publication of false information, publication of defamatory material, indignity to a dead body and conduct likely to cause a breach of public peace.

The court ordered his remand at a correctional centre and adjourned the case until 2 December for further proceedings.

Content creator arraigned

In a separate case, the police arraigned Mr Dunminimnun on Thursday over videos he allegedly produced and circulated during the dispute surrounding Toluwanisings’ death and burial.

Mr Dunminimnun had interviewed members of the singer’s paternal family as the disagreement over his burial arrangements unfolded.

According to the police, he subsequently published videos accusing some of the singer’s relatives and associates of involvement in his death.

Mr Olayinka said the publications continued despite police warnings and an undertaking signed by the parties to end public exchanges that could escalate the dispute.

“Investigation revealed that the suspect proceeded to produce and circulate videos containing unsubstantiated allegations concerning the deceased, his wife and other family members,” he said.

The police spokesperson added that the publications were made despite repeated cautions against circulating unverified claims about the case.

Mr Dunminimnun faces allegations of spreading false information on Facebook, unlawfully publishing defamatory material and engaging in conduct capable of disturbing public peace.

The court adjourned his case until 11 December for further proceedings.

Police caution social media users

The police expressed concern about the circulation of unverified allegations and sensitive images involving deceased persons on social media.

Mr Olayinka said freedom of expression remained constitutionally protected but must be exercised within the boundaries of the law and with consideration for bereaved families.

“The command cautions members of the public, social media users and content creators against using digital platforms to spread false information, circulate sensitive images of deceased persons or make reckless allegations against individuals without credible evidence,” he said.

He urged the public to respect the dignity of the dead and allow investigators and the courts to determine issues arising from suspicious deaths.

The Commissioner of Police in Oyo State, Abimbola Olugbenga, also advised social media users to verify information before publishing it and avoid content that could disrupt public peace.

World.title: NUPRC flags 13 gas leaks as top-priority risks in Bille, Rivers State
World.content:
The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) said it has screened 28 oil and gas wells around reported gas leak locations in Bille, Degema Local Government Area of Rivers State, identifying 13 as top-priority (3 very high risks and 10 high risks) and 15 as medium-to-low risks, as investigations continue to determine the source of the seepage.

In a statement issued on Friday, the commission said the update was announced on Thursday during a special technical paper presentation it hosted at the 44th Annual International Conference and Exhibition of the Nigerian Association of Petroleum Explorationists (NAPE).

The presentation, titled “Unravelling Gas Seepage and Bubbling in Nigeria: The Integrated Study Approach Towards Source Attribution,” provided an update on the ongoing investigation into the leakage reported in the community.

In his presentation, the director of Subsurface Development at the NUPRC, Joseph Ogunsola, said the gas seepage is a new phenomenon in Nigeria’s petroleum industry, prompting the commission to constitute a team to scrutinise the source of the bubbles.

Mr Ogunsola, who was represented by a geologist and senior manager at Onshore Frontier Development Drilling, Azibamikiomam John-Adumo, said studies conducted in one of the affected areas have helped the investigation team understand the underlying geological structures.

He explained that one of the wells in the area was originally drilled to find oil but was shut down after gas, rather than oil, was discovered.

According to him, the well is about 2.5 kilometres from the seepage location, and investigations are ongoing to determine whether the seepage originates from that well or other nearby facilities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He added that other wells in the area are between 2.5 and three kilometres from the seepage locations.

Mr Ogunsola noted that the area is highly explored and hydrocarbon-charged, as shown by the number of wells in the vicinity.

This is the first time the NUPRC has provided a precise update on its investigation into the source of the gas seepage affecting lives and livelihoods in Bille.

In June, a PREMIUM TIMES investigation revealed how toxic gas emerging from beneath the ground in the riverine community is threatening residents’ health and livelihoods.

The leakage, which has persisted for more than a year, raised several life-threatening concerns, including explosions, disturbing sights and odours, and disruptions to residents’ economic activities.

Gas has been bubbling to the surface from abandoned mono pumps and long-abandoned shallow wells across the community, forcing its way through ageing pipes buried underground for decades.

Providing an update on the well-screening workstream, which forms part of the facility and infrastructure component of the investigation, Mr Ogunsola said 28 wells were assessed based on their proximity to the seepage locations and the reservoirs encountered during drilling.

He disclosed that the investigation team physically inspected 14 wells but could not access three others because they are submerged.

During the visits, the team observed gas hissing from some wells, while other facilities were corroded or vandalised.

He further explained that the investigation has progressed from the first reported gas bubbles to an independent gas fingerprinting campaign within 12 months.

Recalling that the first seepage was observed in October 2025, he said results of the independent investigation, using Gas Chromatography-Isotope Ratio Mass Spectrometry (GC-IRMS) and compositional field analysis, were expected in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Residents may be relocated

While investigations continue, Mr Ogunsola said the commission and operators have mobilised relief materials and other forms of support for affected communities.

The interventions include food supplies, medical outreach, efforts to provide potable water, fire-fighting vehicles and safety kits, among others.

He warned, however, that residents might have to be relocated if investigations establish that the seepage is caused by a natural geological phenomenon.

According to him, tracing the migration pathways of naturally occurring gas and designing appropriate subsurface interventions could be considerably more challenging.

He reiterated the commission’s commitment to conducting a speedy, coordinated and integrated investigation to establish the source of the gas seepage.

World.title: 2027: Tinubu orders security agencies to crack down on political thuggery
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has directed security agencies to crack down on political thuggery and other anti-democratic activities ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He also warned politicians and their supporters against violence, saying his administration would not tolerate conduct capable of undermining public order during the electioneering period.

Mr Tinubu gave the directive in a statement issued by the State House on Friday, following reports of violence accompanying political events in different parts of the country.

Electoral violence has remained a recurring feature of Nigeria’s political landscape, with attacks, intimidation, clashes between rival supporters and destruction of campaign materials often accompanying electioneering activities.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that recent incidents have heightened concerns. On 28 October, suspected political thugs attacked a convoy conveying All Progressives Congress (APC) supporters to a campaign rally in Funtua, Katsina State, injuring a woman and damaging vehicles.

On 7 November, violence at a political procession in Asaba, Delta State, left one person dead and five others injured, according to the police. On 12 November, suspected thugs disrupted a Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) town hall meeting in Lagos, attacking supporters and damaging vehicles. Similar attacks were reported during political activities in other places including Ekiti, Cross River and Sokoto states.

“Every form of violence stands condemned. Violence should never have a place in our political campaigns as we move toward the 2027 general elections,” Mr Tinubu said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He urged political parties to focus their campaigns on issues and competing ideas that promote the welfare of Nigerians and national development.

“As the leader of this country, I commit myself to a peaceful, free, and fair election, and I urge political leaders and supporters across party lines to conduct themselves responsibly,” he said.

Mr Tinubu said political differences and competing ambitions should not turn politicians into enemies, stressing that Nigerians belonged to the same national community.

“I have said that being in different political parties or pursuing different ambitions does not make us enemies,” he said.

The president also reiterated his earlier directive to security agencies to act firmly against anyone seeking to undermine public order.

He said all political parties and candidates must be protected and allowed to campaign anywhere in the country without intimidation or threats to their safety.

ALSO READ: Tinubu booed at Abuja mosque after Friday prayers

“Our administration is committed to an orderly and peaceful election, and all political parties and candidates should be protected and free to campaign anywhere in the country without molestation or fear for their safety,” he said.

Mr Tinubu said security agencies had his authorisation to use full force against political thuggery and other activities threatening the electoral process.

“Security agencies are therefore authorised to confront thuggery and other anti-social and anti-democratic activities with full force,” he added.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that in response to incidents of violence, including the destruction of campaign materials in some parts of the country, the police issued a stern warning last week, saying that anyone found engaging in such acts would be arrested and prosecuted.

World.title: Tinubu booed at Abuja mosque after Friday prayers
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu was booed by some aggrieved Nigerians at the Shehu Shagari Central Mosque in Abuja on Friday shortly after observing his Juma’at prayers.

Several video clips obtained by PREMIUM TIMES showed people chanting slogans against the president as his convoy left the mosque.

An eyewitness who attended the prayers told PREMIUM TIMES that the protest may have been triggered by the restrictions imposed on worshippers because of the president’s visit.

The eyewitness, who asked not to be named, said Mr Tinubu arrived at the mosque at about 1:49 p.m., by which time access to the premises had been restricted.

According to the source, security operatives prevented people from entering the mosque after the president arrived. Roads leading to the mosque were also blocked, while some security personnel mounted the mosque’s perimeter fences as part of the security arrangements.

The restrictions continued after the prayers, with worshippers prevented from leaving until the president departed, the eyewitness said.

The source said some people expressed their frustration by chanting “Ba mayi, ba ma so,” a Hausa expression loosely translated as “We are not supporting you.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Others chanted “Tinubu Must Go,” a slogan associated with opposition to the president’s re-election bid.

Another source at the mosque also attributed the booing partly to the security arrangements, which the source described as excessive.

“People were stopped from entering the mosque after the president had entered. Several people were stuck outside,” the source said.

The source added that worshippers were also prevented from leaving until Mr Tinubu departed, and that the booing started from the area where people had been barricaded.

The incident occurred as the president faces growing political contestation ahead of the next presidential election.

Presidential spokesperson Bayo Onanuga didn’t respond to calls as of the time of filing this report.

Friday sermon

During the service, the Chief Imam of the Shehu Shagari Central Mosque, Area 1, Garki, Rabiu Suleiman, delivered a sermon based on lessons from Surah Al-Fatihah, the first chapter of the Quran.

The imam urged Muslims to uphold the oneness of Allah and seek steadfastness through Him.

He also prayed for peace and the president’s good health, asking Allah to grant Mr Tinubu greater wisdom and guide him towards leading Nigeria to prosperity.

Mr Suleiman acknowledged the president’s contribution to the renovation of the historic mosque.

The president was accompanied by the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu; his Special Adviser on Political Affairs, Ibrahim Masari; Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila; and former Kano State Governor, Abdullahi Ganduje.

The presidential election is scheduled for January.

Mr Tinubu is expected to face major challenges from opposition figures, including Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC).

World.title: 2027: PDP’s Popoola pledges to tackle insecurity, infrastructure deficit
World.content:
By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin

The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) senatorial candidate for Kwara South in the 2027 general elections, Hon. Saheed Popoola, has pledged to address insecurity, infrastructure deficits, agricultural challenges, youth unemployment and poor healthcare delivery in the district if elected.
