Popoola, a former commissioner, two-term member of the Kwara State House of Assembly and former Chairman of Offa Local Government Area, made the pledge on Friday during the News Keg Engagement Series organised by the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) in Ilorin.

He identified security as his top priority, arguing that meaningful development could not take place in an environment where residents lived in fear of attacks.

Expressing concern over increasing cases of kidnapping in Kwara South, Popoola said residents could no longer move freely or access their farmlands without fear of being attacked.

He recalled that communities in the district were relatively safe in the past, but said the current security situation had created anxiety among farmers and other residents.

The PDP candidate pledged to replicate the neighbourhood watch initiative he established during his tenure as local government chairman, which he described as effective in maintaining security.

According to him, the initiative would involve youths, Fulani residents and other community stakeholders, with participants properly equipped and registered with the government.

He added that he would deploy personal resources to support the initiative, arguing that residents understood their communities and terrain better than security personnel deployed from other parts of the country.

Popoola, who said his 27 years of political experience had equipped him with the capacity to address the challenges facing the district, also promised to appoint 83 liaison officers across the wards to improve communication and ensure effective representation.

He described the proposed arrangement as unprecedented in Kwara State, saying it would enable him to respond more effectively to the needs of his constituents.

The former lawmaker explained that his decision to join the PDP was informed by his conviction that the party was more committed to the welfare of ordinary Nigerians.

He pledged to use his position in the Senate to lobby the Federal and State Governments, as well as relevant agencies, to address security and infrastructure challenges in the district.

On infrastructure, Popoola lamented the poor condition of roads linking communities in Kwara South, particularly the Iloffa-Ekiti axis.

He promised to engage relevant federal agencies to facilitate the rehabilitation and construction of major roads, including the Ilorin-Omu-Aran-Egbe and Ajase-Offa routes.

He said lobbying government institutions and agencies to attract development projects was an important responsibility of legislators, adding that senators could facilitate infrastructure development through effective engagement.

On his controversial comments at the palace of the Olofa of Offa, Oba Mufutau Gbadamosi, last weekend, concerning his alleged false claims against former Senate President, Dr Bukola Saraki, during the Offa robbery incident, Popoola said he stood by his remarks and had no apology to offer anyone.

“I have no apology to offer anybody on what I said in Olofa’s palace at the weekend. I stand by all that I was quoted to have said. I owe Dr Bukola Saraki an open apology before I enter my grave, and I thank Almighty Allah that He made it possible for me,” he said.

World.title: US says forces responded to suspected drone activity over base in Britain
World.content:
(FILES) A picture shows the signage at the entrance to British Royal Air Force base RAF Lakenheath, which hosts the near the 48th Fighter Wing of the US Air Force, near the village of Lakenheath in eastern England on June 16, 2020. US forces responded to possible drone activity over a military base in Britain on November 13, 2026, a US Air Force spokesperson said. American forces “responded to suspected unauthorized drone activity over RAF Lakenheath. No personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected,” the spokesperson said in a statement. (Photo by CHRIS RADBURN / AFP)

US forces responded to possible unauthorized drone activity over a military base in Britain on Friday, a US Air Force spokesperson said, in the latest security incident at a facility hosting American military aircraft.

“No personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected” at the RAF Lakenheath base, the Air Force spokesperson said in a statement.

“We continue to work closely with our host nation counterparts to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, US and host nation civilians, contractors, and all of our families,” the statement added.

Nick Timothy, a local member of parliament, said in a statement on Facebook that he had been in touch with authorities at the base and was “told there is no threat to the public, and the incident is now resolved.”

A post on the official RAF Lakenheath Facebook page earlier this week urged people to report “suspicious activity, including unauthorized drone activity.”

“Our strongest security asset is an observant community,” the post said.

The possible drone incident at Lakenheath came after the US Justice Department announced charges earlier in the week against three men it described as “Iranian operatives” over their role in an alleged terrorist plot at RAF Fairford, another British base.

The three men allegedly helped plan and direct the September incident at the base, which came to light when police were called after a local farmer reported seeing a group of men with several white vans engaged in “suspicious” activity.

– Iran war fallout –

A US charging document stated that a man identified as Mohammad Ali al-Hassani directed unnamed individuals to drive to the base in the vans, some of which contained barrels of fuel, and that he earlier paid the group to buy metallic objects that could be used as shrapnel.

Days later, the United States withdrew all its B-1 bombers from the base.

UK police last month charged two British men with national security offenses related to the RAF Fairford incident.

One was charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service, believed to be in Iran, and another with entering a prohibited place for a purpose “prejudicial” to the UK.

Flight-tracking data showed Tuesday that the US military had removed at least a dozen aircraft from another British airbase, RAF Mildenhall, following what the Wall Street Journal said was a threat from Iran.

The United States has flown military aircraft from bases in Britain as part of the US-Israeli war against Iran sparked earlier this year, which saw Tehran respond by launching missiles and drones at countries across the region, while the militant groups it backs also entered the fray.

In an interview broadcast Wednesday, Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei threatened to strike US bases beyond the Middle East, including in Europe, if they are used for attacks against the Islamic republic.

Iranian officials have previously threatened to expand the geographic scope of the conflict should the US attack again.

In late September, an adviser to Iran’s new supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei publicly mused that the war could “expand even further, reaching the Indian Ocean and perhaps beyond.”

World.title: Global outage: Microsoft blames network change for service disruption
World.content:
This illustration photograph shows the Microsoft Outlook logo (L) displayed on a smartphone with the backdrop of Microsoft logo on a screen, in New Delhi on November 13, 2026. Microsoft said on November 12 that efforts to repair a major outage of Outlook were not going as expected and the firm was seeking alternative solutions as users around the world were left without its crucial services. (Photo by MANAN VATSYAYANA / AFP)

…Apologises to customers

By Juliet Umeh

The US-based technology, Microsoft, has blamed a recent network change for a global outage that disrupted its workplace services, including Outlook, Teams and Copilot.

While apologising to its customers in a statement, the company said the incident stemmed from an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced after a subsequent network change.

The statement reads: “The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change.”

The outage affected customers and partners in different regions, disrupting access to Microsoft services. The company said it had addressed the underlying issue and was continuing to restore services to remaining customers and regions.

“We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services,” it said, adding that the disruption was “not related to cyber or AI/agents.”

Microsoft said services were restored gradually because of the scale of demand.

“Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration.

“We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners,” it said.

Microsoft added that it would release a full post-incident report after completing its review of the outage.

The disruption affected organisations that rely on Microsoft’s workplace tools, with reports of interruptions to services in sectors including healthcare, aviation, policing and education.

World.title: Silva says Portugal ready for spotlight without Ronaldo
World.content:
Portugal midfielder Bernardo Silva said Friday his team could cope with any extra pressure on them following Cristiano Ronaldo’s international retirement, ahead of their first match without the superstar forward.

Jorge Jesus’s side host Denmark in Braga on Saturday in the Nations League, with a tribute planned for their all-time leading goalscorer.

Real Madrid’s Silva, who inherits the captain’s armband from Ronaldo, admitted that the striker had been the main focus for much of the past two decades but backed the team to cope with the pressure in the 41-year-old’s absence.

“Everyone knows the weight Cristiano carries. Most people went to the stadium to see Cristiano, many went just for him, and that’s not going to happen now,” Silva told reporters.

“The national team players are used to the spotlight, the pressure, and the responsibility, as well as being pointed at when things don’t go well — so that’s not an issue.”

Portugal will pay tribute to five-time Ballon d’Or winner Ronaldo before the game against Denmark, with media reporting the squad will walk out wearing number seven jerseys, Ronaldo’s number.

Whether Ronaldo will be present is unknown, after he fell out with veteran coach Jorge Jesus in September.

Last week Ronaldo said he was bringing down the curtain on his storied international career.

Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 and went on to play a world record 234 times for his country, scoring 146 goals.

“Nobody can forget Cris’s 23 years in the national team and everything he did,” Jesus told reporters.

“I think (paying tribute) is a brilliant idea to continue to remind us that he is a legend of Portuguese football.”

Portugal have already sealed qualification to the quarter-finals of the Nations League, winning all four matches in Group A4.

World.title: FG records 16 Nigerian deaths in Addis Ababa, warns travellers
World.content:
By Favour Ulebor, Abuja

The Federal Government has warned Nigerians, particularly those with pre-existing medical conditions, to exercise caution when travelling through Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, following the deaths of 16 Nigerians in the city this year.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed this in a travel advisory issued on Friday, stating that the deaths recorded by Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa were reportedly linked to health complications associated with the city’s high altitude.

The ministry explained that Addis Ababa is situated approximately 2,355 metres (7,726 feet) above sea level, where lower atmospheric pressure results in reduced oxygen availability.

It noted that the conditions could pose increased health risks to travellers with certain underlying medical conditions, particularly cardiovascular and respiratory ailments.

According to the advisory, although healthy individuals are generally able to adapt to reduced oxygen levels in high-altitude environments, people with certain pre-existing health conditions may experience complications.

The Federal Government therefore advised Nigerians whose medical conditions could be worsened by high altitudes to seek appropriate medical advice before undertaking journeys involving transit through the Ethiopian capital.

It also urged travellers with underlying medical conditions to consult medical professionals and obtain necessary guidance before embarking on their trips.

The ministry, however, clarified that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa.

Rather, it said the notice was aimed at ensuring that medically vulnerable travellers were adequately informed about the possible effects of high altitudes and took necessary precautions.

The advisory stated, “This year, Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa has recorded 16 deaths involving Nigerians transiting through the city, reportedly linked to health complications associated with high altitudes.

“While healthy individuals are generally able to adapt to reduced oxygen levels in high-altitude environments, persons with certain pre-existing medical ailments, particularly cardiovascular and respiratory conditions, may experience increased health risks in such conditions.

“In view of the foregoing, Nigerians with pre-existing health conditions that can be exacerbated by high altitudes are strongly advised to exercise caution when planning journeys that involve transit through Addis Ababa.

“Travellers with underlying medical conditions are also urged to obtain appropriate medical guidance before undertaking such journeys.”

The ministry reiterated that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa but to ensure that those vulnerable to the physiological effects of high altitudes were adequately informed.

It reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to protecting the health, safety and wellbeing of Nigerians travelling abroad, adding that it would continue to provide timely information and guidance to safeguard their welfare.

World.title: Kidnappers kill Kaduna farmer after collecting N56m ransom
World.content:
police badge

By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo

Armed kidnappers have reportedly killed an Abuja-based worker and farmer, Ibrahim Kadafa, popularly known as Ibro, after collecting N56 million ransom and other valuables from his family following his abduction along the Kaduna-Abuja highway.

Kadafa was abducted alongside his friend, Mustapha Shelpidi, on October 28, 2026, while supervising the harvesting of soybeans on his farm around Alheri Camp, Kilometre 30, along the Kaduna-Abuja road.

The two friends were reportedly seized when armed men invaded the farm and took them to an undisclosed location.

Following the abduction, the kidnappers initially demanded N100 million ransom from the family but later reduced the amount to N80 million after negotiations.

A family source said that in a desperate effort to secure Kadafa’s release, the family eventually raised and paid N56 million, alongside three brand-new Samsung mobile phones and a recharge card worth N20,000.

The payment was reportedly made within two weeks of negotiations, as the family struggled to meet the demands of the abductors in the hope of securing his safe return.

However, the family’s hope of reuniting with him was shattered on Wednesday, November 11, when they reportedly received his lifeless body instead.

The source disclosed that Kadafa sustained a gunshot injury to his leg while allegedly attempting to escape during the abduction but was reportedly denied access to medical attention throughout his captivity.

The family reportedly suspects that complications arising from the untreated gunshot wound may have contributed to his death, although the exact circumstances surrounding his demise remain unclear.

The incident has renewed concerns over the activities of armed kidnappers along the Kaduna-Abuja highway, where travellers and residents of adjoining farming communities continue to face security threats.

World.title: Goalkeeper Owono suspended for 12 matches after De Miguel death
World.content:
FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono was suspended for 12 matches by the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee on Friday after his challenge on Jesus de Miguel resulted in the death of the Tenerife striker last week.

Equatorial Guinea international Owono was sent off in the second division clash on November 2 after racing into midfield and colliding with De Miguel while trying to clear an aerial ball.

After the collision De Miguel, 30, was placed in intensive care in hospital and the Spanish forward died on November 3.

“The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee’s report, which states that the player was sent off for ‘violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’,” said the committee in a statement.

“The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge.

“In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances… the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified.”

Spanish police sources last week told AFP an investigation into what happened had been opened under judicial supervision.

Owono said he was enduring the “hardest days of my life” after De Miguel’s death.

“These are the hardest days of my life. I struggle to find the words and it is very difficult for me to process anything that has happened,” said Owono in a statement published by his club Andorra last week.

“I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, of his family, and of all the people who loved him.

“I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are going through. Rest in peace, Jesus.”

FC Andorra coach Carles Manso said Thursday it would be Owono who decides if and when he returns to football after the tragic incident.

On Saturday Tenerife fans and players gathered at the club’s stadium for a memorial and farewell to De Miguel.

His funeral took place last Thursday and around 400 mourners attended, including Spain coach Luis de la Fuente and Real Madrid president Florentino Perez.

World.title: Lagos NDC meeting attack threatens democracy — APM candidate
World.content:
By Dapo Akinrefon

The governorship candidate of the Action Peoples Movement (APM) in Lagos State, Prince Laja Adeoye, has condemned the attack on supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during their town hall meeting in Lagos, describing the incident as shameful and a threat to democracy.

Adeoye said the disruption of the meeting at Classique Event Centre, Oregun, Ikeja, on Thursday, amounted to an infringement on the constitutional rights of citizens to assemble and freely express their political views.

He warned that the use of thugs to disrupt opposition gatherings could heighten political tension ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Adeoye said, “Nobody should be attacked for supporting a candidate of his or her choice. What happened in Lagos on Thursday was shameful and unacceptable in a democracy.”

He described the incident as particularly disturbing, noting that Lagos had traditionally been regarded as a centre of political activities where parties and candidates could canvass for support.

According to him, the attack was not merely against the NDC but also against the democratic process and Nigerians who believe in free and fair elections.

The APM candidate urged the Lagos State Police Command to identify, arrest and prosecute those responsible for the incident, irrespective of their political affiliation or status.

He warned that failure to bring the perpetrators to justice could encourage similar attacks in other parts of the country as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 elections.

Adeoye also expressed concern over the safety of voters, candidates and journalists during the campaign period, recalling reports that a journalist covering the meeting was attacked and dispossessed of his working equipment.

He called on political leaders to rise above partisan interests and condemn violence, stressing that democracy could not thrive in an atmosphere of fear and intimidation.

The APM candidate commended the NDC supporters for maintaining their composure despite the alleged provocation, saying their conduct demonstrated commitment to democratic values.

“The supporters did not retaliate. They conducted themselves in a peaceful manner. That is the spirit we need to sustain our democracy,” he said.

He urged political parties to caution their supporters against violence and embrace issue-based campaigns rather than intimidation and thuggery.

Adeoye also called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), security agencies and other political stakeholders to work together to guarantee a level playing field for all parties ahead of the 2027 elections.

He said Lagos, as the country’s commercial nerve centre, should demonstrate that elections could be contested and won without violence.

He further urged the National Peace Committee and civil society organisations to intervene by encouraging political actors to embrace peaceful political engagement.

According to him, Nigerians were more concerned about finding solutions to insecurity, unemployment, rising cost of living and poor infrastructure than political violence.

Adeoye sympathised with those reportedly injured during the attack and wished them a speedy recovery, while urging the NDC to remain focused on its campaign.

“We must not allow a few disgruntled elements to derail our democracy. The 2027 election must be about ideas, not violence,” he said.

He reaffirmed the APM’s commitment to peaceful, credible and transparent elections, as well as respect for the rule of law and democratic values.

World.title: Data Protection: NDPC Trains DPCOs, Warns Against Sharp Practices
World.content:
In a bid to deepen compliance culture within the Nigeria data processing ecosystem, the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) has conducted a practical audit training for licensed Data Protection Compliance Organisations (DPCOs) in Abuja.

The two-day training, held on November 10 -11, 2026 at the Nigerian Army Conference Centre and Suites (NACCAS),was organised by the commission in collaboration with Meta under the NDPC Initiative for Data Protection.

While declaring the training open, NDPC National Commissioner and CEO, Dr Vincent Olatunji, said the DPCOs as licensed entities authorised to carry out data protection services on behalf of the commission,need adequate training and retraining to effectively discharge their duties in line with ethical best practices.

According to him, the number of licensed DPCOs across Nigeria has expanded from an initial 17 to 367 organisations, a steady growth that reflects rising nationwide demand for data privacy auditing and compliance advisory.

The NDPC helmsman urged the DPCOs to uphold utmost ethical standards as they act on behalf of the commission, warning against nonchalance and sharp practices to avoid penalties, adding that licenses will be revoked for submitting false or misleading compliance audit reports and inaccurate fillings.

“As regulators, we have given part of our power to you to work for us , and you must do the work very well, and that is why this training will continue on a regular basis,” he said.

Olatunji noted that the directive by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and a July 27, 2026 circular from the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (OSGF, mandating all Ministries, Departments, and Agencies (MDAs) to comply fully with the Nigeria Data Protection Act (NDP Act), 2023, has opened new frontiers for the DPCOs in form of consulting opportunities.

In her presentation, Ibukunoluwa Owa, Head of Regulations Unit at the NDPC, spoke on the DPCO ecosystem as a public-private partnership approach to privacy regulation.

While explaining the DPCO code of conduct, OWa noted that limited manpower and resources to supervise data controllers and data processors necessitated the DPCO initiative, adding that Nigeria has over 220 million data subjects, and adopting a Public-Private Partnership(PPP) model was imperative to raise awareness and deepen the privacy culture across Nigeria.

Thematic focus of the two-day training included Compliance Checklist Audit, Audit Governance and Documentation, Auditing Security and Technical Measures, Auditing Transfer and Third-Party Systems, Findings, Risk Rating and the Audit Report, among other topics.

Some of the participants who spoke with newsmen on the sideline, expressed appreciation to NDPC and Meta for the training, describing it as a timely intervention in the discharge of their duties as DPCOs.

Adefunke Makanjuola,Joan Consult Limited, said: “I learnt so much from this training.’ As DPCOs, there are so many things we were not doing so well before now, but with this training we are in a better position to do things seamlessly”.

Also speaking, Adaeze Onu of ECAM Global Services Nig.Ltd, lauded NDPC for the opportunity, adding that “the event has been very insightful and quite practical because the facilitators have been great with the teaching”.

“They have given us practical insight into how to properly ensure that organisations comply with the NDPA Act and also how to perform different kinds of tests,” she said.

A facilitator, Timothy Ogele, said the DPCOs were the only authorised bodies to help the NDPC ensure compliance, and therefore needed periodic training.

“There have been a lot of gaps in compliance audits, either due to lack of depth in terms of understanding what needs to be done right, or procedural defects.

“This training will actually help the DPCOs to actually know what to do in terms of conducting compliance audits,” he said.

World.title: Champion Breweries to Become Champion Brands Amid Drive For Next Phase of Growth
World.content:
Champion Breweries Plc has proposed a restructuring that will establish Champion Brands Limited as the new parent company of the group, reflecting its evolution into a broader, multi-category African beverage business.

Under the proposed Scheme of Arrangement, Champion Brands Limited will be re-registered as a public limited liability company, Champion Brands Plc, and become the group’s new parent company listed on Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX).

Champion Breweries will become its subsidiary and be delisted, while enJOYbev B.V., whose portfolio includes the Bullet range of beverages, will also become a direct subsidiary of Champion Brands.

Chairman of Champion Breweries, Imo-Abasi Jacob, in a statement, said: “Our ambitions extend beyond the businesses and markets we serve today. We want to strengthen our existing brands, develop new products and pursue opportunities in new markets. The proposed structure is designed not just for the business we have today, but for the group we intend to build over the long term.

“We believe this is the right next step for Champion and its shareholders. The Scheme changes the group’s corporate structure, not shareholders’ proportionate ownership. Champion Brands, once listed, will be subject to the governance and disclosure requirements applicable to NGX-listed companies. The Board unanimously recommends that shareholders vote in favour of the Scheme.”

Managing Director/CEO, Malolan Sampath, in a statement, added that: “The group’s operations, brands, employees, customers and suppliers are unaffected by the Scheme. Champion Breweries will continue producing

“Under the Scheme, existing shareholders will receive one Champion Brands share for every Champion Breweries share held, preserving their proportionate ownership. The restructuring remains subject to the necessary approvals.”

The company is proposing one-for-one share exchange: “The 11,323,611,233 ordinary shares of Champion Breweries held by Scheme Shareholders will be exchanged for an equivalent number of fully paid ordinary shares in Champion Brands. Shareholders will retain their proportionate ownership without any additional payment,” the company said in the statement.

New group structure

Champion Breweries will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Champion Brands. Champion Breweries’ shareholding in enJOYbev B.V. will also be transferred to Champion Brands, resulting in both Champion Breweries and enJOYbev B.V. becoming direct subsidiaries of Champion Brands.

Transition of Champion Brands to a new publicly listed parent

Following the implementation of the Scheme, Champion Breweries’ shares will be delisted from NGX, and Champion Brands, following its re-registration as a public limited liability company; it will become the group’s publicly listed parent company, subject to the necessary regulatory approvals.

Champion Breweries will continue its brewing operations in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, producing Champion Lager and Champ Malta.

Champion Breweries has evolved from a Nigerian brewing business into a broader, multi-category beverage group. Its recent acquisition of enJOYbev B.V. brought the Bullet portfolio into the group, expanding its product offering and geographic presence across 14 African markets.

The proposed restructuring reflects this evolution. The Board believes that a holding-company structure is better suited to the scale and ambitions of the expanded group, offering three principal strategic advantages.

First is a clearer group identity and investment proposition. Champion Brands will represent the broader beverage group as its listed parent company, giving investors a clearer view of the group’s portfolio and the businesses underpinning its growth.

Champion Lager and Champ Malta in Uyo, while we remain focused on strengthening our brands, expanding our reach and serving our customers.

Under the Scheme, for every Champion Breweries share held, Scheme shareholders will receive one Champion Brands share, preserving their proportionate ownership. No shareholder is diluted or bought out through the exchange.

The Champion Brands shares will be issued as fully paid. Shareholders will not be required to make any additional payment or application to receive them.

Shareholders own shares in the wider group

Through Champion Brands, shareholders will hold an interest in the parent company of both Champion Breweries and enJOYbev B.V., bringing the group’s beverage businesses under one corporate structure.

The shareholders’ investment remains in a listed group

Champion Breweries will be delisted from NGX, while Champion Brands will become the group’s new publicly listed parent company, subject to the necessary approvals.

A shareholder vote is required

The Scheme proceeds only if shareholders approve it and the necessary regulatory approvals are obtained. The Scheme is to be completed in the first quarter (Q1) of 2027. Shares in Champion Breweries continue to trade on NGX as normal pending implementation of the Scheme.

World.title: Tinubu Fags Off Bakassi Deep Seaport, Says Project Will Redefine Nigeria’s Maritime Economy
World.content:
* Otu hails historic milestone; Oyetola projects massive investment

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has described the groundbreaking of the Bakassi Deep Seaport as a defining milestone in Nigeria’s economic diversification, saying it was a strategic national investment.

Represented by Vice-President Kashim Shettima, at the ceremony in Bakassi on Friday, November 13, 2026, the president said the port would open new commercial corridors, stimulate industrialisation and create jobs.

He commended Governor Bassey Edet Otu and the people of Cross River for sustaining the vision and advancing it towards actualisation.

Tinubu recalled that the project was conceived in 2014, with an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment developed in March 2015, before receiving renewed impetus under Otu.

Designed as a 20-metre-draft facility, the port is expected to accommodate large vessels that currently bypass Nigerian ports. It is also linked to a 260-kilometre superhighway to move cargo to markets across the country.

He credited Otu’s determination with helping to overcome institutional and financial obstacles, including efforts to secure a $3.5 billion Afreximbank financing arrangement and formalise the PPP framework in February 2025.

“This is beyond a Cross River dream. It is a Nigerian project. It is a poverty breaker,” he declared.

He stressed that the port would complement, not undermine, Lagos. “Lagos is not our enemy. Lagos is our elder brother in trade. No country eats with one hand. No country carries all its loads on one shoulder. That shoulder will break,” he said.

More than 80 per cent of Nigeria’s foreign trade, he noted, passes through Lagos, contributing to congestion and rising costs. A second major maritime gateway, he argued, would strengthen the national economy: “When Calabar works, Nigeria works on two legs.”

The president said Nigeria had not fully exploited its Gulf of Guinea coastline, while neighbouring countries benefited from trade Nigerian ports could attract.

The Bakassi project, he maintained, would help retain regional cargo, expand international market access and strengthen the country’s maritime competitiveness.

Tinubu further observed that roughly 90 per cent of cargo moves by sea, yet Nigeria handles only a fraction of regional cargo trade despite its economic weight in West Africa.

The port, he said, would help close that gap, reduce dependence on a single gateway and position the country to capture a greater share of maritime commerce.

He acknowledged the territorial and economic losses Cross River suffered following the Bakassi peninsula ruling and the loss of oil revenue, but said these setbacks had not diminished the people’s courage, hospitality or resilience.

“The peninsula was not the end of your story, but the beginning of your next chapter,” he declared, urging residents to protect the project from political interference and regard it as an inheritance for future generations.

The state governor, Senator Bassey Otu, in his speech, hailed the groundbreaking and credited President Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda with providing the decisive federal support that revived the project.

He said political, administrative, legal and environmental challenges had stalled implementation until Tinubu’s plan to expand and upgrade maritime corridors created a fresh opportunity for Cross River.

Lauding Tinubu for guiding the state through the processes leading to the Certificate of Compliance and final federal approval, Otu described him as “a bastion of economic diversification and social equity.”

He recalled Calabar’s long maritime heritage, saying the new facility would reinforce Cross River’s established littoral status, adding that the project’s approval and delivery demonstrated the value of cooperation between the federal and state governments.

The governor said the state had completed preparatory work, including an Environmental Impact Assessment and hydrographic, geotechnical and geophysical surveys, and secured federal approvals.

The project is to be delivered through a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) arrangement, with an initial funding approval of $2.27 billion.

He said logistics, trade, fishing, shipping, tourism and shipbuilding would benefit, positioning Cross River as a Gulf of Guinea maritime hub. The surveys, he added, exposed flaws in the 1903 navigational charts, which the Federal Government replaced on October 1, 2026, affirming the state’s littoral status.

Otu disclosed that selected Cross Riverians were undergoing specialised training for construction and operational roles, with knowledge transfer planned.

He pointed to the state’s three-way economic corridor—the airport, seaport and Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway—to facilitate cargo movement and attract investors.

He invited investors in maritime and related industries to take advantage of the project’s prospects and the state’s investment-friendly environment, including a one-stop investment hub and tax incentives.

He described the economic possibilities as boundless and called on development partners to help build a resilient economy.

In his goodwill remarks, the Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Dr Gboyega Oyetola, praised Tinubu’s efforts to unlock Nigeria’s maritime potential, citing the creation of the ministry in 2023 and approval of the country’s first National Policy on Marine and Blue Economy.

Oyetola disclosed that revenue generated by agencies under the ministry rose from N700.79 billion in 2023 to N1.83 trillion in 2025, attributing the increase to improved revenue assurance and the closure of leakages.

He also cited the elimination of piracy in Nigerian waters, approval for modernisation of the six legacy seaports, stronger port governance through the Nigerian Ports Economic Regulatory Act, and Nigeria’s election to the decision-making Council of the International Maritime Organization after almost two decades.

He also cited the lifting of United States Coast Guard restrictions on Nigerian-bound vessels in August 2026, release of the Cabotage Vessel Financing Fund to shipowners and growth in fish production from 1.1 million to 1.4 million tonnes.

He said Bakassi would improve market access and create industrial, investment and employment opportunities. Its integration with the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, he stressed, would enhance commercial viability and extend benefits across Cross River, the South-south and the wider Nigerian economy.

Oyetola pledged the ministry’s support for a modern, efficient and environmentally sustainable port. He described the seaport as an important instrument for translating Nigeria’s maritime advantages into sustainable growth.

The minister said the groundbreaking marks a shift in Nigeria’s maritime geography, offering Cross River the prospect of converting its coastal location and heritage into investment, jobs and sustained economic activity, while helping Nigeria diversify its economy, ease pressure on existing ports and strengthen its role in regional trade.

World.title: NNPC Ltd., Pipeline Professionals Partner To Boost Infrastructure, Indigenous Capacity
World.content:
Bennett Oghifo

The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Ltd. (NNPC Ltd.) says it will collaborate with the Pipeline Professionals Association of Nigeria (PLAN) to strengthen indigenous capacity, reduce pipeline operational costs and improve infrastructure financing.

The Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Ltd., Mr Bashir Ojulari, said this when members of PLAN, led by its Chairman, Board of Trustees, Mr Geoff Onuoha, paid him a courtesy visit on Thursday in Abuja.

Ojulari identified capacity building, cost reduction and innovative financing as key areas of collaboration between the company and the professional association.

“By working together, we will be able to reduce overall pipeline costs and make more projects economically viable and attractive to investors.

“The partnership will focus on developing individual expertise and training more pipeline engineers to strengthen indigenous technical capacity in the oil and gas industry,” Ojulari said.

On financing, he disclosed that NNPC Ltd. had raised 1.5 billion dollars for the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) Gas Pipeline Project based solely on projected pipeline throughput.

He described the development as a milestone, noting that it demonstrated the viability of securing financing for pipeline infrastructure independently of upstream or downstream projects.

Ojulari said the financing model had created opportunities for similar projects, adding that NNPC Ltd. would explore further collaboration with PLAN in developing bankable pipeline projects.

On pipeline security, he said the company was working with government security agencies and community surveillance contractors under an integrated pipeline security framework coordinated by the Office of the National Security Adviser.

He explained that the approach combined conventional security measures with community engagement to address pipeline vandalism, crude oil theft and other operational challenges.

According to him, the strategy has improved the availability of major pipelines to between 95 and 100 per cent over the last 18 months.

Ojulari further emphasised the importance of host community development, saying the effective implementation of Host Community Development Trusts under the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) 2021 was contributing to improved relations with host communities.

He said NNPC Ltd. was also exploring ways to promote shared prosperity through job creation and other economic opportunities to discourage youths from engaging in pipeline vandalism.

Earlier, Onuoha said PLAN had consistently advocated the integration of social considerations into pipeline operations, adding that host communities must have a sense of ownership and involvement in protecting the infrastructure.

He said the association had developed and promoted social metrics for pipeline operations, recognising that effective pipeline security depended not only on technical measures but also on the relationship between operators and host communities.

“And we’ve been communicating with NNPC on that, especially on the social, technical relationship as far as pipeline operation is concerned.

“The association’s advocacy has contributed to discussions around host community development and the need to strengthen the social dimension of pipeline operations,” he said.

Also speaking, PLAN’s Vice President, Mr Adeche Omotosho-Oboro, said the visit was aimed at strengthening engagement with NNPC Ltd., and establishing a strategic partnership to address challenges in the transportation of crude oil and gas.

Omotosho-Oboro, who is also the Managing Director of Umugini Pipeline Infrastructure Ltd., said the association was bringing pipeline professionals together to promote collective solutions to infrastructure and transportation challenges.

He identified security, long-term infrastructure planning and indigenous technical capacity as key areas requiring collaboration with NNPC Ltd.

He said the partnership would enable industry professionals to align their technical capabilities with NNPC Ltd.’s long-term plans for pipeline infrastructure and projected transportation requirements.

He added that PLAN’s forthcoming 2026 Nigerian International Pipeline Technology and Energy Conference and Exhibition (NIPITECS), scheduled to hold from Nov. 17 to Nov. 18, would focus on financing and developing bankable pipeline projects.

Mr Audu Ibrahim, Managing Director, NNPC Gas Infrastructure Company (NGIC), a subsidiary of NNPC Ltd., was appointed as PLAN’s NNPC focal point person to strengthen coordination between the association and the national oil company.

Speaking on the appointment, Ibrahim described it as an opportunity to advance the oil and gas industry through stronger partnerships and the integration of indigenous technical expertise.

He said although NNPC Ltd. already worked with several members of the association in their individual capacities as service providers, PLAN offered a platform for consolidating their expertise into a unified resource.

“The platform will enable NNPC Ltd. to leverage the collective knowledge and capabilities of pipeline professionals to improve industry operations and deliver better results.

Highlights of the visit included the presentation of plaque to the NNPC Ltd. GCEO, as well as the presentation of the brochure for the 2026 NIPITECS and information materials on PLAN.

World.title: Police Dismantle Terrorist Logistics Network, Arrest Eight Suspected Bandits, Criminals
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Nigeria Police Force has said that operatives of the Intelligence Response Team (IRT) dismantled a terrorist logistics network and arrested no fewer than eight suspected terrorists, bandits and other criminal elements during intelligence-led operations at different locations across the country.

Speaking during a press briefing and the parade of arrested suspects at the IRT headquarters in Abuja on Friday, the Commander of the Force Intelligence Department, Intelligence Response Team (FID-IRT), DCP Adamu Muazu, said the operations were part of the team’s intelligence-led activities aimed at identifying, disrupting and dismantling criminal networks involved in kidnapping, banditry, armed robbery, terrorism-related activities and other violent crimes across the country.

He revealed that the operations had yielded significant results, including the arrest of suspected criminal elements and the recovery of illegal firearms.

According to him, “On 29/08/2026, in a significant intelligence-led operation, operatives of the Intelligence Response Team successfully apprehended two suspects, namely Nura Umar, ‘M’, 20, of Kidandan, and Alh. Rabiu Aliyu, ‘M’, 58, of Zaria, Kaduna State, who were involved in kidnapping and banditry-related activities, with links to suspected terrorism-financing operations. They specialise in supplying motorcycles to bandits and confessed to having supplied several motorcycles to bandits operating along the Kaduna and Katsina axis. One Honda CV-125 motorcycle without a registration number was recovered as an exhibit.

“The arrest represents an important step in the ongoing efforts of the Nigeria Police Force to identify and dismantle the financial networks that sustain kidnapping, banditry and other forms of terrorism-related criminality.

“The suspects are currently undergoing further interrogation to establish the full extent of their involvement, identify possible accomplices and trace the financial channels through which criminal activities may have been funded.

“The IRT remains committed to ensuring that not only the perpetrators of violent crimes but also those who provide financial and logistical support to such criminal networks are brought to justice.”

DCP Muazu said six other suspects were arrested in separate operations.

He said, “In another successful operation, operatives of the Intelligence Response Team, acting on credible human and technical intelligence on the activities of a gang involved in one-chance operations, car snatching and armed robbery in Kaduna and its environs, arrested Abdullahi Abubakar, ‘M’, on 12 October 2026 at about 20:30 hours.

“The gang allegedly specialised in strangling tricycle and motorcycle operators before dispossessing them of their valuables. Abdullahi, who had previously served a 13-year prison sentence for a similar offence, was arrested during the operation.

“During interrogation, the suspect mentioned one of his gang leaders, identified as Boniface, who is currently in Kaduna Prison. Boniface reportedly directed Abdullahi to their hideout, where their operational firearms were concealed. The operatives subsequently obtained a reproduction warrant and recovered two pistols as exhibits.

“The suspects also confessed to snatching several vehicles in Kaduna and its environs and selling them to their receivers in Kano, Kaduna and the Niger Republic. Yusuf Mohammed and Bala Ibrahim, both male residents of Kaduna, were arrested as receivers. Yusuf Mohammed allegedly received stolen vehicles and arranged their delivery to the Niger Republic through Sokoto, with the assistance of one Dahiru, who is still at large. Bala Ibrahim, on the other hand, received stolen motorcycles and tricycles.”

He said the recovery of the firearms was a significant achievement in the ongoing efforts to prevent the use of illegal weapons in the commission of violent crimes, particularly armed robbery and other offences that threaten public safety.

World.title: 2027 Elections: Immigration Service, DSS Move to Block Foreign Interference, Irregular Migration
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) and the Department of State Services (DSS) have vowed to strengthen border security and tighten migration controls to prevent foreigners and irregular migrants from interfering in Nigeria’s 2027 general elections.

The two security agencies said they would intensify intelligence sharing, joint surveillance and coordinated security operations to prevent foreign elements from exploiting the country’s borders to infiltrate Nigeria and undermine the electoral process.

The commitment was made on Friday at the headquarters of the Nigeria Immigration Service in Abuja during the formal flag-off of the 2027 General Elections Sensitisation Programme.

The event was attended by the Comptroller-General of Immigration, Kemi Nandap; Director-General of the DSS, Oluwatosin Ajayi; and representatives of the Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Ahmed Abubakar Audi, and the Controller-General of the Nigerian Correctional Service, Sylvester Nwakuche.

Speaking at the event, Nandap, who was represented by the Deputy Comptroller-General in charge of Visa and Residency, Franca Usiwoma Nwanneka, charged immigration personnel to remain vigilant and ensure effective coordination of their operations before, during and after the elections.

She described the 2027 general elections as a critical period requiring collective vigilance and the commitment of all institutions responsible for protecting the country’s security and democratic processes.

According to her, the Immigration Service occupies a strategic position in Nigeria’s security architecture because of its responsibility for border security and migration management.

She warned that irregular migration, human trafficking, migrant smuggling and other transnational criminal activities could pose significant threats to national security if not adequately addressed.

“Today’s workshop is particularly significant as Nigeria prepares for the 2027 general elections. Beyond the responsibility of conducting credible elections, there is the equally important task of providing a peaceful and secure environment in which the democratic processes can thrive.

“Achieving this requires collective vigilance, effective coordination and the commitment of all institutions entrusted with safeguarding our nation,” she said.

Nandap stressed that no single security agency could independently address the complex security challenges confronting the country, noting that effective intelligence sharing and sustained inter-agency collaboration were essential to preventing security breaches.

She also cautioned immigration officers against taking sides with political parties or individuals participating in the elections, insisting that personnel must maintain strict political neutrality and professionalism.

“Our officers must demonstrate the highest standards of political neutrality, discipline and respect for the rule of law. Under no circumstance should our personnel use official resources to promote partisan interests. Our loyalty must remain firmly in the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria,” she said.

The Comptroller-General further directed zonal coordinators, controllers and heads of formations to strengthen surveillance, intelligence gathering and operational deployment while ensuring close coordination with other security agencies.

She also called for proactive participation in the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES), stressing that collaboration must produce measurable results.

“Our participation in ICCES must be proactive, purposeful and result-oriented,” she added.

In his remarks, the DSS Director-General, Ajayi, represented by the Deputy Director-General in charge of Operations and Intelligence, Patrick Ikenweiwe, reaffirmed the agency’s commitment to strengthening collaboration with the Immigration Service to safeguard Nigeria’s borders throughout the electoral period.

He said the security of the country’s borders and the integrity of its migration control system would be critical to protecting the 2027 electoral process against external threats.

According to him, electoral activities could attract individuals seeking to exploit weaknesses in border controls for the movement of mercenaries, political operatives and other persons intent on undermining democratic processes.

Ajayi described the Immigration Service as the first line of national defence against irregular migration and other cross-border security threats, noting that its effectiveness would be crucial to maintaining a peaceful electoral environment.

“The Department of State Services remains committed to deepening collaboration with the Nigerian Immigration Service through timely intelligence sharing, joint threat assessments and coordinated operations, particularly along our land borders and at entry points.

“No single agency can secure the electoral space alone. Our strength lies in absolute synergy,” he said.

The DSS chief also emphasised the importance of effective supervision, accountability and measurable performance in achieving institutional security objectives.

He urged supervisors to lead by example and ensure that personnel remained professional, accountable and politically neutral throughout the electoral cycle.

The renewed security commitment comes as preparations for the 2027 general elections gather momentum, with security agencies expected to play critical roles in protecting the electoral environment, preventing cross-border threats and ensuring that eligible Nigerians can exercise their democratic rights peacefully.

World.title: Fani-Kayode Presents Letter of Credence to Ramaphosa, Pledges to Rebuild Nigeria-South Africa Relations
World.content:
*Recalls Nigeria’s anti-apartheid support

*Says historic friendship must be rebuilt

Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Ambassador Femi Fani-Kayode, has pledged to rebuild diplomatic relations between Nigeria and South Africa, describing the two countries as historic friends whose cooperation is vital to Africa’s future.



Fani-Kayode made the pledge on Friday, November 13, 2026, when he presented his Letter of Credence to South African President Cyril Ramaphosa at the Sefako Makgatho Presidential Guest House in Pretoria.



The envoy, who is also concurrently accredited to the Kingdom of Lesotho and the Kingdom of Eswatini, conveyed the warm greetings of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to the South African leader.



Speaking during the ceremony, Fani-Kayode recalled Nigeria’s support for South Africa during its struggle against apartheid, stressing the longstanding historical ties between the two countries.



“I come here standing tall and proud, having been sent by the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria to present my Letter of Credence to you, his brother and his friend. Nigeria and South Africa have a long history of fraternity and friendship. We fought together, we stood by you, and we gave our blood and our treasure for you during your dark days,” he said.



He noted that Nigeria and South Africa had reciprocated their solidarity over the years and remained major trade partners on the African continent.

The High Commissioner said one of his key responsibilities would be to rebuild confidence and strengthen cooperation between both countries.

“Part of my job here is to reset that relationship, to come and build that bridge, and to ensure that whatever concerns we have, we can work them out and move forward together. If Nigeria and South Africa work closely together, the destiny of our great continent will be more secure. It is in our mutual interest, and in the interest of our people and our continent, that we ensure that we stand tall, stand strong, and build that bridge,” he said.



Fani-Kayode also commended South Africa’s contributions to international diplomacy, particularly its role in BRICS, the Global South and Nigeria’s inclusion in the G20, describing the country’s efforts as significant to strengthening Africa’s representation in global affairs.



He further conveyed President Tinubu’s goodwill to Ramaphosa, describing the Nigerian leader as a great friend of South Africa and a personal friend of the South African President.



“Your brother, our President, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, is a great friend of South Africa and a great personal friend of yours. My prayer is that our friendship continues to grow stronger. We wish you well. We wish South Africa well. May God be with you,” he said.



In his response, President Ramaphosa urged the newly accredited heads of diplomatic missions to work closely with South Africa’s Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) to identify practical areas of collaboration.



He particularly highlighted economic growth, industrial development, job creation and skills development as priority areas for partnerships.

“We encourage you to work closely with our Department of International Relations to identify practical areas of cooperation. We particularly welcome partnerships that support economic growth, industrial development, job creation and skills,” Ramaphosa said.



The South African President assured the diplomats of his government’s support, urging them to engage relevant stakeholders and deploy diplomacy to build bridges, create opportunities and improve the lives of ordinary citizens.



He also wished the newly accredited diplomats successful tenures and welcomed them to South Africa.



Fani-Kayode subsequently presented his Letter of Credence, issued by President Tinubu, reaffirming Nigeria’s commitment to strengthening diplomatic relations and advancing mutually beneficial cooperation between the two countries.



The ceremony also featured the presentation of Letters of Credence by ambassadors and heads of diplomatic missions from the European Union, France, Germany, South Sudan, Somalia, Comoros, Madagascar, Uruguay, Vietnam, Seychelles, Belgium, Cyprus, Timor-Leste and the Maldives.

World.title: Lagos East Mega Rally: Sanwo-Olu, Others, Seek Voters’ Support for Tinubu, Hamzat
World.content:
Bennett Oghifo

Lagos State Governor, Mr. Babajide Olusola Sanwo-Olu, has applauded President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s contributions to Lagos’ development, urging residents to show appreciation for his infrastructural interventions by supporting his second-term bid.

The Governor, who spoke while addressing party faithful, at the Lagos East Senatorial District All Progressives Congress (APC) State Mega Rally, Epe, Lagos said President Tinubu had laid a solid foundation for Lagos State over two decades ago, providing the blueprint for the state’s sustained growth and development.

According to him, “ The President deserves more than our votes. He deserves our prayers and our support. I therefore urged Lagos residents to demonstrate their appreciation for the President’s leadership by turning out in large numbers on January 16 to express their support and vote massively for him.”

The Governor added that Lagos had become one of Africa’s most sought-after city-states through deliberate policies, strategic planning and visionary leadership initiated under the President’s political and administrative stewardship.

Sanwo-Olu observed that the President’s transition from Lagos to the national stage had provided an opportunity to replicate his development philosophy across Nigeria, with ongoing interventions and projects cutting across the six geopolitical zones.

The Governor further highlighted the President’s commitment to improving the welfare of Nigerians, noting that students were benefiting from educational interventions, young people were receiving grants and empowerment support, retirees were accessing their pensions, while vulnerable and elderly citizens were receiving assistance through various social investment programmes.

Speaking further, the Governor stated that Tinubu is also commited to Lagos State, acknowledging that the Federal Government’s support for critical infrastructure projects, including the proposed development of the Green Line Rail and Lekki International, Airport, alongside other major projects expected to strengthen connectivity, boost economic activities and consolidate Lagos’ position as a leading investment destination.

Similarly, the Deputy Governor, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, said the purpose of the campaign visit to the Lagos East Senatorial District was to canvass support for all APC candidates, urging residents to come out en masse on election day to vote rather than stay at home.

He noted that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu had recorded significant achievements in infrastructure, education, healthcare and other critical sectors, stressing the need for Lagosians to support the continuation of the administration’s development efforts.

“On election day, let us not stay at home. Come out with your PVC and ensure that everyone in your neighbourhood votes. We have the highest number of registered voters in Nigeria. Let us come out to vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and every candidate that will support the continuity of his good work,” Hamzat said.

In his remarks, the Senator representing Lagos East Senatorial District, Senator Tokunbo Abiru, said President Bola Ahmed Tinubu had laid the foundation for the development and transformation Lagos State was witnessing today, noting that his contributions to the state and the country were significant.

He urged Lagosians to demonstrate their appreciation for the President’s efforts by supporting his re-election for a second term, adding that the state had capable leaders to sustain the administration’s development agenda. “We have capable people in Lagos. So, on election day, let us come out in our numbers to vote for all our candidates and ensure that they all return to power,” Abiru said.

The former governor of the state, Mr. Akinwunmi Ambode emphasised the APC’s consistency and longstanding presence in Lagos politics, noting that the party had remained committed to its political identity rather than moving between political platforms.

Ambode described the APC as a party that represents the people, stressing the importance of cooperation between the party and the electorate, saying that “the left hand washes the right hand, and the right hand washes the left hand” to illustrate the need for mutual support.

He also drew attention to the history of the APC compared with other political parties, noting that some of the other contenders and their parties were relatively new, while the APC had a longer history of governance and political experience.

In his remarks, the Chairman, APC Lagos Chapter urged eligible voters who were yet to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) to do so, describing the card as their investment in the future and a vital instrument for participating in the democratic process.

He admonished residents to come out and exercise their civic responsibility, expressing confidence in the party’s vision of development and concluding that unity remained its strength and victory its destination.

In his welcome address, the Director-General of the PBAT-KOH Campaign Organisation, Lagos State, Senator Musiliu Obanikoro, urged Lagosians to remain steadfast in their support for the All Progressives Congress (APC), urging them to vote for all candidates of the party in the 2027 General elections to sustain the state’s tradition of progressive governance, continuity and development.

While describing Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, as the most prepared men for the development of both the state and the country, Obanikoro stressed the impressive track record and experience of both candidates.

In the same vein, the Chairman of Ibeju-Lekki Local Government and Chairman of Conference 57 (the umbrella body for the 57 local government and LCDA chairmen, Mr. Engr. Abdullahi Sesan Olowa called on party members and supporters to intensify grassroots mobilisation across Lagos East, urging them to take the APC message to every household, neighbourhood, community, village and town in the Senatorial District.

He stressed the need for sustained unity and collective commitment among party faithful in demonstrating support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the Lagos State Governor, the Senator representing Lagos East and members of the House of Representatives

World.title: Updated rankings after Springboks lose to France
World.content:
The battle between the Springboks and France was always expected to be an epic encounter, and ultimately some ill-discipline and poor executions came back to haunt South Africa, while also impacting the World Rugby rankings.

In the first half, France scored three tries to one to take a 21-7 lead, and although the Springboks were far better in the second period, they ultimately couldn’t capitalise.

Withstanding immense pressure during the final stage of the clash, France ultimately held on for a 21-19 win, which has also had a huge impact on the rankings.



The defeat sees the Springboks lose 1.56 rankings points, which sees them drop to second in the rankings behind New Zealand.

In turn, Les Bleus gain 1.56 rankings points and jump into third place into third spot ahead of Ireland.

HOW THE RANKINGS LOOK After THE SPRINGBOK DEFEAT

Rank Country Points 1 New Zealand 92.65 2 Springboks 91.53 3 France 89.05 4 Ireland 88.70 5 England 86.99 6 Scotland 84.40 7 Australia 83.12 8 Argentina 81.62 9 Fiji 77.79 10 Wales 77.37 11 Italy 76.30 12 Japan 75.25 13 Georgia 73.94 14 Portugal 70.52 15 USA 67.80

match recap

The hosts had more possession and enjoyed territorial advantage in the first half, and their back-three of Aaron Grandidier Nkanang, Theo Attissogbe, and Louis Bielle-Biarrey all crossed for tries.



Their first two tries came while Lood de Jager was in the sin-bin for a dangerous tackle, with Maxime Lucu yellow carded for the same reason later in the half.

Jan-Hendrik Wessels scored the Boks’ only try in the opening half, while Kurt-Lee Arendse went over on the stroke of half-time, but he was adjudged to be offside at the lineout.

The Boks scored two tries in the second half while France failed to add any points to their tally, but the hosts did enough to seal their first win over South Africa in Paris since 2005.

World.title: Springboks beaten in Paris, lose World Rugby No 1 ranking
World.content:
The Springboks fell short in their Nations Championship clash against France at the Stade de France in Paris on Friday. Image: X @Springboks

The Springboks fell short in their Nations Championship clash against France at the Stade de France in Paris on Friday, losing their World Rugby No 1 ranking in the process.

When the final whistle sounded, France emerged narrow 21-19 winners having led 21-7 at half-time.

It was France’s first win over South Africa in Paris since 2005.



Slipped to second place

The Springboks scored three tries through hookers Jan-Hendrik Wessels and Malcolm Marx, and replacement scrumhalf Cobus Reinach. Flyhalf Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu added two conversions.

South Africa entered the match top of the World Rugby standings on 93.09 points, 0.44 ahead of New Zealand on 92.65.

However, they lost 1.56 points to drop to second, with France picking up 1.56 points, moving to third place overall.

South Africa will take on Ireland in their next Nations Championship match on Saturday, 21 November in Dublin.

World.title: Gayton seeking votes in Orania: ‘I need to visit more’

Gayton McKenzie is hoping to receive more votes to his party from Orania residents. Images via X/Canva

Gayton McKenzie has joked about campaigning for votes in Orania, a white Afrikaner-only town in the Northern Cape, after his party, the Patriotic Alliance, received a single vote in last week’s local government elections.

As did the EFF, whose lone voter has made headlines over their “rebellious” act.

GAYTON JOKES ABOUT CANVASSING VOTES IN ORANIA

On his social media platforms, Gayton McKenzie reacted to the PA receiving only 1 vote at the Orania voting station during last week’s local government elections.



He posted: “My visit to Orania delivered one vote; I need to visit more between now and 2029😂🤛🏾”

Apart from the PA, the following parties recorded votes in the conservative town…

Freedom Front Plus – 405

DA – 44

ACDP – 5

EFF – 1

PA – 1

ANC – 0

My visit to Orania delivered one vote, I need to visit more between now & 2029😂🤛🏾 pic.twitter.com/8Vuxgq2aK4  November 10, 2026

‘PITY IT IS ONLY FOR AFRIKANERS’

Gayton McKenzie is one of several South African public profiles who have documented their trip to Orania. In 2023, the PA leader visited the Afrikaner-only town to meet with local leaders and learn more about the community.

Sharing a lengthy X thread, the Gayton came to the following conclusions:

Orania is a white-only town. Black people are not allowed to buy land or stay there. According to leaders, this is a means to “preserve” the Afrikaaner culture

The town does not permit any members of the LGBTQ community to enter the town

The population is about 3000 people, and residents thrive on keeping the town clean

Orania has its own currency – Ora – and even its own Reserve Bank-registered bank. It also has its own flag

The town has multiple thriving businesses which employ residents

It is self-sufficient, with its own schools, factories, and hospitals.

Afrikaans is the only language spoken and taught

Despite having a small population, the town has “futuristic” financial practices

Reflecting on the experience, he added: “The saddest part about Orania is that they are doing exactly what we should be doing in SA, which is building infrastructure, technical schools, empowering people, and having dreams.

He shared: “I met the leaders of Orania, and they are all very idealistic. Just a pity that it is only for Afrikaners”.

Many of those insulting her defended the millions spent on the so-called super fans – I wonder if Mama Joy knows the difference between a ruck and a maul”

The sports fan cheekily clapped back: “I don’t know”



I only know Mapimpi — MamaJoy Chauke (@JoyChauke5) November 12, 2026

Another X user questioned her knowledge of sports icons in South Africa, to which she sarcastically responded: “I only know Mapimpi”

I don’t know — MamaJoy Chauke (@JoyChauke5) November 11, 2026

I just wish it’s true pic.twitter.com/7T9AeS05t3  November 12, 2026

In an interview with SwimSwam, Tatjana Smith set the record straight on why she chose to switch sporting nationalities.

World.title: Food delivery e-riders face ‘dehumanising’ work conditions as some earn R50 a day
World.content:
An organisation is calling for meaningful reform to improve working conditions for e-riders. Image: ILRIG

According to the International Labour Research and Information Group (ILRIG), some food delivery e-riders in South Africa earn as little as R50 a day.

Others work up to 12 hours daily, seven days a week, just to make ends meet.

A new study has exposed the harsh realities facing motorcycle delivery riders in Cape Town and Johannesburg. It paints a picture of low wages, dangerous working conditions and little support from delivery platforms.



The research was conducted between July and September 2026. It involved interviews with 60 e-riders as part of a project by the ILRIG.

The findings challenge the idea that food delivery is a flexible side hustle. Instead, the study found that it is the sole source of income for most riders.

In fact, 98.3% of those interviewed worked full-time. Most had been continuously employed for more than two years.



Despite being classified as independent contractors, riders faced strict monitoring and surveillance. These included roster, rating and clocking systems, as well as rules enforced through algorithms.

“In the interviews conducted with the e-riders, several digital platforms were implicated in exposing workers to dehumanising and repressive working conditions through authoritarian algorithmic management,” writes Danmore Chuma, the author of the ILRIG research paper.

E-riders face long hours, low pay and mounting expenses

The study found that riders could work up to 12 hours a day, seven days a week. However, they were only paid per delivery, with no compensation for waiting time.



Some earned an average of around R35 per order. Others reported receiving as little as R17, despite rising fuel costs.

In an interview with Cape Talk, ILRIG’s Dan Montgoma revealed just how little some riders were taking home.

“Some riders were claiming they were getting five orders per day,” Montgoma said. “If those orders were paid around R20/ order, that would mean a rider would only earn R100/day.”



“In some instances, especially in the Western Cape, they were claiming they were only getting two-three orders per day, meaning riders were getting R60, even R50 per day.”

Even these meagre earnings are further eroded by running costs. Weekly expenses can include up to R800 for bike rental and R700 for fuel.

The study found riders facing monthly costs of around R200 for data and R1 500 for shared accommodation. Food and other essentials add further pressure.



Some platforms also penalise e-riders for rejecting orders.

“On stricter platforms, turning down a delivery is treated as a refusal to work, triggering fines or two-week suspensions,” Chuma added.

“To avoid punishment and protect their algorithmic scores, riders are forced to accept low-paying or dangerous assignments without question.”



The study found that riders with ratings below 75% could face immediate dismissal.

Crime, accidents and ‘dehumanising’ treatment

The financial pressures are compounded by serious safety risks. Riders regularly navigate crime hotspots and face robberies, hijackings and road accidents.

In Cape Town, areas identified as particularly dangerous include Bellville, Kensington, Elsies River, Cravenby and Belhar.



The majority of e-riders interviewed had either survived an accident themselves or lost a colleague on the road.

Migrant riders also reported xenophobia and hate speech from customers, restaurant staff, security guards and motorists.

The study further found that platforms offered little support when things went wrong. Some riders reported being threatened with account deactivation for speaking out about their working conditions.



Montgoma added that certain riders struggled to access compensation after workplace accidents.

“Some e-riders are paying the Road Accident Fund R235.25 a week,” Montgoma said. “They told us that in some instances, they weren’t getting their RAF claims if they were involved in an accident.”

Chuma noted how one rider who suffered a fractured leg said they received no assistance, despite contributing towards accident insurance.



ILRIG argues that South Africa urgently needs a policy framework to protect digital platform workers.

While food delivery platforms offer employment opportunities, the organisation says meaningful reform is needed to ensure riders receive fair pay, safer working conditions and basic labour protections.

World.title: TikToker defends sponsored Israel trip: ‘I’m just trying to survive’
World.content:
Roseanne Pillay, a TikToker known as 'Roseyma' has defended her sponsored trip to Israel. Images via TikTok

Durban content creator Roseanne Pilay, popularly known as “Roseyma”, has defended herself amid backlash to her recent sponsored trip to Israel. The TikTok influencer was one of 12 South Africans invited to explore Tel Aviv and Jerusalem.

The controversy arose out of public support for Gaza, and South Africa’slandmark case at the International Court of Justice (ICJ) accusing Israel of committing acts of genocide against Palestinians.

INFLUENCER NOT SORRY OVER ISRAEL TRIP

In the first week of November, Roseanne Pillay joined a group of 12 South African content creators who were invited to explore Israel on an all-expenses-paid trip.



The Chatsworth-born woman stated that she was approached by an organisation, which she did not wish to name, to create content during their time in Tel Aviv, Jerusalem and the Dead Sea.

The 47-year-old grabbed the opportunity with both hands, stating that it had been a “lifelong dream” as a Christian to “walk on the land where Jesus walked”.

However, the popular TikToker, known as “Roseyma” was inundated with backlash from followers who accused her of supporting the “gnocide” country.



On her accounts, Roseanne has clapped back at her critics and defended her decision to accept the sponsored vacation.

She told Sunday Tribune that she was unaware of the conflict between Israel and Gaza.

She said: “I am being honest when I say I did not know the history between Israel and Palestine. I had too many issues in my own life and was trying to survive to put food on the table. It may sound insensitive, but I am just trying to survive.



“I did not even research the country; I only checked on the weather so I knew what clothes to pack”.

Roseanne added that while she has since become aware of the extent of the backlash, she used her own personal hardships to relate.

She continued: “I know people are suffering, but I suffered as well as a child. I stood outside people’s doors asking for food. People eventually got fed up and told me to leave. So do not think I do not care about people. I just had my own struggles to deal with.



“People started speaking about genocide and, to be honest, I did not even know what the word meant. It was not my fault that I could not finish school. I was worried about surviving.”

‘I AM TRULY SORRY’

While “Roseyma” did not apologise outright for accepting the sponsored trip to a country many of her followers described as promoting “Apartheid”, another TikToker, Andile Ngidi, known as Space Andza, has published a written apology for being part of the group that travelled to Israel.

Andile cut short his week in the country and returned to South Africa amid the social media backlash.



He shared: “I have seen and noted all the concerns, critiques, and disappointment surrounding my trip to Israel. I have come to understand the hurt and disappointment my presence here during this painful time has caused to many of you. I am truly sorry.”

While he claimed his Christian faith was his biggest motivation for accepting the invitation, he confessed that he had not properly researched the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

He added: “As a young queer man from a disadvantaged background, opportunities like this do not come often.
