World.title: Microsoft Global Outage Disrupts Outlook, Teams and Health Services Worldwide
World.content:
Microsoft’s global outage ran into a second day Friday. Outlook email is still failing for many users, and parts of Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 tools only partly work. If your work or school email runs through Microsoft, this is what’s happening and what you can do.

The problems began late Thursday morning, Costa Rica time, when Microsoft opened an incident for users who couldn’t reach their Exchange Online mailboxes. At first the company said the problem was concentrated in the Americas. It later confirmed that users in any region could lose their connection to Microsoft 365.

Downdetector, which tracks outages, logged problems in 74 countries and territories. At Thursday’s peak it had more than 130,000 reports about Outlook alone, most of them from the United States. On Friday morning Microsoft said traffic was gradually coming back. The biggest improvements were in North America, with steady progress in much of Europe. The company still hasn’t said when everything will be fully restored.

Microsoft says Teams messaging, calls and meetings are mostly working. Teams calendars, meeting invitations and scheduling are still affected because they rely on the same email system. Some Outlook users still can’t sign in, and many messages are arriving hours late. Copilot users may get errors when they load a chat or ask for an answer. Planner, To Do and some SharePoint sharing features have also had problems.

Microsoft hasn’t named a root cause. It first blamed heavy load on part of its infrastructure in several regions. Later it said many servers had unexpectedly gone offline, which pushed their traffic onto the machines still running. Engineers stopped all deployments, moved traffic away from the affected systems and restarted servers. They’re also reviewing recent network configuration changes. Some servers brought back overnight failed again once traffic returned, and Microsoft said its early fixes had only marginal success.

Microsoft said it isn’t aware of any malicious activity. Executive vice president Charles Lamanna said the outage doesn’t appear to be a cyberattack. Many Costa Ricans remember the 2022 ransomware attacks that took down Finance Ministry systems and the Social Security System (CCSS). This is different: people can’t get into their accounts, but nothing Microsoft has said suggests customer data was exposed.

Health services abroad have been hit hard. In the United Kingdom, the National Health Service rescheduled some procedures after Teams went down, because it’s a key link between managers and health workers. The NHS also warned that some patients may struggle to get prescriptions, since pharmacies can’t reach doctors’ offices by email.

A UK union, the GMB, said ambulance services and medical centers saw a serious impact, although urgent care appeared unaffected. Japanese economy minister Ryosei Akazawa warned the impact was significant. New Zealand’s foreign ministry had trouble receiving email at its embassies and consulates.

In Australia, schools, courts and government offices began Friday without Outlook. The Euronext stock exchange told listed companies to use the phone, and Workhorse Group, a US company, postponed its quarterly results. No count of affected users in Costa Rica has been published, and no national institution has announced disruptions so far.

Still, Microsoft 365 is part of daily public life here. The Ministry of Public Education gives public school students and teachers institutional email and Microsoft Teams accounts. The Judiciary has made Teams its official platform for virtual hearings. If your email is down, check Microsoft’s official service page at status.cloud.microsoft before you assume the problem is on your end. Resetting your password or reinstalling Outlook won’t fix this.

A message that hasn’t arrived isn’t necessarily lost. Microsoft extended its delivery window to 48 hours, so delayed email is held and delivered instead of bounced back. If you’ve sent anything urgent since Thursday, call or use another channel to make sure it arrived. For urgent coordination, use Teams chat and calls, which mostly work. Double-check meeting times, though, because calendars may be out of sync.

Watch for scama since outages bring a wave of fake “support” emails and texts asking you to log in or reset your password. Don’t click links in those messages. Go to the status page directly. Microsoft said it will keep posting updates on its service status page until everything is restored. It’s the latest of several large cloud outages this year, and it shows how much work, school and public services depend on a few technology providers.

World.title: Costa Rica Moves to Dock Pay for Education Workers Who Joined Strike
World.content:
Costa Rica’s government is moving to dock a day’s pay from education workers who joined Wednesday’s march against cuts to public education, after the Ministry of Public Education (MEP) counted 36,994 staff absent from work. The figure, released by the ministry on Thursday, represents more than a third of the MEP payroll. The ministry said 175 school dining halls did not open and some 800 schools reported problems with cleaning or security during the protest.

President Laura Fernández declared the strike illegal at her weekly press conference on Wednesday. She said the government would deduct the day’s wages from those she described as vagabonds who had gone out to demand things that do not exist, and she called union leaders leeches.

Education Minister Leonardo Sánchez said the ministry had already coordinated with the Attorney General’s Office to ask a Labor Court to declare the strike illegal. The MEP sent its report to the Attorney General’s Office on Wednesday night, and a Labor Court will decide whether the walkout was lawful.

Costa Rican labor rules treat the loss of pay for days not worked separately from disciplinary sanctions. Sanctions require a court ruling that a strike was illegal. Thousands of teachers, university students and union members marched through downtown San José on Nov. 11 to demand more money for public education. Their demands included payment of seniority bonuses and pending salary increases, settlement of the state’s debt to the teachers’ pension board, known as Jupema, and changes to the transition to a single global salary scheme.

Marchers also rejected the proposed 2027 education budget, which equals 4.9% of gross domestic product. The Constitution sets 8% of GDP as the target for public education spending. The 2027 national budget includes a cut of 19.23 billion colones, about $42.9 million, to the MEP. Public universities joined the march to protest reductions to funds the government had agreed to return to them after the pandemic.

Sánchez rejected the unions’ arguments, saying the government had met and exceeded the agreements it reached two years ago. He pointed to an increase in the sector’s budget during a period of deflation and falling enrollment, without comparing that figure with GDP. The minister also criticized union proposals to raise the MEP budget from 2.8 trillion colones, about $6.2 billion, to nearly 5.8 trillion colones, about $12.9 billion. Fernández said she had held two working meetings with education union leaders during her first six months in office.

The National Association of Educators (ANDE) sent a statement on Thursday to Fernández and Sánchez objecting to the pay deduction and asked the president for a public apology. The Association of Secondary School Teachers (APSE), whose president is Dennis Solís Cruz, defended teachers’ participation and said that taking to the streets is a way to defend labor rights and public education.

The unions maintain that the strike was legal. Many teachers also responded on social media, posting messages about the demands of their work and rejecting the president’s description of them. The dispute comes as the 2027 national budget remains on hold. The Constitutional Chamber has barred lawmakers from holding the final vote on the spending plan before Nov. 29 while it reviews challenges tied to funding for the Judiciary and public universities.

The Labor Court will now decide whether the government can treat the walkout as illegal. The budget vote at the end of the month will set how much money public schools and universities receive in 2027.

World.title: National Police Leadership workshop strengthens youth diversion efforts
World.content:
National Police Leadership workshop strengthens youth diversion efforts

The Ministry of Human Development, Family Support and Gender Affairs, through its Community Rehabilitation Department (CRD), in collaboration with the Belize Police Department (BPD) and with support from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) through the European Union-funded PACE Justice Project, today hosted the National Police Leadership Diversion Workshop at Hidden Hall by Oasis in Belmopan.

The workshop brought together senior police officers, including the Commissioner of Police, Superintendents, and Officers Commanding various police formations, to strengthen their understanding of youth diversion and its application at the police station level.

Youth diversion allows eligible young people under the age of 18 who come into conflict with the law to be referred to the Community Rehabilitation Department for structured rehabilitation and support programmes instead of being formally charged. These programmes, typically lasting three to six months, may include counselling, life skills development, mentorship, and referrals to community-based organizations, depending on the young person’s needs and the nature of the offence.

The workshop featured welcome remarks by Mrs. Ganesha Smith, Acting Director of CRD; special remarks by Mr. Michael Lund, UNDP Deputy Resident Representative; and a keynote address by Commissioner of Police Dr. Richard Rosado.

Facilitated by Attorney-at-Law Diana Shaw, the workshop examined the legal framework for diversion, institutional responsibilities, and proposed updates to police and court diversion protocols. Participants also engaged in discussions and group activities to review and validate procedures aimed at strengthening the consistent application of diversion.

The workshop forms part of the ongoing Police Diversion Training Campaign under the National Diversion Program and follows consultations on the 2026 Revised National Diversion Protocol. The initiative seeks to strengthen coordination between the CRD and the Belize Police Department while reinforcing the important role of police leadership in ensuring that eligible young people are appropriately considered for diversion.

Youth diversion is not about removing accountability. It is about providing young people with the guidance, support, and opportunity to learn from their mistakes and make better choices.

Through continued collaboration with the Belize Police Department and development partners, the Ministry remains committed to strengthening a child-centered justice system that prioritizes rehabilitation, accountability, and second chances.

World.title: EntreCon 2026 brings entrepreneurs together in Belize City
World.content:
EntreCon 2026 brings entrepreneurs together in Belize City

By Zoila Palma: Small business owners and entrepreneurs from across Belize have gathered at the Biltmore Plaza Hotel in Belize City for the 2026 National Entrepreneurship Convention (Belize EntreCon), hosted by BELTRAIDE and the Government of Belize.

Organized by SBDCBelize, a unit of BELTRAIDE, the convention aims to promote the growth and development of micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) through networking, knowledge-sharing, and business development opportunities.

Prime Minister John Briceño delivered the keynote address, sharing his own journey in business and highlighting his Government’s efforts to create an enabling environment for entrepreneurs.

Belizean businesswoman Kalila Enriquez-Reynolds, founder and CEO of Jamaica-based Money Media Limited, also shared insights into the strategies and experiences that helped grow her company from a start-up into a successful business.

World.title: International News: ALL flights grounded across U.S. following communications outage
World.content:
International News: ALL flights grounded across U.S. following communications outage

By Zoila Palma: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has issued a rare nationwide ground stop, temporarily halting all flights across the United States due to a telecommunications outage affecting aviation operations, CNN reports.

The agency said the decision was made “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,” with no immediate timeline provided for when normal operations would resume.

U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the disruption was not caused by a threat to national security and was not connected to the recent Microsoft outage. Preliminary reports also indicate that the incident was not a cyberattack. President Donald Trump has been briefed on the situation.

The ground stop has triggered delays and cancellations at major airports across the country, leaving thousands of travelers uncertain about their travel plans.

United Airlines notified passengers that all new domestic departures would be suspended while the FAA restriction remains in effect, although aircraft already in the air would be allowed to continue their flights. The airline said it would work with affected customers to get them to their destinations once the issue is resolved.

Passengers at airports including New York’s John F. Kennedy International Airport and Chicago O’Hare International Airport reported receiving limited information about the disruption. Some travelers were informed shortly before departure, while others learned about the nationwide ground stop through news reports.

Pilots and air traffic controllers also reported significant communication difficulties, with outages affecting air traffic control radar systems and radio frequencies.

Aviation officials have yet to establish the precise cause of the telecommunications failure, and authorities have warned that resolving the disruption could take time.

World.title: ‘$500 Is No Kind Of Money To Me’: Roy Earl Jones ordered to repay runman $501 and pay $1,435 in fines and court costs
World.content:
‘$500 Is No Kind Of Money To Me’: Roy Earl Jones ordered to repay runman $501 and pay $1,435 in fines and court costs

By Breaking Belize News Staff: “$500 is no kind of money to me,” Roy Earl Jones said in an interview Friday after spending a night at the Belize Central Prison. The 24-year-old Belize City man walked free after sentencing, but the senior magistrate ordered him to repay a deliveryman $501 before paying another $1,435 in fines and court costs.

Jones pleaded guilty Thursday to seven counts of obtaining property by deception and was remanded overnight pending sentencing. He apologized in court and said he needed time to get a loan to clear his debts.

On Friday, the senior magistrate fined Jones $200 on each count and added $5 per count in court costs. He has until February 26, 2027, to pay the court, with a default sentence of two months on each count if he fails to pay. The magistrate told him the deliveryman must be repaid first.

According to the facts presented in court, the deliveryman agreed to use his own money to buy items and deliver cash to Jones’ mother on the understanding that Jones would pay him back. On September 29, he said he dropped off $100 in cash, then returned later that day with a $100 bag of dog food and another $40. The next day, he said he spent $50 on cereal and condensed milk and delivered another $50 in cash.

The requests continued into October. The deliveryman said he paid $20 for fried chicken from Benny’s Restaurant on October 6 and $29 for two orders of rice and beans with pork and two Cokes the next day. When he asked Jones on October 8 when he would get his money, Jones replied on WhatsApp, “Thank you for your patience.” The deliveryman said he still dropped off another $70 that evening, followed by $22 in barbecue meals on October 10 and another $20 in chicken on October 12.

The deliveryman told police he never got his money back. After repeated attempts to collect, he made his own inquiries and learned that the man he knew as “Rayjaughn” was Roy Jones. He reported the matter to police on November 9, and officers detained Jones two days later.

In handing down the sentence, the magistrate cited the seriousness and prevalence of the offence, the financial loss and the breach of trust. She also weighed Jones’ early guilty plea, his remorse, his lack of previous convictions and the night he had already spent in custody. She noted that although the transactions took place on different days, the seven counts arose from the same course of conduct.

In Friday’s interview, Jones called the deliveryman a friend and said their agreement gave him until that day to repay the money. He said he had not expected the deliveryman to go to police.

World.title: American tourist says San Pedro vendor cursed him after he refused to buy carving
World.content:
American tourist says San Pedro vendor cursed him after he refused to buy carving

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): An American visitor to San Pedro says he and his wife were verbally abused by a street vendor on Friday after they declined to buy a wood carving.

In a social media post tagged in downtown San Pedro, the tourist said the couple was walking peacefully down the street when a man asked if they wanted to buy one of his carvings.

The visitor said he told the vendor the carvings were beautiful but that he had no cash on him. According to the post, the vendor responded with an insult laced with profanity, calling him an “American” in a derogatory way.

“I was pretty shocked because this isn’t our first time in Belize and we’ve never been treated so unkindly,” the tourist wrote.

He said he was wearing camera equipped smart glasses and told the vendor he was being recorded. At that point, he said, the man apologized, quickly packed up and left.

The visitor said he shared the post so others could be careful, but stressed that he sees it as a one off.

“I realize this was an isolated event,” he wrote.

The vendor’s side of the story is not known.

World.title: Godwin Haylock asks government to disclose Frankfurt flight guarantee, presses for sargassum plan
World.content:
Godwin Haylock asks government to disclose Frankfurt flight guarantee, presses for sargassum plan

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Queen Square Area Representative Godwin Haylock has asked the government to disclose the terms of Belize’s revenue guarantee for a new Frankfurt–Belize air service and publish a funded plan to tackle sargassum in Placencia and other coastal communities.

Speaking before the House adjourned on Thursday, Haylock welcomed the European route as a way to diversify Belize’s tourism market. He asked what the government had agreed to cover under the guarantee, including whether it would pay for empty seats. No terms of the agreement were confirmed during the exchange.

Discover Airlines is scheduled to begin twice-weekly seasonal service on December 16, 2027. The outbound flights from Frankfurt will stop in San José, Costa Rica, before continuing to Belize City. The return flights will go nonstop to Frankfurt.

Haylock also raised concerns about declining overnight arrivals in the months leading up to the high season, the effect of travel advisories on bookings and heavy sargassum that he said had left stretches of beach in Placencia unusable in September. He urged the government to prepare while the seaweed had receded.

Prime Minister John Briceño said the tourism minister had left the sitting after feeling unwell. The House was told Haylock’s questions would be forwarded to the minister for a written response.

World.title: St. Vincent and the Grenadines prime minister to visit Belize for Garifuna Settlement Day
World.content:
St. Vincent and the Grenadines prime minister to visit Belize for Garifuna Settlement Day

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Prime Minister Godwin Friday of St. Vincent and the Grenadines is expected to arrive in Belize on November 18 and take part in Garifuna Settlement Day celebrations the following day, Prime Minister John Briceño announced in the House of Representatives on Thursday.

Briceño said Friday would be accompanied by his wife and a government minister. He also said the visiting delegation was expected to experience Garifuna music and culture during the visit.

St. Vincent, known to the Garifuna as Yurumein, is their ancestral homeland. Briceño used the announcement to recognize Garifuna contributions to Belize in education, agriculture, music, food and the arts, and invited Belizeans to join the November 19 celebrations.

World.title: Belize to face UN Committee against Torture later this month
World.content:
Belize to face UN Committee against Torture later this month

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Belize’s record on preventing torture and ill treatment will be examined by a United Nations committee in Geneva this month.

The UN Committee against Torture will review Belize during its latest session, which runs from November 16 to December 4.

Belize’s public hearings are scheduled for Tuesday, November 24, and Wednesday, November 25, from 3:00pm to 6:00pm Geneva time. That is 8:00am to 11:00am in Belize.

Belize is a party to the Convention against Torture and Other Cruel, Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment. Countries that have signed on are required to undergo regular reviews of how they are putting the convention into practice.

The committee is made up of 10 independent human rights experts from around the world. It has received Belize’s country report, along with submissions from non governmental organisations and other stakeholders, and will raise a range of issues with the Belize delegation.

The hearings will be held at the Palais des Nations and broadcast live on UN Web TV.

After the review, the committee will issue its concluding observations, an independent assessment of how well Belize is meeting its obligations.

World.title: FAA grounds all flights across US amid communications problem
World.content:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has issued a nationwide ground stop, grounding all flights across the United States (US) until further notice because of what it described as extraordinary circumstances and safety concerns.

According to CNN, the FAA said a communications problem affecting Air Route Traffic Control Centres, which manage flights travelling across the country, prompted the disruption.

The cause of the problem was not immediately known. However, preliminary reports from two law enforcement officials indicated that it was not a cyberattack, CNN reported.

The nationwide ground stop is a rare occurrence. The last time such a measure was implemented was in January 2023, when a pilot notification system went down. Before that, a nationwide ground stop was issued following the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks.

World.title: CORRECTION AND APOLOGY
World.content:
On October 16 2026, the Jamaica Observer on its online edition published an article entitled “Update: Two men killed after gun battle with police in Sligoville” which contained a photograph and several allegations and statements concerning Lamond Sutherland.

The information contained in the article was published based on information received from law enforcement authorities at the time. It has since been established that Mr Lamond Sutherland was incorrectly identified, that the allegations and statements were false and that he was not in any way a party to the incident.

Jamaica Observer unreservedly retracts the article and sincerely apologises to Mr Lamond, Sutherland who is still very much alive, for any distress, embarrassment or damage to his personal and professional reputation which may have been caused by the publication.

World.title: JC’s Walker Cup ban overturned, school instead placed on probation
World.content:
Jamone Lyle (second right) and his Jamaica College teammates celebrate a goal in their Walker Cup semi-final against Mona High on Saturday, October 10, 2026. (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

Jamaica College (JC) have now been placed on a two-year probation by the Inter-Secondary Schools Sports Association (ISSA) Appeals Board for using an ineligible player during the ongoing schoolboy football season, replacing an earlier decision that would have barred the school from next year’s Walker Cup competition.

The latest ruling, announced in an ISSA press release, follows a meeting of the Appeals Board last Friday to review Jamaica College’s appeal against decisions made by the association’s Disciplinary Committee and subsequently upheld by its Executive Committee.

The Appeals Board set aside the decision that JC would not be invited to participate in the 2027 Walker Cup and instead placed the school on two years’ probation, effective November 6, 2026.

However, the board dismissed the other two aspects of the school’s appeal, leaving intact the sanctions imposed in relation to player Jamone Lyle.

The decision to forfeit all points earned from matches in which Lyle participated was upheld, as was his one-year suspension from ISSA competitions.

Under the terms of the suspension, Lyle may become eligible to participate in ISSA competitions after serving the period, provided he remains a student in good standing and has relinquished his professional status in accordance with FIFA guidelines.

Both decisions were originally taken by ISSA’s Executive Committee on October 18, 2026.

The latest ruling therefore allows Jamaica College to remain eligible for consideration for the 2027 Walker Cup, but the school will now serve another two-year probation, having just completed a previous two-year probation for another matter.

ISSA Competitions Officer Ewan Scott, who signed the release, noted that the association’s rules state that decisions of the Appeals Board are binding on all concerned.

World.title: Nine years on, CRH to open renovated A&E department
World.content:
ST JAMES, Jamaica — The newly rebuilt Accident and Emergency (A&E) Department at the Cornwall Regional Hospital (CRH) is set to be opened on Friday, nine years after the department along with the rest of the hospital was shuttered after noxious fumes made the condition untenable for staff and patients.

The project faced notable delays over the period, but the A&E department, which is currently housed at the Mount Salem Health Centre, will finally return to the main building.

It has been described as at least twice the size of the previous area and will include operating theatres to make it one of the most modern A&Es in Jamaica.

It follows the opening of the Administration department at the CRH building in April 2025.

World.title: WATCH: ‘No hit in 20 years!’ McKenzie takes aim at Beenie Man
World.content:
West Kingston Member of Parliament Desmond McKenzie has declared that Beenie Man’s Weh di money deh? that was released as a single earlier this month will not sell.

“You have a certain deejay, for the last 20 years him can’t make a number one hit song, and all of a sudden … left the shores of Jamaica and gone out deh and talk about ‘Weh di money deh’,” McKenzie said.

“Dat deh record nah sell at all, nobody nah buy it,” added McKenzie who is also Deputy Leader of the governing Jamaica Labour Party (JLP).

He was speaking Thursday night at the annual West Kingston Constituency Conference inside the Edward Seaga Auditorium at the Tivoli Gardens High School.

His remark is the latest salvo in a dispute that erupted in October when Beenie Man, during an interview with British broadcaster ITV News, questioned how millions of dollars in donations to the Jamaican Government intended for Hurricane Melissa victims was distributed.

READ: ‘You don’t see where the money go’: Beenie Man criticises Gov’t hurricane relief spending

“This is nothing new that the Government get the money, the Government distribute the money the wrong way. The people who supposed to get the money haven’t been getting any,” Beenie Man claimed.

His remarks have met with pushback from members of the Government including Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness. But, when it was thought that the matter was settled, Beenie Man released Weh di money deh? And McKenzie ripped into him Thursday night.

Suggesting that Beenie Man was seeking relevance, he said, “Yuh have a certain DJ, fi di last 20 years him caw mek a number one hit song. And all of a sudden, him caw mek it locally caw him nah say nutten. [So] him lef di shores of Jamaica an gone out deh go talk about ‘weh di money deh…government hold on pon di money”.

The deputy leader of the JLP told the conference that, “We’re at a point in the country’s history where what matters more is substance than fluff. And what we have is a government of performance”.

He admitted that like any other government, the Holness-led Administration would have got some things wrong. “We would not be the only government in the world that makes mistakes but we admit to our faults and we do what is necessary to correct our mistakes,” he said.

-Lynford Simpson

World.title: Toll rebels being barred
World.content:
The Caymanas toll plaza where motorists enter and exit the Edward Seaga Highway. (Photo: Jamaica North South Highway Company Limited)

Unruly motorists have pushed the operators of the Edward Seaga Highway (or T3 leg of Highway 2000) to develop a blacklist system that flags vehicles linked to toll road violations and restrict them from accessing the motorway.

According to the Jamaica North South Highway Company Limited (JNSHCL), developer and operator of the 66.13-kilometre road which has six toll plazas and one local head office operating on a 24/7 basis, the violations include tailgating through the barrier, forcing the barrier, and stealing or swapping toll cards to avoid payment. Verbal abuse or violent threats against staff will also result in blacklisting. Blacklisted vehicles are prohibited from entering the highway and once identified will be turned away.

According to the operators, those responsible will bear full legal responsibility under applicable law for any resulting harm, disruption or consequences to the highway and the travelling public.

Trudy-Ann Williams, deputy commercial and compliance manager for the JNSHCL, told the

Jamaica Observer that a pilot of the feature was conducted last month and full roll-out is slated for the end of this month.

“We had security on the ground, personnel from the Jamaica Constabulary who were willing to assist us once we were able to identify these motorists, to escort them from the toll lane

— if it is that they became boisterous

— or just simply to provide further information to them about the reason they were placed on the blacklist,” Williams told the Observer.

She said the operators have developed a working list based on past violations committed by operators of private and public passenger vehicles.

“The numbers fluctuate. Right now I think we have over 50 licence plates; it’s not an extensive list and the list is updated as time goes by, as we do more research, so the list will change if a motorist comes forward and clears themselves; they will be removed and the list updated,” she told the Observer.

Williams said an individual who, for example, was blacklisted because they did not pay the toll can clear themselves by coming forward to pay the relevant sum.

Explaining how the debarring feature works, Williams said, “Once a motorist who is on the blacklist approaches the toll lane, their licence plate will be detected by our new QR code system and an alert will go off, meaning an alarm, and they will be barred and not allowed to enter the highway. Once they are discovered we will alert the motorist that they are on the blacklist and that they should remove themselves from the toll lane,” Williams said.

“There is a flashing light, there is an alarm and the barrier will not open,” she said, adding that motorists who wish to be clear about their status can contact JNSHCL through its general office or customer service lines (1-876-803-5075 or 1-888-429-5674), respectively.

“We also will make a list available through our website where they can search to confirm whether or not they are on the blacklist. However, their full details will not be available on the website because we do not want to disclose sensitive details to just about anyone who has access, so they will still have to call to clarify the reason they are blacklisted,” Williams outlined.

She also emphasised that individuals who are involved in altercations with toll booth staff are only blacklisted after thorough investigations.

“There are different reasons why motorists might become blacklisted; it might not only be for toll evasion, even through toll evasion is the number one reason. If we have persons who have violated or abused the toll in any way, including being overly rude or violent toward our staff, they can also be placed on the blacklist. There are not a lot of those persons; however, we would just like persons to bear in mind that we are non-tolerant of our staff members being abused in any way,” she pointed out.

“If it is that someone thinks it was unfair of us to have blacklisted them for that reason, we would have ensured that we did our due diligence before adding them to that list, which includes gathering relevant evidence… for any of those violations. We have evidence, and that is how we determine if the vehicle will be blacklisted. We are not taking it lightly or trying to just build a list on a whim; it is all evidence-based,” Williams said.

In the meantime, she said in addition to the blacklist feature, the JNSHCL is introducing a new way to access the toll road via the QR code or cardless system, effectively phasing out the use of toll cards.

“Persons will be able to access the toll road without taking a toll card and, instead, will use their cellphone to scan a QR code. The cellphone, if it has data or even if it doesn’t have data, we will provide free Wi-Fi at our toll plazas; they can connect or use their data, scan the QR code app or feature on their phone, and that will generate a journey code. Once that information is captured, then they are allowed access to the motorway and then when they get to the exit the information, in most cases, will automatically populate. If it is, that it is not automatically populated, then they can show the QR code on their phone or scan another at the exit. The payment is normal, you can pay via cash or debit card,” Williams explained.

“For persons who are not so familiar or tech-savvy, we are trying to ensure that we do some more public education campaigns. We will have persons at the entrance who can show them how to access the feature and to give further instructions. We will ensure that this happens for a period of at least 10 days once the feature has been launched,” she assured.

Toll evasion in Jamaica is a criminal offence under the Toll Roads Act, resulting in fines up to $10,000 or 30 days’ imprisonment per count for non-payment. Authorities, including TransJamaican Highway

— concessionaires for the tolled motorway running between Portmore and Kingston, and Kingston and Manchester

— use surveillance and police enforcement to target offenders, especially those tailgating or using stolen tags, which can lead to higher penalties.

World.title: Bell in hot water
World.content:
BELL... the Integrity Commission found that he attended deliberations on his wife’s application to the municipal corporation without withdrawing or recusing himself from the Commercial Services Committee

Councillor Ian Bell (People’s National Party, Beecher Town Division) is facing a two-month expulsion from the St Ann Municipal Corporation, removal from two key committees, and a formal reprimand following an Integrity Commission investigation which found that he failed to withdraw from discussions concerning his wife’s application for space at the Ocho Rios Transportation Centre.

St Ann’s Bay Mayor Michael Belnavis announced the proposed disciplinary measures during Thursday’s monthly council meeting, saying a notice of motion for Bell’s expulsion would be brought before the council later that day.

Belnavis said the corporation would also seek Bell’s immediate removal from the Commercial Services Committee, which considers applications and matters relating to the corporation’s commercial activities, and the Planning Committee.

According to the mayor, the proposed two-month expulsion is being pursued under section 44(1) of the Local Governance Act, 2016, on the grounds that Bell brought the corporation into disrepute.

The measures follow an investigation into the circumstances surrounding an application made by Bell’s wife, businesswoman Shirlyn Campbell-Bell, to rent a section of the transportation centre to operate a gaming lounge.

The Integrity Commission found that Bell, who was a member of the Commercial Services Committee, attended deliberations on his wife’s application without withdrawing or recusing himself. The commission said this breached the conflict-of-interest standards expected of elected officials under the Ministry of Local Government and Community Development’s Councillor’s Handbook.

The Integrity Commission recommended that Bell be formally reprimanded for failing to withdraw from the committee’s consideration of the application, despite his personal interest in the matter and his knowledge of the proper procedure.

“The purpose is to protect the integrity of the committee and ensure that its membership can carry out its responsibilities without any unresolved concern regarding this matter. In addition, mandatory refresher training will be required for all members of council. That training must strengthen members’ understanding of the conflicts of interest, disclosure, recusal, ethnic decision-making, statutory obligations and good governance,” Belnavis announced on Thursday.

“We must ensure that members understand not only the procedures but their personal responsibility to uphold them. We cannot allow uncertainty, silence or conflicting interpretations of procedures to compromise the work of this corporation,” he added.

He also noted that the corporation will introduce stricter procedures requiring councillors to formally declare conflicts of interest, with every departure from and return to committee meetings duly recorded in the minutes.

“Conflicts must be declared in writing. Every withdrawal and return must be recorded in the minutes. The clerk to the committee must provide guidance whenever conflict arises and the presiding chair must confirm that the matter can properly proceed before discussion or decision-making begins,” he said.

The Integrity Commission report traced the matter to March 31, 2023, when Campbell-Bell applied to rent space at the transportation centre to place a 40-foot container for a gaming lounge.

The investigation found that the application was delivered to the corporation by Bell rather than being submitted through its Registry Department, as required under the established procedure. It also found that Campbell-Bell’s married name was omitted from the application.

Although the corporation sent her correspondence in May 2023 indicating that the request had been approved, the commission found that the required approval process had not been completed.

The report also found that the structure was built without the necessary building and planning permits, in breach of the Building Act, 2018. It said there was no evidence of a lease agreement between Campbell-Bell and the corporation, or that the application had been referred to the Ministry of Local Government for the minister’s approval.

The commission further found that the gaming lounge had operated since 2023 without paying user fees to the corporation, and that the corporation had made no attempt to collect those fees.

The investigation also examined whether Bell had declared his relationship with the applicant. While six councillors told investigators that he had disclosed that Campbell-Bell was his wife, they could not identify the specific meeting at which this was done. The commission said it was therefore unable to definitively conclude that he had made the declaration.

However, it found that Bell remained present when the application was considered and that the evidence suggested he did not recuse himself from the meeting.

Belnavis said the corporation would now examine the status of the building and take the necessary steps through the relevant legal and technical processes.

“The Integrity Commission’s report indicates that the required building plans were not submitted to the relevant agencies before construction commenced. The existence of the structure does not, in itself, constitute lawful approval,” he said.

The mayor said the corporation would also consider the requirements of section 49 of the Local Government Act, which deals with the sale or lease of land vested in a municipal corporation and requires ministerial approval.

The Integrity Commission recommended that the corporation assess and recover all outstanding fees relating to the business and enforce the relevant laws and policies concerning Campbell-Bell’s occupation of the property.

It also recommended that the corporation strengthen its conflict of interest procedures and consider disciplinary action against Bell, including a formal reprimand.

Belnavis said the measures were intended to ensure that the commission’s findings led to changes in how the corporation manages its commercial properties and conducts its affairs.

World.title: Complex Ricki’s Loving You embraces healing
World.content:
Complex Ricki.

Recording artiste Complex Ricki is encouraging listeners to embrace healing and second chances in love with her latest single, Loving You, released on November 6 through VPAL Music, the distribution arm of VP Records.

The track explores the emotional journey of moving beyond past disappointments, rediscovering one’s worth and finding the courage to pursue meaningful relationships.

For Complex Ricki, the song represents a celebration of personal growth and the possibilities that come with allowing oneself to love again.

“Loving You is about healing, embracing second chances, and finding happiness again. I want people to know that no matter what they’ve been through, they deserve genuine love,” she shared.

Through reflective lyrics, the entertainer addresses the importance of emotional maturity, commitment, and self-discovery, while highlighting the reassurance that comes with finding a relationship built on mutual understanding.

Rather than allowing previous experiences to dictate her outlook on romance, Complex Ricki uses the single to promote a renewed sense of confidence and optimism.

The song also touches on the importance of recognising one’s value and refusing to settle for relationships that do not contribute positively to personal development.

Beyond its romantic message, Loving You encourages listeners to acknowledge their individual progress and remain receptive to new experiences, even after navigating difficult circumstances.

The release adds to Complex Ricki’s growing musical catalogue as she continues to use relatable themes and personal experiences to connect with audiences.

With Loving You, the singer hopes to resonate with individuals who have experienced heartbreak but remain hopeful about finding genuine affection and happiness.

The single is available on all major digital streaming platforms through VPAL Music.

World.title: EU deal on Ukraine talks overshadows AI-focused summit in Dublin
World.content:
Ireland, which holds the EU’s rotating presidency and hosted the informal gathering, had billed the meeting as a rare chance for a high-level discussion on how to develop artificial intelligence in accordance with European values.

But the question of how to secure peace in Ukraine — and who should negotiate on Europe’s behalf — quickly dominated discussions, as leaders sparred over the format of future peace negotiations and warned about the risks of a potential deal brokered between Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Indeed, a meeting next week between the U.S. and Russian leaders has set Europe on edge, prompting warnings about a possible Yalta-type agreement in which superpowers would decide on European security questions over the heads of countries directly concerned, reminiscent of talks toward the end of World War II that divided Europe up between the four allied powers.

UAE’s Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al-Nahyan, members of the Ukrainian and Russian delegations hold talks mediated by U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff Jared Kushner in Abu Dhabi on November 10, 2026. | Pool photo by Altaf Qadri/AFP via Getty Images

“That is why I want to make our message to the U.S. very clear: Please, no surprises!” German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said regarding the Trump-Putin meeting, scheduled to take place during an APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, on Nov. 18-19. “Continue to play on Team Europe and on the same team as Ukraine. And let’s work together for genuine peace in Ukraine.”

The question of who should represent Europe in future discussions about Ukraine and the post-conflict security order was added to the summit’s agenda at the last minute, following a request from Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni.

Earlier in the day, Merz had voiced preference for a narrower group made up of officials from Berlin, Paris and London, while Kaja Kallas, the EU’s chief diplomat, argued that she was best placed to lead discussions.

World.title: Why Europe failed to find a superhero to take on Putin
World.content:
The push to identify one representative to speak for Europe was understandable. The appeal of having a single, respected leader taking the reins is largely based on a desire to project European strength and unity — as well as an interest in making negotiations with Russia, the U.S. and Ukraine efficient and effective.

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy himself said this week he wanted Europe to identify within days who will take its place in the talks, and suggested he’d prefer it was one person (he even indicated that he had a preference, though would not reveal a name).



He didn’t get his way. Instead, leaders at a summit in Dublin on Friday, decided that the “E5” made up four big EU countries ― Germany, France, Poland and Italy ― and the U.K., plus officials from the European Commission and Council, would take the work forward as a team.

Technical discussions

The search for a top representative to fill Europe’s seat at the negotiating table at the next round of peace talks had become a political obsession in Brussels that missed at least two big points.

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy takes part in a press conference at Government Buildings in Dublin on November 11, 2026. | Paul Faith/AFP via Getty Images

The first is that the leadership level is not currently where the negotiations are at. Talks this week in Abu Dhabi were technical discussions between senior officials. The big political players like Putin and Zelenskyy were not there, never mind Trump. Russia sent a Kremlin aide to lead its team and Ukraine tasked its intelligence chief with making its case.

If these officials make progress toward a deal, leaders will no doubt want to get involved. Ultimately, it will be leaders who sign any peace agreements that follow — and there’s no limit on the number of EU presidents or prime ministers who could join such a meeting as signatories or guarantors of the final deal.

The next thing that needs to happen, according to both Ukraine and the U.S. envoys mediating the talks, is for Europe to join the discussion with Russia — at this technical level.

World.title: Le Pen offers to meet Zelenskyy in Brussels
World.content:
Marine Le Pen delivers a speech during a visit of the "Salon Made in France" at Parc des Expositions of Porte de Versailles, in Paris on November 13, 2026. | Geoffroy van der Hasselt/ AFP via Getty Images

The Ukrainian leader wants to persuade the far-right leader to continue supporting Ukraine if she becomes president of France.

PARIS — Far-right leader Marine Le Pen said she would be prepared to hold talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Brussels, in the wake of her promises to stop French financial aid to Ukraine.

Speaking on the sidelines of a trade fair in Paris, Le Pen said a meeting in Brussels would be “justified” because “the topic of Ukraine financing is rattling Europe.”

“The German chancellor is starting to threaten people, it’s starting to be an issue in Europe and it would be interesting to discuss this,” she said in a reference to Friedrich Merz’s threats to cut EU funds for countries who refuse to support Ukraine financially.

World.title: Cut off from Europe, Russia will have to rewire its Arctic gas trade
World.content:
The LNG trade “is going to look completely different,” said Malte Humpert, senior fellow and founder of the think tank Arctic Institute. The ban gives Moscow “a bigger incentive” to find another route, he said. “It’s not easy. It’s not cheap. It’s very slow,” but Russia will “figure it out.”

From black markets to new ports

An increase in black market LNG trade could be one way out. A classic shadow fleet has not been needed so far, since Yamal is not under sanctions, said Sebastian Rötters, sanctions campaigner at Urgewald.

Nor is a shadow fleet well suited to the job. They typically use old, unregistered oil tankers that can easily disguise their movements. On the other hand, there are fewer LNG carriers globally and they follow a limited number of routes, making them easier to track, said Martin Vladimirov, a senior analyst at the Center for the Study of Democracy, a think tank that follows EU sanctions policy.

Bovanenkovo gas field on the Yamal peninsula in the Arctic circle on May 21, 2019. | Alexander Nemenov/AFP via Getty Images

One possible workaround is a “virtual swap.” Russia could sell more gas to countries such as Turkey or China, which could then sell more of their own or other countries' gas to Europe. That would preserve Russia's income even as its LNG is barred from European ports, Vladimirov said.

But even if Moscow finds buyers, it still has to get the LNG to them. That means Russian ships unable to access Europe will need to rebuild their logistics chains to sail farther or transfer their cargoes to other ships elsewhere before sailing on to alternative markets.

Either way, officials are already gearing up to confront the anticipated increase in black market activity. The matter requires “more attention on the European level," said Lithuanian Energy Minister Lukas Savickas, whose government will helm the EU's six-month rotating presidency from January.

World.title: Microsoft outage renews European calls to detox from US tech
World.content:
Mensch didn't specifically address the Microsoft outage, which lasted nearly 24 hours and affected millions of users in 74 countries. Still, the shutdown of key tools like Outlook email and Teams messaging impacted plenty of the tech and government leaders gathered in Dublin to chart Europe’s AI future.

French President Emmanuel Macron closed the day with a post on X: “Our independence cannot be outsourced. It must be built here at home, in Europe,” he wrote. "When it comes to artificial intelligence, too, Europe has everything it takes to compete. We have no time to lose.”

An EU diplomat present at the leaders' talks said that "we need to pick up speed, permitting and investment to compete on the world market, to have sovereignty."

Tech sovereignty, including control over the cloud, chips and models that power AI, has been a rallying cry of the second mandate of European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, and was one of the key agenda items at Friday's gathering of the leaders of the EU's 27 member countries.

"We have outsourced too much of our digital infrastructure to actors outside the EU," Finnish European Parliament lawmaker Aura Salla said in a press release Friday following the outage. She suggested that government contracts specifically "must support European technology."

Others zoned in on the risk created by relying on digital infrastructure controlled by a couple of large companies.

World.title: Ex-Labour MP accused of sexual harassment joins Plaid Cymru
World.content:
In 2023, five women alleged that Davies, a former Commons select committee chair, subjected them to unwanted sexual attention, both physical and verbal, after coming into contact with them through his work as an MP. Davies had the whip suspended as a Labour MP immediately after the allegations were made public but remained a member of the party until 2025.

When the claims against Davies were first reported by POLITICO, he said he did not “recognize” them, adding: “If I have inadvertently caused offence to anyone, then I am naturally sorry.”

In these instances, the women had raised concerns about his behavior informally but had not complained in writing.

At least two women later filed official complaints with the Labour Party, resulting in an investigation lasting more than a year.

Davies was not eligible to stand as a candidate in the 2024 election because he was suspended, and quit the party ahead of a planned hearing on his conduct in 2025. As a result, the hearing never went ahead.

The former MP for Swansea West argued in the article published Thursday that the party engineered his removal as a candidate for factional reasons. “I was made to wait 23 weeks without any complaints. When complaints were made, they were ‘to support other women’ who had not made any complaints. None were reported to Parliament,” he said.

World.title: EU countries to announce deportation hub deal with Rwanda
World.content:
The countries previously confirmed that they aim to close the first deals to set up the off-shore centers in 2026, with plans to make them operational as of next year.

The deportation hub in Rwanda would function as a pilot project and deals with other countries and involving other EU countries are likely to follow.

A recent reform of EU rules made it possible for EU members to cut deals to set up such deportation hubs with other countries on the condition that they meet international human rights standards.

Specifics of the scheme, including the nationalities of the people that would be moved to the hubs, their living conditions there and oversight of the deal, all depend on the agreement countries cut.

But human rights groups have warned that the hubs risk opening the door to human rights abuses, far removed from EU oversight or recourse.

Plans by the Conservative British government plans to deport asylum seekers to Rwanda were slapped down by the U.K. Supreme Court in 2023, which ruled the scheme unlawful. After coming into power in 2024, the Labour government shelved the plans, with then-Prime Minister Keir Starmer calling the Rwanda plan “dead and buried.”

The U.K. had aimed to move people to Rwanda to process their applications remotely, whereas the incoming deal of the EU countries would target people who have been ordered to leave the bloc’s territory.

Seb Starcevic contributed to this report.

World.title: What Vladimir Putin won in Abu Dhabi Ukraine peace talks
World.content:
The ambitious aim apparently now agreed between Washington and Moscow is to discuss all the issues together. And then to “find a pathway to settle them all at the same time,” Jared Kushner explained to reporters in a post-talks briefing in the UAE’s capital. Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law, was representing the U.S. in the talks, along with Steve Witkoff, a real estate investor who is Trump’s special envoy to the Middle East.

So much for sequencing — generally seen by experienced diplomatic negotiators as crucial to any successful peace talks. And so much, too, for starting with a ceasefire or the tiresome breaking down of complex issues into discrete and manageable tasks to try to move things along while raising confidence and inspiring trust.

To be sure, Russia and the United States won’t be able to strike a deal on their own. Ukraine will get a say, and European leaders have already pushed back against Trump’s big, beautiful deal, rejecting any attempt by the White House and the Kremlin to reshape the continent’s security architecture.

Russia’s Foreign Affairs’ Minister Sergei Lavrov delivers a press-conference following the Collective Security Treaty Organization meeting in Moscow on November 10, 2026. | Igor Ivanko/AFP via Getty Images

But it has been a longstanding Kremlin goal to get the U.S. to agree to the “let’s talk about everything” strategy, a process that will succeed in “diverting attention from what really is the critical issue, and that’s the war on Ukraine,” said Eugene Rumer, who served on the U.S. National Intelligence Council under President Barack Obama.

Rumer told reporters in a briefing that the lack of sequencing speaks volumes and is a hallmark of Russian diplomacy which aims at “muddling any situation.”

It’s difficult to quibble with his pessimism. Russian President Vladimir Putin has a long track record of using peace talks to delay, obfuscate and exhaust opponents as he continues doing whatever he wants — all the while insisting that everything is interconnected and must be solved all at the same time.

World.title: Tanker collides with New Orleans river cruise carrying 129 passengers, rescue operation underway
World.content:
A tanker struck a New Orleans river cruise on Friday, partially submerging the boat.

 

New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno’s office said multiple people have been rescued, and search-and-rescue operations are still ongoing.

Approximately 129 passengers were aboard the riverboat American Heritage at the time of the incident, according to the Port of New Orleans.

Video from the scene showed the much larger boat operated by American Cruise Lines crashing into the paddlewheel cruise boat while it appeared to be docked.

People were seen in the river in life jackets or standing near the railing as the other side of the ship listed further into the water.

It was reported that the ship docked two hours early to begin passenger disembarkation.

Passengers are being brought inside the Port of New Orleans Administration Building, Port NOLA said.

Authorities did not immediately release whether there were injuries or deaths.

Our journalists are working to bring the latest on the story.

World.title: EU leaders bring Italy and Poland into Ukraine peace talks team as Kallas fights for spot
World.content:
European Union leaders have agreed on a joint team to represent Europe in the ongoing negotiations to end Russia's war on Ukraine, comprising France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the United Kingdom.

 

The UK is not an EU member but belongs to the E3 group.

The European Council, European Commission and NATO will also be represented.

The decision was taken on Friday at an informal summit in Dublin, Ireland, where the possibility of appointing a special envoy dominated discussions. Ukraine, the United States and even Russia had called on the EU to appoint a single representative.

Ahead of the meeting, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni had criticised the "disarray" of voices in the peace process and called for a single European envoy.

Instead, EU leaders opted to expand the existing negotiating group, adding Italy and Poland. Warsaw had pointedly warned against Western European countries making decisions on behalf of the East.

"We are fully engaged in supporting the ongoing process, and we hope it will deliver concrete results," European Council President António Costa said.

"The leaders agreed that our European team for the negotiations on peace in Ukraine is the European Union institutions and the E5 of the Coalition of the Willing."

The decision leaves EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas without the special envoy role she had publicly sought, as the diplomatic process increasingly sidelines her.

On Friday morning, Kallas made a forceful case for taking on the role, arguing that representing the bloc on foreign policy was part of her mandate.

"In June 2024, there was a decision by the leaders (on) who is representing (the EU) when it comes to security and foreign policy. And it was the discussion that in these five years there is going to be a negotiation with the Russians," she said.

"If the leaders want to change that agreement, of course, they may, because it is the leaders' decision, but I think we should focus our energy actually on the substance."

Kallas acknowledged that "Russians do not want me" because of her "strong" views.

Asked about her remarks, Costa appeared to dismiss her claim, pointing to the EU treaties.

"The treaties are very clear. The president of the European Council represents the European Council and represents the Union when it comes to the common foreign and security policy at the level of head of state and head of government," he said.

"The president of the European Commission represents the Commission, and the Commission represents externally the Union in community issues."

However, the negotiations have yet to reach the level of heads of state and government, taking place so far among national security advisers and senior officials.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen also declined to back Kallas, despite her serving as a vice-president in the Commission.

"We decide on who represents us, and that's what we've done today, and how we are being represented to 27 sovereign countries plus the EU institutions," she said.

"We have taken our decision."

Friday's agreement largely formalises the negotiating format shaped by the United States, which is brokering the talks. The E3, EU institutions and NATO were represented at recent rounds of peace negotiations in Miami, Oslo, Brussels and Abu Dhabi.

Italy took part in the Abu Dhabi meeting. Poland is expected to join the next round.

"The E3 format has proven very effective. Incidentally, we always include Italy and Poland," German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said in Dublin, signalling that Berlin was not prepared to give up its seat in favour of a single envoy.

"In that regard, I don't see any need to have an institutional debate at the moment."

The key question now is whether Russia will agree to negotiate directly with European representatives, having repeatedly refused to sit at the same table as them.

US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner travelled to Moscow on Thursday to persuade Russian President Vladimir Putin to engage. After the meeting, both said Moscow had indicated it was willing to hold face-to-face talks with Europeans.

But the Kremlin played it down, casting uncertainty over whether such a meeting will take place.

World.title: Russia sends major business delegation to Kabul for business talks with the Taliban
World.content:
Russian deputy prime minister Alexei Overchuk was welcomed by a guard of honour when he arrived in Kabul on Thursday with a delegation of 70 Russian business people to conduct business talks with the Taliban government, Afghan officials said.

 

Overchuk met Taliban prime minister Mohammad Hassan Akhund, the deputy prime minister for economic affairs Abdul Ghani Baradar as well as foreign minister Amir Khan Muttaqi.

According to a statement by the Afghan government published on X, Abdul Ghani Baradar described to the Russians Afghanistan's potential for economic development and investment, pointing to "strategic location, abundant resources and a workforce of 24 million people".

Abdul Ghani Baradar invited Russian companies to invest in agriculture, mining, constructions of roads, railways and factories, and to create a special economic zone in Afghanistan, while expressing his wish to expand exports of Afghan agricultural products to Russia.

The deputy prime minister also asked Russia to "provide the necessary facilities for Afghan products to be supplied to Russian markets and to cooperate in reducing transport and transit costs".

A Russian news agency quoted Alexei Overchuk as saying that the Russian delegation represent companies that are already operating in Afghanistan and that "many others want to start operating in this country."

Overchuk said that the companies represented in the delegation work in the fields of transport, logistics, agriculture and pharmaceuticals and that the Afghan government is interested in Russian chemical fertilisers, as well as in "building fertiliser production plants on Afghan soil".

Overchuk estimated that trade between Russia and Afghanistan in the first eight months of 2026 had more than doubled, reaching over 349 million dollars.

Russia officially recognised the Taliban government in July 2025, being the only state to have taken such a step since the Taliban seized power in August 2021, after the withdrawal of the United States.

Although no country other than Russia has formally recognised the new Afghan regime, the Taliban authorities have so far held high-level talks with many states and have established specific diplomatic and economic relations with some governments.

World.title: France and Germany near deal on De Cos for ECB top job as EU confirms two candidates
World.content:
Two candidates have been put forward to replace Christine Lagarde at the helm of the European Central Bank, an EU official said on Friday, as EU leaders gathered in Dublin for an informal summit.

 

Spanish daily El País also reported that France and Germany were finalising a deal on the central bank's top jobs, with Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos as the favourite to become the next president.

The official did not name the two candidates, but as Euronews previously reported, the contenders are Pablo Hernández de Cos and former Dutch central bank chief Klaas Knot.

The Eurogroup confirmed both nominations last week.

European Council President António Costa updated leaders on Friday morning and aims to begin consulting the European Parliament and the ECB's Governing Council at the EU summit on 26 November, the official said.

A new deadline of 18 November has been set for nominations to fill the other two vacancies on the central bank’s six-member Executive Board, which runs the ECB day to day. The posts are chief economist and head of market operations, both significant roles in the leadership.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and French President Emmanuel Macron are currently in "intensive" talks to negotiate the candidates.

In Dublin, Merz told reporters that agreements were in sight but not yet final, and that he needed a few more days to consult his coalition partners before presenting Germany's proposal next week.

Who gets what

France leans towards Hernández de Cos, a former Bank of Spain governor whose more moderate stance on monetary policy suits a country under fiscal strain, El País reported.

He would be the first Spanish economist to lead the ECB.

Spain's Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo told Euronews on Monday that Hernández de Cos' expertise and ability to build consensus made him an ideal candidate.

The proposed deal would give Berlin the chief economist post and Paris the seat of Germany's Isabel Schnabel, who is in charge of market operations, German business daily Handelsblatt reported.

Merz's office wants Princeton University economist Markus Brunnermeier for the role, which is seen as the ECB's second most important job, the newspaper reported.

Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz speaks during a press conference at the EU Summit in Dublin, 13 November 2026 AP Photo/Virginia Mayo

He would be the first German chief economist since Jürgen Stark left at the end of 2011, replacing Ireland's Philip Lane, whose term ends in May.

If Knot won the presidency instead, France would take the chief economist post and Germany would keep the market operations portfolio, Handelsblatt added.

Either way, a Franco-German deal would probably mean both posts would go to the eurozone's two biggest economies.

A German government spokesperson said Berlin wanted "adequate" representation in the ECB's leadership and expected a deal by the end of the year.

A vacancy in Basel

Picking Hernández de Cos would also free up the top job at the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), where he has been general manager since 1 July 2025.

Owned by central banks around the world and based in Basel, Switzerland, the BIS is often called the "central bank of central banks".

His departure would create another senior vacancy, and the BIS Board of Directors would choose his successor.

With Schnabel due to leave the ECB on 3 January for a role at the IMF, three of the Executive Board’s six members are due to leave in less than five months.

Governments are therefore negotiating the posts as a package.

World.title: Iran MPs debate possible shift in nuclear doctrine and exit from NPT
World.content:
Iran’s nuclear doctrine is generating a heated debate in the Islamic Republic’s parliament and power circles as the United States and Israel designated Iran’s capability to develop a nuclear weapon as the primary objective of their war on Iran.

 

Kamran Ghazanfari, a member of Iran's parliament, told Euronews on Friday that building nuclear weapons is far more essential for Iran that neutralising what he called “"US and Israeli propaganda against the Islamic Republic."

"When America and the Zionist regime have repeatedly threatened us with the use of nuclear weapons, we cannot be indifferent to this issue, as it is a threat that targets all the people of Iran and our very existence,” Ghazanfari said, adding that “they are enemies and have shown that they will not refrain from any crime so we cannot say 'God willing they will not use nuclear weapons against us'. We must confront them,” the Iranian lawmaker said.

He called on Iran’s leadership that “we must review the nuclear doctrine of the Islamic Republic so that the enemy knows that if it seeks a nuclear attack on Iran, it will face a reciprocal response from Iran,” adding that “just as since the Second World War until now none of the countries that possess nuclear weapons have used these weapons against each other because they fear that the other side will carry out such an attack against them, the Islamic Republic must also create deterrent power."

Ghazanfari does not see the lack of nuclear submarines and bombers capable of carrying nuclear weapons as undermining the Islamic Republic's nuclear deterrence, stating that missiles are also a solution to carry nuclear warheads.

But a former Iranian lawmaker, Heshmatollah Falahatpisheh, told Euronews that even if Iran had several nuclear warheads it would still lack nuclear deterrence, stating that "I find it unlikely that nuclear deterrence is part of our country's strategy because nuclear deterrence has three components: having an atomic bomb, a deterrent nuclear balance, and the ability to deliver the final blow. Those who think nuclear deterrence is created simply by having an atomic bomb are mistaken."

In a telephone call with Euronews, he said that "I really do not know whether the country has an atomic bomb or not, but, as far as I was aware, Iran's nuclear programme was peaceful, and even its possible military dimensions were closed by the JCPOA so that Iran's case would be removed from Chapter Seven of the UN Charter.”

“In my view Iran's military strategy is a conventional strategy, and this strategy has been fairly effective. I also find it unlikely that what Iran’s Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei meant when he said that Iran has certain things was an atomic bomb," Falahatpisheh said.

Kamran Ghazanfari, however, believes that when the secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council says that "we have something", he is referring not to an ordinary weapon but to a "special weapon".

He said that Iran is trying to formally withdraw from the Treaty of the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT), the landmark international treaty whose objective is to prevent the spread of nuclear weapons and weapons technology.

"I infer that this change of doctrine has in practice already happened. In parliament we are also pursuing withdrawal from the NPT, and last year some members of the presiding board of parliament blocked it, but MPs are still pressing for this plan to be put on the open floor, although a series of obstruction efforts are still preventing the plan from reaching the floor, Ghazanfari said.

But Heshmatollah Falahatpisheh considers the withdrawal from the NPT to be laying the groundwork for future wars against Iran, stating that "Iran's relations with the NPT have in practice been destroyed and whether Iran remains in the NPT or not depends on the nature of relations between Iran and America.”

“The discussion of Iran leaving the NPT does not help Iran's national interests because leaving the NPT amounts to hiding part of Iran's nuclear programme,” Falahatpisheh told Euronews, adding that Iran’s “Supreme National Security Council has not agreed to the MPs' triple-urgency bill to withdraw from the NPT, otherwise this plan would have been put before an open session of parliament."

Meanwhile on Thursday, Iran’s Assembly of Experts also called for examining the issue of Iran's withdrawal from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.

In a statement, the assembly, whose main task is oversight of the performance of the leadership, said that "examining the issue of withdrawal from the NPT, reviewing the country's defence doctrine and creating the necessary deterrence has become an unavoidable necessity and has turned into a public and national demand."

Finally, in announcing Iran’s latest position on the NPT membership, Iran's Foreign Ministry stressed that the Islamic Republic still remains committed to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons.

World.title: Berlin clan boss Issa Remmo appears as 'state guest' at EU Parliament event
World.content:
Clan boss Issa Remmo from Berlin took part in a conference of imams at the European Parliament in Brussels, as first reported by the Jüdische Allgemeine. The fact that the head of a clan, which in Germany is associated with an apparently endless list of offences, appears in Brussels as a state guest is seen as a slap in the face not only to the German justice system.

 

Photos show him listening to the speeches and applauding when the discussion turns to the fight against antisemitism. Yet his extended family in the Berlin district of Neukölln is hardly a symbol of successful integration and acceptance of Germany's basic values.

Serious crimes time and again

The 58-year-old is regarded in Berlin as the head of the so-called Remmo clan. The Remmo clan is estimated to have around 500 to 1,000 members, while the core family around its head, Issa Remmo, in Berlin, comprises around 103 people.

The immediate family circle around clan boss Issa Remmo lives predominantly in Berlin-Neukölln. Not all relatives are criminals. However, part of the extended family has repeatedly come to notice for serious offences. In 2023, five young men from the Remmo clan were convicted of the spectacular jewel theft from the Green Vault in Dresden.

Imam meeting in Brussels

According to information from the newspaper "Bild", Issa Remmo took part in the anti-Islamism conference at the EU Parliament at the invitation of French EPP politician Céline Imart and imam Hassen Chalghoumi. Chalghoumi is known as an interfaith bridge-builder and a clear opponent of terror.

The topics of the meeting were the fight against Islamism and antisemitism.

According to the report, the hosts initially knew nothing about Remmo's clan background. Imart later apologised to everyone who may have been hurt by his participation.

In the group photo of the organisation ELNET (European Leadership Network), which aims to improve relations between Europe and Israel and apparently organised the meeting alongside French conservative MP Céline Ismart, Remmo is clearly visible.

Jewish, Christian and Muslim religious representatives took part in the conference.

According to the Jüdische Allgemeine, Issa Remmo spoke in Brussels with French author of Jewish faith Marek Halter about antisemitism and said: "I am not an imam, but I can say one thing: we are all brothers in this world. Let us all live together, together. Where is the problem? Love will win, and terror will lose."

According to Remmo, there should no longer be any antisemitism, and Marek Halter agreed with "Inshallah".

Clan boss Remmo overshadows the Left party's election campaign in Berlin

Issa Remmo recently made headlines for attending an election party of the party Die Linke in Berlin-Neukölln. His son Firas is said to have communicated beforehand via chat with Left Party Bundestag member Ferat Koçak.

The Left party in Berlin-Neukölln insisted that it has neither political nor personal ties to Remmo. He stated in several conversations, including in Brussels, that he was disappointed with the Left party.
