World.title: Review: No excuses to skip workout as Relive Studio offers range of fitness options
World.content:
RIYADH: Finding a fitness routine that stays interesting can be a challenge, particularly when the same workout starts to feel repetitive.

At Relive Studio in Riyadh, members can switch between mat and reformer Pilates, barre and Lagree, with each class offering a different approach.

Having tried all four, I found that each brought something different. Mat Pilates offers a more traditional floor-based practice, while reformer sessions introduce resistance through machines. Barre draws on ballet-inspired movements and strength exercises, while Lagree delivers a more demanding workout through controlled, low-impact movements. Despite enjoying the variety, Lagree is the format I have ultimately committed to.

Class sizes are kept relatively small, so participants are less likely to get lost in the crowd and instructors can give closer attention to their form and technique. This is particularly important in sessions that rely on controlled movements and precise positioning. The studio’s coaching team also includes trainers of different nationalities, each bringing their own background and experience to the classes.

Relive also has a dedicated app through which members can browse the class schedule, reserve sessions and manage their memberships, keeping bookings and account details accessible in one place.

Beyond the workout space, Relive has an in-house juice bar offering smoothies, cold-pressed juices, coffee, and matcha. Its menu features seasonal options, including a pumpkin spice protein shake available during the fall.

The studio also engages with the wider wellness and lifestyle scene through brand partnerships and pop-up events, with collaborations including Kayanee, Gold Apple and The Garage.

Relive is ideal for those interested in trying different workout styles but who do not want to visit multiple studios. And although I have gravitated towards Lagree, I still appreciate having the option to switch things up if I want to.

For more information, follow Relive on Instagram @relivestudiosa.

World.title: Man Utd name Pochettino as new manager
World.content:
London – Manchester United named Mauricio Pochettino as their new manager on Friday following the dismissal of Michael Carrick.

The club issued a statement saying the USA coach, who has extensive experience in the Premier League, would take charge from November 18 following two matches against Haiti.

“The club has reached an agreement with the US soccer federation for Mauricio and his staff to be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the US men’s national team,” United said.

“The Argentinian is renowned for his high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players.

“Pochettino has consistently performed at the highest level of football across multiple leagues.”

Pochettino, who led the United States to the last-16 of the World Cup on home soil earlier this year, has previously managed in the English top flight with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.

He has a huge job on his hands at United, who have made their worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign.

The 20-time English champions are in the relegation zone after winning just one of their 10 league matches so far.

“The opportunity to represent the USA crest was one of the greatest honours of my career,” Pochettino said in a statement released by US Soccer.

“We are so grateful to the players for their commitment, to the fans for their belief, and to the federation for always supporting our staff and creating the opportunities to impact the culture of soccer in this great country.”

US Soccer CEO and secretary general JT Batson said the 54-year-old had left a “lasting mark on US Soccer through his leadership, professionalism and commitment to our players and culture”.

United’s next game is at the home of fierce rivals Liverpool on November 22.

World.title: Iraq to close Mandali border crossing with Iran
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has announced the temporary closure of the Mandali border crossing with Iran, as Baghdad is under increased US pressure to limit trade channels with Tehran amid the continuing US-Iran dispute.

The crossing, in Iraq’s eastern Diyala region, is set to shut on Friday, November 13, for maintenance and technology improvements.

Iraq’s Border Ports Authority said that the work is meant to enhance operations ahead of the rainy season but did not say when the crossing will reopen.

The decision came after Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein announced that Washington had urged the closing of practically all border crossings with Iran, leaving just two open.

Hussein admitted that such limitations might have a considerable impact on Iraq’s economy, considering the extensive commerce between the two nations.

The statement comes after another incident involving Iranian aviation, in which Iraqi officials denied permission for an airplane carrying Iran’s national football team to land at Basra International Airport on November 10.

The plane returned to Iran, and the players continued their trek to Iraq by road.

The denial reportedly stemmed from US restrictions on Iranian airlines.

Baghdad has also increased its inspection of border operations and smuggling networks, as it faces pressure to put Iran-backed armed organizations under state control.

Groups like Kataib Hezbollah and Harakat Hezbollah al-Nujaba continue to wield considerable power in Iraq, hampering the government’s attempts to keep the nation out of the larger regional struggle.

At the same time, Iraq reopened the Sheeb border crossing with Iran in Maysan province on November 10, after many weeks of shutdown for security and technological upgrades.

The reopening reveals that Baghdad has not implemented a complete blockade of its border with Iran.

The events reflect Iraq’s increasingly strained relationship with Washington and Tehran, as the government works to bolster national security, comply with international sanctions, and safeguard its economic interests.

As the US-Iran war continues, Baghdad is under increasing pressure to display stronger control over its borders, airspace, and armed groups while preserving vital commerce with its eastern neighbor.

World.title: Spinneys opens second Iraq branch at Baghdad’s Iraq Gate Residential Complex
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Spinneys, an international grocery chain, has launched its second branch in Baghdad, increasing its presence in Iraq with a new location at the Iraq Gate Residential Complex in the Mansour area.

The 700-square-meter grocery serves inhabitants of the complex, which has around 4,800 residential homes.

The supermarket is intended to serve as a neighborhood shopping attraction, selling groceries, fresh organic produce, bakery goods, dairy, deli items, and common home necessities.

The new facility also provides grocery delivery services, enabling consumers to have their purchases delivered straight to their homes.

The launch follows Spinneys’ introduction into the Iraqi market and is part of the company’s ambition to grow its supermarket network in Baghdad and across the nation.

Spinneys opened its first Iraqi branch at Iraq Mall in Baghdad earlier in 2026. The flagship supermarket covers more than 7,000 square metres, making it considerably larger than the new residential-focused location.

Spinneys’ activities in Iraq are overseen by Gray Mackenzie Retail Lebanon (GMRL), a retail firm founded in 1996 that manages the Spinneys supermarket brand in Lebanon and has expanded into the Iraqi market.

The Iraq Gate location features a smaller residential-focused supermarket concept, intended to enable quick shopping for residents inside the development rather than operating as a huge independent retail attraction.

The launch is another step in Spinneys’ development in Iraq, as multinational supermarket operators increase their presence in Baghdad’s retail sector.

World.title: Silicon Valley insiders nervously eye Nvidia scandal fallout
World.content:
San Francisco – Hours after Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia, shocked tech insiders at a conference in San Francisco saw his departure as troubling for the business but were uncertain over how heavy the impact would be.

Many were still processing the spectacular departure of the rockstar CEO, who came to embody the global boom for AI chips but fell from grace after revelations of multiple extramarital affairs, one reportedly with a Chinese spy.

“It’s a blow to I think everything and pretty much every player in (the) space, except direct competitors,” Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi said in onstage remarks.

“The culture of the company is a lot… the personality of the CEO that is there for a long time,” Ghodsi said.

A lot now “depends on who the next CEO is,” he added.

Nvidia’s board has appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress to replace Huang on an interim basis, but it remains unclear who will take over in the long term.

Investors had begun taking a dimmer view of the company even before news of the scandal broke.

Nvidia’s shares have lost 13 percent of their value since Monday, and are down more than 26 percent over the past month.

One venture capitalist told AFP that the fallout from Huang’s infidelities was accelerating a correction that had already been underway.

– Show must go on –

Others were more sanguine about the industry’s prospects.

“We’re very sad to see Jensen go,” Asher Spector, the founder of an artificial intelligence startup called Flapping Airplanes, said onstage at the Cerebral Valley AI Summit.

“That said, Nvidia has been a great partner,” Spector said, adding: “We’re very optimistic.”

A lighthearted note came from an arcade game in the style of “Mortal Kombat”, which pitted tech CEOs like Huang, Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI’s Sam Altman and even disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes against each other.

Other major tech companies, including Microsoft, Uber and Apple, have survived and even thrived after the departure of era-defining executives.

Still, some attendees noted that Huang’s downfall might leave competing AI chip designers circling for a chance to grab a piece of Nvidia’s market share.

“It was kind of unimaginable to us that there would be a world where Nvidia wouldn’t be the biggest player a few years from now,” Robert Wachen, the co-founder of AI computing startup Etched, said.

“But now you see there’s probably a pretty big opening” for other players in the sector, Wachen said.

– Open-model guru –

Huang’s exit has particularly rattled the open software community.

The former Nvidia chief advocated for an ecosystem that includes so-called open models, which users can download and customize to varying degrees.

That differs from leading model developers like OpenAI, which makes ChatGPT, and Anthropic, which crafts Claude, both of which push for closed models.

Huang was “the leader of the pack” for open models and his departure does “create a lot of uncertainty,” Igor Babuschkin, the CEO of a startup called River AI, said.

He also led Nvidia to provide billions in financing commitments to other companies, notably a more than $100 billion data center for OpenAI, which sparked concerns about circular dealmaking and a growing tech bubble.

“Will circular deals face greater scrutiny and a reality check? Very likely,” Hivemind Capital partner Emmanuel Vallod told AFP via email.

“But does that mean the music is about to stop? I very much doubt it.”

World.title: Iraq orders only national flag at government buildings amid crackdown on militias
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi is said to have instructed ministries, government agencies, and public institutions to show only the Iraqi national flag, with other flags prohibited from flying at official sites.

The decision comes as Baghdad steps up attempts to reinforce state authority and limit the influence of armed factions, especially those with strong links to Iran.

Iran-backed militias, such as Kataib Hezbollah and Harakat Hezbollah al-Nujaba, have maintained a visible presence in Iraq, with their flags and insignia seen at public meetings, roadblocks, and other armed group sites.

The alleged limitation would highlight the contrast between Iraqi state institutions and political or military groups, stressing that government buildings should represent the nation rather than specific factions.

Since entering office in May 2026, Al-Zaidi has progressively opposed militia authority, pushing for firearms to be solely controlled by the state and warning that armed organizations who refuse to comply might face legal penalties.

The government has also taken action against alleged militia-related business interests, including the cancelation of contracts at Mosul International Airport.

The moves have heightened tensions with Kataib Hezbollah and other Iran-aligned militias who oppose Baghdad’s disarmament initiatives.

The restrictions come amid ongoing regional instability in the aftermath of the US-Iran war earlier this year, which has exposed Iraq to assaults and raised pressure on the government to prevent armed groups from pulling the nation into the fight.

For Baghdad, limiting flags at official buildings would be a symbolic step toward bolstering national sovereignty. The greater question is whether the administration can transform such efforts into effective control of armed groups and their weaponry.

World.title: Iraq offers condolences to UAE after Fujairah road accident kills 14
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has sent its condolences to the United Arab Emirates after a tragic traffic accident in Fujairah that killed 14 people and wounded 30 others.

Iraq’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs released a statement on November 12 expressing sorrow to the UAE government, its people, and the families of those killed, confirming Baghdad’s support for the nation in the aftermath of the tragedy.

According to the UAE’s Emirates News Agency (WAM), the accident happened soon before midnight on November 11 on Sheik Khalifa bin Zayed Road, near Fujairah’s entrance.

Fujairah Police reported that a truck driver lost control and struck another car before flipping and colliding with many automobiles stuck in sluggish traffic.

A fire then broke out, spreading to surrounding automobiles.

According to UAE media outlets, the collision included 23 cars, five of which were trucks, and was one of the country’s bloodiest in recent years.

Emergency responders, including police, ambulance personnel, and Civil Defense teams, were sent to put out the fire, rescue casualties, and take the wounded to hospitals.

Fujairah Police stated that 15 wounded individuals had been released from the hospital, while another 15 were still receiving medical attention.

Authorities reportedly indicated that the dead were Emirati and international nationals, with DNA tests underway to identify some of those slain.

World.title: Microsoft battling to fix global Outlook outage
World.content:
Washington – Microsoft said on Thursday that efforts to repair a major outage of Outlook were not going as expected and the firm was seeking alternative solutions as users around the world were left without its crucial services.

The hours-long disruption, which Microsoft attributed to “elevated load” on its infrastructure, has hit email as well as products such as Teams and the AI assistant Copilot.

The impact of the outage has been felt globally, with users ranging from companies to governments reporting that they were unable to communicate via Outlook.

“We’ve monitored the status of the changes applied to improve serviceability and confirmed they’re not taking as expected,” Microsoft said on X.

“We’re identifying alternate workstreams that can be applied to increase capacity,” the tech giant added, without saying when service was expected to be fully restored.

The disruption went global within an hour, knocking out Microsoft products in 74 countries and territories, outage tracker Downdetector reported.

A map posted by Downdetector on X showed the outage affected users across the Americas and parts of Europe, Asia and Africa.

One of the impacted countries was New Zealand, where the foreign ministry sent a notice saying its “ability to receive emails has been affected by the global Microsoft outage. This also impacts all New Zealand Embassies, Consulates and Representative Offices around the world.”

Microsoft initially said it was investigating outage reports “in the Americas,” but later confirmed that the issue apparently affected “Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region.”

Microsoft 365 is the company’s cloud-based subscription service that includes popular applications such as Outlook and Teams.

“We’ve determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors,” the company wrote on X.

“We’re aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact,” it added.

Downdetector, which tracks online outages, showed a sharp decline around 0450 GMT in users’ reports of disruptions in Washington and Hong Kong.

Thousands of users also reported issues with Teams and Copilot, according to Downdetector.

As the outage dragged on for hours, Microsoft posted a series of updates on X, detailing continued but unsuccessful efforts to restore full service.

In one update shortly after 6 pm Eastern Time (2300 GMT), Microsoft said it was “observing limited recovery” as it sought to route user traffic away from affected servers.

“As capacity is restored, users may experience a gradual recovery as their clients reconnect,” the company added.

World.title: SpaceX Starship test to attempt first-ever spaceship ‘catch’
World.content:
Houston – Elon Musk’s SpaceX was poised Friday to carry out its latest test of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket, the Starship, with plans for a groundbreaking “catch” of the spaceship following a day in orbit.

A successful capture of the Starship upper stage would mark a significant milestone in the space industry’s decades-long pursuit of fully reusable spacecraft that can drastically reduce mission costs and make frequent travel possible.

“If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket,” SpaceX said.

For the 15th Starship test flight Friday, SpaceX aims to recover both stages of the massive 124-meter (407-foot) launch vehicle.

The company has caught the booster, dubbed Super Heavy, on three previous occasions, with the first stage descending vertically back to the launch site shortly after blastoff and nestling into mechanical “chopstick” arms.

It will now attempt to do the same with the spaceship. Some versions of the vessel are designed to launch internet satellites and data centers into orbit, while others will be made to ferry people to the Moon and Mars.

A spacecraft that can be fully reused is the “Holy Grail” of the space industry, said Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.

“No one’s really been able to do that so far,” he said. “People have been trying to do that since the (NASA) space shuttle. But the space shuttle ended up being kind of a compromise because a lot of the vehicle wasn’t reusable.”

Reusing the Starship spacecraft would require the vessel to withstand the extreme heat of reentering Earth’s atmosphere and then return to service without extensive refurbishment.

– Refueling challenge –

Musk, the world’s richest person, has already revolutionized the space sector with the partially reusable Falcon rockets, which are regularly employed to launch satellites and carry astronauts to the International Space Station.

The Starship project, however, has been plagued by years-long delays as SpaceX grapples with novel engineering challenges — even as NASA is counting on the spaceship to serve as a lunar lander for its Artemis program.

Other technical challenges include transferring fuel to Starship in orbit — a requirement for any journey to the Moon or Mars.

Following SpaceX’s high-profile stock market debut in June, the company carried out the first orbital flight of Starship in September, though the mission was cut short due to an engine issue.

It is also investing heavily in additional launch sites for its mega-rocket in Louisiana and Florida.

– Complex capture –

Friday’s launch is scheduled to take place at SpaceX’s “Starbase” in southern Texas at 4:45 pm (2245 GMT).

Following liftoff and the mid-air separation of the two stages, SpaceX plans to bring Super Heavy back to Earth six and a half minutes later, catching it at the launch site on the Gulf of Mexico coastline.

The spaceship will continue to reach Earth’s orbit, where it will deploy 26 satellites into Musk’s Starlink satellite internet constellation that has become a major revenue stream for SpaceX.

It will then circle the planet 14 times, before returning 22 hours later and — SpaceX hopes — descending safely into the chopstick arms.

This capture attempt is more complex than that of the booster, as the spaceship will be descending much faster and from a much greater altitude.

SpaceX has said it would proceed with these maneuvers only if conditions are optimal, and in the past has made last-minute changes to test flights under Musk’s “fail fast” strategy of learning through crashes, explosions and other mishaps.

As of late Thursday, the US Federal Aviation Administration had not yet given its final approval for the test flight.

World.title: Urea overuse in 169 dists raises red flags, CAG probing diversion
World.content:
NEW DELHI: CAG has initiated an all-India performance audit of fertiliser subsidy, specifically to look into the alleged diversion of subsidised urea in at least 169 districts across a few states, including the possibility of diversion outside the country.

The audit, which started in May this year, is likely to be completed by mid-2027 to be tabled by the winter session of Parliament.

Govt spends more than Rs 2 lakh crore annually on the subsidised urea, and their overconsumption above the national and state average in some districts has raised concerns within govt. CAG will assess the demand and efficiency of the urea subsidy framework, which is also the terms of reference of the audit.



The selected 169 districts to be assessed for alleged diversion, include 149 initially chosen by CAG based on their consumption pattern, which were above the state and national average. Twenty other districts were added later after recommendation from the Centre to examine their consumption pattern. The audit will look into the fertiliser movement mechanism, their transportation arrangements, freight subsidy and associated monitoring and control system.





This integrated audit approaches a wider cooperation and participation from different govt departments, like the GST network, agriculture ministry, railways and others, who will assist the auditors in its assessment of the fertiliser control system and the efficacy of the regulators.

The finance ministry recently flagged the possibility of diversion of urea based on e-way bills as it found trucks were taking detours or making multiple stops.

A parliamentary panel too had flagged concerns over diversion of urea, especially in border districts.

Officials said the alleged diversion of subsidised urea from some of the bordering districts in UP, Rajasthan, Punjab and Bihar has also raised doubts if they are also being smuggled out of the country. The highest 37 districts being assessed for overconsumption of urea are in UP, followed by 16 each in Bihar and Tamil Nadu, and 14 each in Punjab and Gujarat.

The 20 districts that were later added for further examinations are in Karnataka, Rajasthan, MP and Maharashtra.

India's total urea consumption is estimated at around 400 LMT a year, of which more than 100 LMT are imported. Even for domestic production, it requires a huge amount of imported LPG, as the fuel constitutes 90% of the input cost of urea. Over-consumption of subsidised urea raises additional subsidy burden on the energy bill and increases our import dependence, besides adding to greenhouse gas emissions, an official said.

Technical grade urea is a core commercial raw material in resins, glues, plywood fabrication, crockery manufacturing, cattle feed, and commercial explosives," the official added.

World.title: Pakistan 80 years old, can't appropriate Indus Valley civilisation: Culture minister
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Culture minister

Friday expressed hope that

will participate in the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi from Nov 20 to 22, even as he trashed Pakistan's attempts to appropriate Indus Valley civilisation, pointing out that the neighbouring nation came into existence only around 80 years ago.

Fifteen countries, including China, Iran, UAE, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, have confirmed their participation for the event, which India will host at the historic Purana Quila complex. Pakistan is yet to respond to the invite.

will attend the inaugural ceremony of the dialogue forum, where India will showcase its 5,000-year-old civilisational journey.

Shekhawat highlighted that PM had proposed the establishment of a Civilisational Dialogue Forum at the 2025 SCO Summit in Tianjin, and it was subsequently, welcomed and endorsed, with India announcing to host the inaugural forum.



The invitation to Pakistan gains significance as it happens to be the first New Delhi has extended after Operation Sindoor last year. Ministers of 25 countries were invited, of which 15 countries have confirmed participation so far, he added.

When asked about attempts by a "neighbouring country" to appropriate Indus Valley civilisation, he said if a country is trying to make such a claim, the question to ask is that "did they even exist then".





"They (Pakistan) came into existence only around 80 years ago..." he said.

The minister noted that Pakistan's civilisational and cultural evolution is no different from India as the former became a separate country after Partition in 1947. "So, at least on this aspect there should be no space for differences... Moreover, whatever may be a country's geopolitical, strategic and bilateral ties, one must take a step forward to reinforce cultural relations so that it can help build better dialogue and coordination between people of the two countries," he said.

The four broad themes of the dialogue are civilisational and cultural expressions; art and architecture; language, literature, script and manuscript traditions; and monastic trails.

Row erupts over foreign medicos' 'MD Physician' title

NEW DELHI: An 'MD' title after a doctor's name usually signals a postgraduate medical qualification in India. But for some foreign medical graduates, MD (Physician) is the title of their primary medical degree.This difference has triggered a dispute over professional titles, with doctors warning that patients could be misled and foreign medical graduates arguing their qualifications are officially recognised.Dr Dhruv Chauhan, national spokesperson for Junior Doctors' Network (JDN) of Indian Medical Association, flagged the issue in a post on X, alleging some doctors misuse the 'MD' degree title awarded in foreign countries, where it may denote a primary medical qualification equivalent to MBBS in India.He said that using it in professional titles and online biographies could mislead patients and even other doctors, and warned of possible legal consequences. He also advised doctors against such representations.Dr MK Ramesh, president of NMC's Medical Assessment and Rating Board told TOI the issue arises from differences in medical qualification nomenclature across countries. In some countries, the basic medical qualification is called an MD, whereas in India it is MBBS.This distinction needs to be clearly recognised. Some measures have already been taken to address the issue, and further steps will be pursued.A senior doctor said the issue had persisted for nearly a decade despite repeated representations to regulators. "Patients cannot be expected to know the difference," he said.All FMGs Association has defended the use of the title "MD Physician", arguing the qualification is recognised as equivalent to MBBS in India and that graduates should not be branded fraudulent merely for mentioning the degree awarded by their foreign universities.

World.title: Breakthrough HIV drug sees 18 patent filings, may delay affordable generics
World.content:
An unusually high 18 patent applications filed in India for lenacapavir

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: An unusually high 18 patent applications filed in India for lenacapavir, a breakthrough HIV therapy, have raised concerns that these could prolong market exclusivity, delay affordable generics, keep prices high and restrict patient access. Contesting the move, patient groups and civil society have filed opposition with the regulatory authorities, arguing the applications lack novelty and inventive steps.Lenacapavir, a long-acting injectable, administered twice yearly for both HIV prevention and treatment, a medicine designated as essential by WHO.Last year, US FDA approved Gilead Sciences' lenacapavir as the first and only twice-yearly injectable pre-exposure prophylaxis to reduce sexually acquired HIV. Gilead has filed at least 18 patent pleas till date in India, covering different aspects of it, including the base compound, salt forms, formulations, dosing regimens, compositions, and methods of use."The pattern of filings reflects a systematic strategy to create layered patent protection around a single medicine, with the effect of deterring generic entry and prolonged monopoly control beyond the standard 20-year patent term.Such practices, also referred to as "evergreening", whereby multiple secondary patents covering minor variations in forms, formulations, or used or pursued to extend exclusivity," KM Gopakumar, senior researcher and legal advisor at TWN told TOI.In a letter to the department for promotion of industry and internal trade, patient groups demanded that the patent office must rigorously examine and reject the company's secondary patent applications.Dr Reddy's is one of six generic manufacturers which has signed voluntary licenses with Gilead to manufacture and commercialise lenacapavir across 120 low and lower middle income countries, including India. The generic injection is projected to cost approximately $40 per person annually. So, apart from the voluntary licence holders, no other generics can manufacture and market the drug.Further, the patents, if granted, are set to expire in 2042, 28 years after the first application was filed. "Granting these patents would legitimise Gilead's evergreening strategy," Prathibha Sivasubramanian of Working Group on Access to Medicines and Treatments, told TOI.

World.title: SpiceJet troubles mount, board to weigh fundraise on Nov 18
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Cash-strapped SpiceJet's troubles have mounted to a level where the airline carrying on its skeletal operations without a fresh infusion of funds may soon become difficult.

The low cost carrier Friday informed BSE its board will meet on Nov 18 "to consider and approve the proposal for raising of fresh capital by way of issuance of equity shares, preference shares..."

Once again company sources have claimed there are two investors eying the airline. Whether this goes through and if there's a change of promoters and management - something the airline has seen multiple times in its turbulent life - remains to be seen.

SpiceJet's intimation to BSE came after multiple developments like Dubai Airports that operates Dubai International and Al Maktoum airports stopping its check-in services for SpiceJet over non-payment of about Rs 36 crore. On Thursday, its four flights to Amritsar, Jaipur, Mumbai and Delhi were cancelled due to non-payment to ground-handling company dnata. These aircraft operated to India without passengers.

On the Dubai issue, the airline spokesperson said the company is "in the process of resolving the matter. We have adequate bank guarantee cover in place and are working to ensure that the issue is sorted out at the earliest."

World.title: Display revised anti-cancer drug prices prominently: NPPA
World.content:
NPPA has called for strict monitoring of the implementation of trade margin rationalisation (TMR)

NEW DELHI: Drug prices regulator, National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), has called for strict monitoring of the implementation of trade margin rationalisation (TMR) on 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs, notified on Oct 17 with revised prices effective Nov 9.All manufacturers, retailers, dealers, stockists, hospitals and medical institutions have been directed to comply with the revised prices and prominently display the updated price lists at their premises and websites, the authority said in an office memorandum issued earlier this week.The revised price lists, based on submissions received from companies up to Nov 11, are available on the NPPA website along with the 'Pharma Sahi Daam' app and portal.State drug controllers have been directed to strictly monitor compliance by manufacturers, dealers, hospitals and medical institutions to ensure that the benefits of revised MRPs are passed on to patients. Any violation may attract overcharging proceedings under the provisions of DPCO, 2013, NPPA said.Complaints regarding overcharging, shortage or non-availability of medicines can be reported through the 'Pharma Sahi Daam' app/portal, NPPA helpline or email.Further, the state drug controllers have been asked to submit their action taken reports to NPPA by Nov 16.The move comes days after NPPA fixed 30% trade margins on 137 non-scheduled cancer drugs, translating to 1,391 brands and dosage forms. The list includes both patented and non-patented drugs based on a list recommended by an expert committee under Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

World.title: CBI probing impersonation of PMO official
World.content:
NEW DELHI: CBI has initiated an investigation following a complaint from the prime minister's office regarding an impersonation and extortion attempt targeting Aditya Khemka, managing director of CP Plus, a leading security and surveillance brand, officials said.

The impostor, identified as Manish Kumar Gupta, fraudulently masquerading as an IAS officer, allegedly pressured CP Plus executives to install high-end indoor and outdoor CCTV surveillance systems free of cost or at rock-bottom rates at a residence purportedly belonging to his parents. When CP Plus personnel and their vendors sought clarification, Gupta allegedly issued verbal threats of dire official consequences.

World.title: Searches continue for Kulgam terrorists
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Security forces continued Friday massive cordon and search operations to track down terrorists who shot and injured three CRPF personnel in south Kashmirâs Kulgam district two days ago.

Around 200 alleged overground workers have been picked up but all have been released after questioning, a senior police officer said.

World.title: All departing U.S. flights grounded due to communication outage
World.content:
U.S. aviation regulators issued an extremely rare ground stop of all flights across the country on Friday (November 13, 2026) after a major communications outage, which the Department of Homeland Security said did not appear to be the result of any "nefarious attack."

The halt triggered immediate chaos and confusion for travellers, with departure boards at many airports showing flights were operating normally, even as customers were unable to board planes.

The Federal Aviation Administration "issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centres," the agency said. "FAA technicians are investigating the issue."

In a subsequent message on X, the agency described the problem as "a temporary telecommunications outage" and said it was acting "out of an abundance of caution."

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no sign of a threat to the United States and "this isn't another 9/11."

"There was no indication, as of yet, that this was a nefarious attack against us, it's just a telecommunication outage, as of right now," Mr. Mullins said, adding officials were "not ruling out anything at this point."

The FAA has announced similar orders in recent years on individual airlines due to communications issues, usually lasting a couple of hours or less. Systemwide groundings nationwide are far less common.

In January 2023, the FAA called a nationwide ground stop due to problems with the Notice to Air Missions system (NOTAM), which provides information to pilots about hazards and information that can affect flights.

That outage lasted just under two hours, and was thought at the time to be the first nationwide grounding since 9/11.

Friday's (November 13, 2026) FAA order came a day after U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy formally asked Congress for $30.1 billion in funds to upgrade and modernise the U.S. Air Traffic Control System.

"This investment is critical to complete the modernization of our national airspace — delivering a resilient telecommunications backbone for air traffic controllers, modern hardware and software, state-of-the-art control towers, and world-class airport infrastructure," Duffy and Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought wrote in a letter to lawmakers.

Confusion and delays

At Las Vegas airport, the Southwest Airlines check-in desk told passengers there could be no flights taking off for the night.

Check-in staff at one desk said they had been told the ground stop would last at least eight hours, with one member of airline personnel saying it would be 24 hours.

Travellers were left in the dark, with some saying they had been told their flight was delayed because of wind, while others were left to gather what information they could.

"So supposedly, nobody's flying, but they haven't told the public yet," said an exasperated Joseph Anderson, 72, who was trying to fly from Las Vegas to Oakland, California.

"We're trying to debate whether or not we need to reschedule or drive or what, but if the whole country is stopped, that means the highways are going to be jammed too.

"We can't get our luggage, so we kind of stuck," added the retired Air Force veteran.

"I would hope the communication can be better from the from the FAA in the next hour or so."

World.title: After CBI, ED arrests Mahadev betting app scam accused
World.content:
The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) on Friday (November 13, 2026) said it has arrested Saurabh Chandrakar, co-owner and promoter of the Mahadev Online Book illegal betting syndicate, and would now be confronting with the evidence of money laundering against him.

Earlier on Thursday (November 12, 2026), a special CBI court remanded Chandrakar to seven days’ judicial custody and dismissed ED’s application to execute their non-bailable warrant against him. On Friday (November 13, 2026) post the arrest, the ED produced him at a special PMLA [Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002] court in Raipur which remanded him to ED custody for seven days till November 19 for further investigation.

“In ED custody, Saurabh Chandrakar will be confronted with the statements of his associates, digital data and documents concerning his foreign entities and evidence of commission of offence of money laundering,” an ED official said.

According to the ED, Chandrakar and another co-promoter Ravi Uppal operated “Mahadev Online Book” (various online betting websites) from Head Office in Dubai through a franchise of “betting panels” across India and the United Arab Emirates.

A statement further noted that player money went through bank accounts held in other people’s names and left India through hawala. ED’s main complaint of October 2023 estimated the syndicate’s earnings at about ₹450 crore a month.

“Saurabh Chandrakar did not answer the summons issued to him by ED in September 2023 and continued to evade investigation by law enforcement agencies. On ED’s application, the Special Court issued a Non-Bailable Warrant against him on 04.09.2023, and shortly thereafter, INTERPOL also published a Red Notice against him on ED’s request. His challenge to the warrant was dismissed by the High Court of Chhattisgarh on 22.03.2025. He obtained a passport of Vanuatu while holding an Indian passport, and even claimed before the Special Court that he had given up Indian citizenship on 28.06.2022,” the official said.

On the progress of the investigations into money laundering allegations, the official said that the ED had thus far searched about 190 premises, seized or frozen about ₹2,000 crore and attached property now valued at about ₹3,500 crore, about ₹1,800 crore of it abroad, including 22 immovable properties in Dubai. It has filed six prosecution complaints against 116 accused. Saurabh Chandrakar is the fifteenth person arrested by ED in this case, the ED statement noted.

The agency purportedly followed the money from panel operators through the Dubai Head Office to hawala handlers and share-market investors. “It froze securities of about ₹236 crore held by Dubai companies in September 2023. In July 2026 ED arrested Vikas Garg, whose companies received about ₹940 crore of betting proceeds, of which about ₹766 crore went into the acquisition of the United States company Ebix Inc. ED has attached about ₹941 crore in that limb,” the official said.

The ED statement also mentioned Chandrakar’s lavish wedding in UAE in the year 2023. “The wedding at Ras Al Khaimah in February 2023 cost about ₹200 crore in cash, with three chartered aircraft from Nagpur. ED traced that money through the event company, hotels and angadia firms, and the guest list it recovered identified the management of the syndicate,” the official added.

World.title: Tanker hits a river cruise boat on Mississippi River in New Orleans; rescue operations under way
World.content:
A tanker in New Orleans that apparently lost its steering slammed into a docked river cruise boat with 180 people aboard on Friday (November 13, 2026), the Mayor said. All aboard survived after the crash prompted a massive rescue operation for passengers and crew who plunged into the Mississippi River as the ship took on water and began to topple over.

Video from the scene showed the much larger Atlantic Asphalt tanker hit the cruise boat while it was docked as metal and glass crashed and crunched.

Tugboat operators, nearby workers, police and several other rescuers rushed to help. New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno called it “a miracle on the Mississippi.”

The Mayor said 32 people were taken to the hospital, but none of them had critical injuries.

The boat started listing within minutes and flipped while emergency workers were still trying to get everyone off the ship.

Dozens of people on board and at least two police officers were dragged from the 19°C river onto nearby ships.

Devon Flanagan was at his job nearby at the Port of New Orleans when workers rushed down the dock. He got out of his truck and saw the American Heritage on its side and passengers in the water.

“It was just chaos,” he said. “You had all types of ships, like other barges and other companies down there trying to help out, which also was a little convoluted because you had people still in the water.”

The cruise ship was built in 2015 and operated by American Cruise Lines. It is five stories and can hold up to 150 passengers.

The American Heritage was finishing an eight-day cruise to several Mississippi River destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi.

The cruise line said it was working with the Coast Guard and would share more information when it can.

The tanker involved in the crash specialises in carrying large quantities of asphalt and bitumen, a semi-solid substance that is often used for road construction and roofing, according to the live shipping tracker MarineTraffic.

Ships carrying asphalt and bitumen are often heated well above 120°C to prevent the asphalt from solidifying on the ship, according to the maritime periodical Marine Insights. It is not immediately clear whether the ship was carrying any materials when the crash occurred.

The 160-metre-long vessel had a final destination in New Orleans, according to MarineTraffic, and was sailing under a flag for the Marshall Islands.

World.title: Two-year-old dies after firecracker explodes inside his mouth
World.content:
A two-year-old boy died after a firecracker exploded inside his mouth in Chhattisgarh’s Surguja district, according to his family members.

The victim Aditya’s parents told journalists that on November 9, the boy put a pop-pop firecracker — that’s called lehsun due to its garlic like shape and is designed to explode when thrown on the ground — in his mouth while playing.

His father Indrajit Manjhi said the firecracker exploded inside his mouth, injuring his gums and causing bleeding. After other children informed the parents about the mishap, the child was first taken to a community health centre in Sitapur and brought back home after the bleeding stopped. However, when the bleeding started again, he was taken back to the health centre next day. Later, he was taken to a mission hospital in Ambikapur on November 11 where he succumbed to his injuries the same night.

The police have registered an accidental death report and further investigation is underway, the father added.

World.title: File FIR against those who tarnish party’s image says Bengal BJP chief
World.content:
Observing that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power without the support of those trying to make into the party now, president of the party’s West Bengal unit Samik Bhattacharya on Friday (November 13, 2026) said that FIR should be registered against elements who are trying to associate with the party and tarnish the image of the party.

“Register FIRs. Suvendu Adhikari is the police minister. Give me the papers, I will file them,” Mr. Bhattacharya said. The remarks made by the Bengal BJP chief have been made at a time when there are allegations that leaders and supporters of other parties are trying to join the BJP. There have been certain reports of BJP supporters allegedly indulging in extortion after the party came to power, a charge that was levelled against Trinamool Congress leaders when the party was in power. “BJP has reached here (came to power) by keeping them out. BJP has no need to touch them,” he said.

Mr. Bhattacharya said that there can be some ‘deviations’ and the “party will correct them”. The BJP leader said anyone cannot claim allegiance to the party simply by garlanding BJP leaders. “The door was closed before; it is still closed. The door has not been officially opened,” he said. The remarks by the Bengal BJP chief come amidst claims that it is facing a challenge of “Trinamoolisation of the BJP” and Mr. Bhattacharya has been saying that the party will resist it.

BJP leaders to be appointed ward coordinators

While the BJP president warned against outsiders getting into the party, he made it clear that it will be BJP leaders who are appointed as ward commissioners. Mr. Bhattacharya said that the party will not take suggestions from Md. Salim, the CPI(M) State secretary or any other party to appoint coordinators to oversee civic services in Kolkata and Howrah if municipal elections were delayed.

“They (the ward coordinators) will be BJP people,” he said. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari had said that the government will appoint coordinators in the wards of Kolkata Municipal Corporation and Howrah Municipal Corporation if the stay on civic polls is not lifted by the Supreme Court.

The Calcutta High Court on October 6 restrained the West Bengal State Election Commission from issuing any notification for the upcoming KMC elections based on newly redrawn wards until a pending petition challenging the delimitation exercise is decided.

World.title: NHRC seeks Education Ministry’s response over alleged neglect of Veer Baal Diwas in schools
World.content:
National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) on Friday sought an explanation from the Union Ministry of Education over allegations that schools across the country give greater prominence to Children’s Day celebrations on November 14 while failing to adequately highlight the historical significance of Veer Baal Diwas, observed on December 26.

The Commission’s bench, headed by member Priyank Kanoongo, acted on a complaint submitted by Sanjeev Newar of the Seva Nyay Utthan Foundation, which raised concerns about the limited awareness among school students regarding the courage and supreme sacrifice of the four Sahibzadas of Guru Gobind Singh.

The Commission hence issued a notice to the Secretary of the Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education, Government of India asking whether the Central Government or any competent authority has issued an official notification, order or circular declaring November 14 as Children’s Day. If such a directive exists, the Ministry has been asked to furnish a copy and provide the relevant details.

The Ministry has been directed to submit a detailed Action Taken Report (ATR) within 14 days, addressing the concerns raised in the complaint.

The NHRC has also sought clarification on whether schools are being encouraged to conduct dedicated educational and awareness programmes on December 26 to commemorate Veer Baal Diwas. Such initiatives, the Commission has indicated, should help students understand the historical significance of the four Sahibzadas and their extraordinary courage and sacrifice.

Highlighting the broader educational implications of the issue, the Commission stressed the need to ensure that children are exposed to important chapters of India’s history and cultural heritage. It observed that educational institutions play a significant role in nurturing awareness of values such as bravery, faith, sacrifice and resistance to injustice.

World.title: Urgent climate finance pleas at COP31 face a non-urgent response
World.content:
Urgent pleas for cash from poor ​nations most exposed to the kind of climate-related disasters that have marked this year risk meeting a sluggish response at Turkiye’s COP31 talks as Western governments put ‌national security and living costs first.

Two years ago, rich countries agreed at UN climate talks they would triple ​climate funding for poorer countries to $300 billion per year by 2035 versus a previous 2020 target. Also by 2035, financing ⁠from all public and private sources combined would be $1.3 trillion annually.

The rich countries met their 2020 target two years late.

Also Read | Why climate finance remains a recurring flashpoint at UN summits

Since then, climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security.

Vulnerable small island nations say the cash they need to repair damage and to guard against future climate-related crises is again arriving too slowly and their own budgets have shrunk.

“Like many small island ‌developing states, we remain in a perpetual climate disaster recovery mode,” Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale told the conference. “We cannot build resilience ‌while ⁠our fiscal space erodes.”

Even when money is available, technical hurdles set by lenders can stretch the administrative capacity of ⁠small states.

For many developed nations, facing international and domestic unrest as citizens protest against the rising cost of living, their focus has narrowed.

Britain, which has sought to be a leader in addressing climate change, said in July savings made from switching some climate finance contributions from grants to loans would be used to help fund a cap on ​domestic bus fares.

Meanwhile, defence spending has climbed significantly.

The Stockholm ‌International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) estimated in April that world military expenditure reached $2.89 trillion in 2025, up 2.9% in real terms from 2024.

Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine said military defence ultimately was the smaller concern.

“We are told there is no money, but as spending on war grows, the greatest security threat we face remains underfunded. I appeal to you: Find money for life, not death,” she said ‌in her speech to the conference in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

Also Read | UN climate summit pushes electrification goal as groups call for mining safeguards

COP31 seeking implementation, not new targets

As they ​respond to the contemporary mood, host country Turkiye and lead negotiator Australia have emphasised making previous pledges work, rather than securing a new headline target at the conference, which continues until the end of next week.

“COP31 must respond to ⁠the global moment and send a clear message to accelerate implementation,” Australia’s COP31 negotiating president Chris Bowen said. He also said finance must be “faster, simpler and fairer”.

Analysis by previous COP host Brazil published earlier this week found that $137 billion was mobilised in 2024, a slight increase on 2023, but that ‌direct aid and future commitments to multilateral funds were lower.

Current trends suggested provision would fall $840 billion short of the $1.3 trillion goal, it said.

“Geopolitical tensions, constrained fiscal space in many developing countries and the high cost of capital where it is most needed are among the obstacles,” the report said.

By way of solutions, it urged measures such as risk-sharing and clearer links between national plans and budgets.

Some smaller nations have taken novel steps to find cash and to spur richer nations to match it.

The Solomon Islands pledged $400,000 from its own pocket on Thursday (November 13, 2026), saying it was determined to show leadership and calling on rich countries to do the same.

The Bahamas committed $75 million to protect and restore its seagrass meadows, which ‌store carbon, to try to persuade investors to fund verified carbon projects.

The Hindu Editorial | New deal: On COP31 and lofty climate goals

Unclogging the system to get money flowing

Both public and private funding provide climate finance grants, loans, ​aid and investment in measures ranging from renewable energy to flood defences.

Multilateral development banks are a conduit for finance that leverages capital provided by shareholder countries to increase lending power and they say they are delivering. Their lending reached record ⁠levels in 2025, according to the European Investment Bank.

But, they could do more, according to Washington-based think tank the Center for Global Development and recipients ⁠of the finance have said the development banks should make access easier.

Addressing that, a group of multilateral funds told the COP31 talks they would rely more on one another’s assessments in co-financed operations rather than having to go through multiple overlapping processes.

For private investors, ‌the most obvious issue is the risk of investing in an instrument that does not guarantee returns.

Given how unforthcoming the world’s richer governments have been, the private sector is ever more important.

“Our clients see opportunities in the energy transition, but they need reliable ​power, predictable costs and confidence in customer demand before they invest,” HSBC Chief Sustainability Officer Julian Wentzel said. “COP31 needs to help create that confidence.”

World.title: ‘John Doe’ movie review: Madhumita finds her footing with a neat, effective thriller
World.content:
They say we are what our fathers leave behind. The latest Tamil film John Doe revolves around fathers of all kinds — one who fed shame and toxicity to his child, one who failed to stand by his daughter, and one who looks after a childlike wife. Even when they are absent, or through that very absence, some of these fathers keep shaping their children’s lives.

Which is why, even though John Doe revolves around the mysterious murder of an eight-year-old boy, director Madhumita begins her story elsewhere — with another boy child in another period who grows up listening to his terrorising, toxic police officer father humiliate him daily. The child can’t eat as much as he wants to, can’t score anything less than first rank, and isn’t even allowed to cry at his mother’s funeral.

As fate would have it, Chandru (Arjun Das) becomes a police officer, a Kerala Police Sub-Inspector in Kadampuzha. He has achieved what his father said he couldn’t, and yet Chandru’s father (Badava Gopi is a great casting choice; his voice becomes a character), even posthumously, has his clutches firmly on his son’s psyche, constantly chiding and shaming him, especially when he feels low or makes mistakes. Credit to Madhumita for how John Doe becomes the story of Chandru proving his father wrong by becoming a good police officer.

It is also about figuring out who he is. He knows he isn’t the person the voice in his head keeps portraying him to be; if so, who is he? In fact, even the film’s title alludes to this. ‘John Doe’ — as a coroner explains — is a term used in American law enforcement to refer to an unidentified male body or patient (‘Jane Doe’ is for a female). By attempting to identify and seek justice for this young John Doe, who was killed by drowning in a lake in Kadampuzha, Chandru is also identifying who he himself is and seeking justice for the child in him who was slowly killed.

Simultaneously, we follow a new family arriving in Kurinjimedu, Tamil Nadu: Darshana (Srishti Y), a widow, her eight-year-old son Hriday (Nirav S), and teenage daughter Lakshmi, a.k.a. Lucky (Zaara Vineet Chandhokhe). One evening, Hriday goes missing, after which Inspector of Police A Rao (Sanchana Natarajan) begins a missing-person investigation. By initially showing the drowned corpse of a boy who resembles Hriday in Kadampuzha, Madhumita ensures that every additional shot of Hriday, a normal child who just wanted a dog in his new, spacious house, disturbs you. The rest of the film shuttles between Kurinjimedu and Kadampuzha, and these worlds collide when Chandru unearths disturbing details.

First and foremost, if you believe the sole worth of a whodunit or investigative thriller lies in how cleverly it executes its climactic twist or reveals the killer’s identity, John Doe may compel you to rethink. A genre fan would see the pre-intermission twist coming from afar, and the film hardly tries to hide its killer. Though it mostly gets its casting right, in a whodunit, when you see a familiar face amidst a group of non-actors, you tend to look closer, which spoils the fun. A more experienced genre filmmaker could have done it differently to drive home the fact that anyone can commit crimes.

Such predictability aside, John Doe would compel your attention and keep you hooked throughout its runtime. Madhumita excels in the little moments between the dramatic spikes in the narrative. The nuances and the sensitive writing are what you might take home with you. Watch how a couple takes the news of the death of their child. Their son had gone missing five years ago, and Madhumita tells you what the psyche of such parents would be like — they don’t scream and wail as you might expect; the mother, who had held on to hope, struggles far more than the father, who had long accepted grief. Similarly, you will see a child suffering from trauma wanting a family member to accompany him into a psychologist’s room — because, to him, the doctor too is a stranger, and he doesn’t wish to go anywhere alone with him after what has happened to him. Now, also see how sensibly the psychologist (Karthik Kumar) behaves, in contrast to the hot-blooded cops. We wish more filmmakers had this emotional aptitude.

‘John Doe’ (Tamil) Director: Madhumita Cast: Arjun Das, Sanchana Natarajan, Zaara Vineet Chandhokhe, Srishti Y Runtime: 149 minutes Storyline: Two police officers join forces to investigate the mysterious death of an eight-year-old boy, uncovering disturbing secrets along the way

The film’s genre pleasures include how Chandru and A Rao, a unique buddy-cop duo, also become metaphorical parental figures to the children of this world. Chandru is so attached to the case that he puts his career in jeopardy; even if she appears stoic, Rao, too, takes this quite personally. Just as you begin to wonder if this is the typical good-cop-bad-cop routine — where the good cop is usually more intelligent and the bad cop more brawny — a superb action scene set in a lodge tells you these two truly complete each other. One follows ‘instincts’, while the other packs a punch — you can never settle on who is who. It also helps that these two actors look the part; Arjun moves like a cop finding his footing, while Sanchana, despite some occasional theatricality, shows immense potential.

Of course, the film takes some liberties with that idea in the second half that don’t work. More subtlety could have helped the film in general, like when it keeps underlining Lucky’s bratty, hormonal teenage personality (here, a line about the goth subculture feels stereotypical, given that the subculture is now far beyond its conventional association with darkness and death).

You are also asked to extend some cinematic liberties for a few nitty-gritty details — like how you don’t understand how the car plunged into the lake in Kadampuzha at that speed, or how Chandru failed to notice the culprit. Also, this could have been a far more atmospheric thriller, had the film taken these characters through these hillside towns more often instead of the few locations the plot circles (cutting between two similar-looking police stations also disturbs the immersion at times).

Now, if this film still manages to steer through all these flaws, it is because of how resolute the writing feels in giving its viewers an engaging experience. Which is why, when I realised that John Doe might have a sequel, I wasn’t all that sceptical (given it is a trend to end films with a hint at a sequel to aid potential franchising). It seems like Chandru and Rao are just starting, and Madhumita is testing the waters in a genre she is not too used to making films in.

In cinema, it is unfair how filmmakers are often weighed against their last film. But I must confess that having two Madhumita directorials released in the same month meant that I still carried the aftertaste of Love Always before entering John Doe. You might too, if you watched that JioHotstar series. However, all works of art deserve an objective, discerning audience, and this John Doe deserves its attention.

Contrary to its title, this film isn’t suffering from an identity crisis. It knows what it wants to be, and it puts in the effort to become that. Such cinema is worth rooting for any day.

John Doe is currently running in theatres

World.title: UP ATS asks Google to block 20L email accounts created by man arrested over hoax bomb threats
World.content:
The Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) has written to Google’s Gmail office in California, seeking the blocking of over 20 lakh email accounts allegedly recovered from the laptop of 24-year-old Ankit Shankhwar, who was arrested last month for allegedly creating fake email IDs linked to a series of hoax bomb threats in Delhi-NCR and Mumbai last month.

Officials said Shankhwar allegedly used fictitious identities to create the accounts and sold them in bulk to anti-India elements based in Pakistan, Bangladesh and other countries in exchange for cryptocurrency.

A senior ATS officer said the agency has sent an online request, along with a covering letter, to Gmail, sharing a list of the accounts and seeking their blocking to prevent possible misuse. The ATS is also preparing to seek Shankhwar’s police custody remand following the recovery of fresh evidence from his mobile phone and laptop. Shankhwar was arrested on October 28.

World.title: ‘Antim mauka’: In Uttar Pradesh, BJP sets target for restoring deleted Hindu voters
World.content:
Days after Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath claimed that 1.27 crore Hindus had been excluded from the state’s electoral rolls and the number of Muslim voters had increased by 1.65% during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the BJP has urged its leaders to work on a war footing to ensure that most of these names are added back to the voter list during the ongoing Special Summary Revision (SSR) of the rolls, The Indian Express has learnt.

The 1.27 crore figure across UP’s 403 Assembly constituencies comes up to an average of just over 31,000 such voters allegedly excluded from the rolls in each seat. The BJP has set its district leaders a target to ensure that 10,000 to 25,000 such voters in each constituency are added back to the rolls, sources said, adding this translates to at least 50 voters in each polling booth. The drive is expected to begin on November 20, three days after the SSR draft rolls are published.

The target was conveyed to BJP district presidents and in-charges at a meeting in Lucknow on Friday. Adityanath, his deputy Keshav Prasad Maurya, and state BJP chief Pankaj Chaudhary addressed the meeting. Sources said the party decided not to “undertake any other programme” over the next month and instead completely focus on updating the voter list. “Even if we succeed in adding back 40 lakh to 80 lakh voters, that should suffice,” said a leader.



Leaders privy to the discussions said Adityanath had labelled the next month “antim mauka (last chance)” to bring back these eligible voters and emphasised that opportunity should not be missed. While the draft rolls after this special summary revision are scheduled to be released on November 17, the claims and objections period will run until December 16. The electoral rolls are scheduled to be published on January 4, 2027.

The CM also directed party leaders to compare the Assembly voter lists with the electoral rolls for panchayat polls and the list of government welfare scheme beneficiaries to figure out who had been left out of the Assembly election rolls. While the Election Commission of India (ECI) prepares the rolls for the Assembly polls, the State Election Commission (SEC) prepares the rolls for the panchayat polls.



For the BJP leadership, the concern is that the party won several seats in the 2022 Assembly polls by 1,500-3,000 votes and if the rolls shrink by even 5,000-10,000 voters, it could bring these constituencies into play. Sources said Maurya has told those at the meeting that the difference between the BJP and the Samajwadi Party (SP) was 1.55 crore votes in 2017 and this shrank to 85 lakh in 2022.

This makes the number flagged by the CM a matter of concern, sources said. “If we consider the data of 1.27 crore names, their average deletion is 31,513 votes per Assembly constituency, which is a significant number. So, the party has set a goal to reach out to left out eligible voters and bring back to the rolls an average of 10,000-25,000 names,” said a senior BJP leader.



Sources further said that the BJP had decided to focus on the voters who have shifted to another constituency in the state or have migrated to another state. There will also be an emphasis on including more women and youth in the rolls.

“During SIR, a sizable number of urban voters opted to shift to their rural addresses. This created a problem for the party in urban regions, which have been its traditional zone of strength. We will speak to such voters and help them fill forms to shift back to the urban seats. Similarly, people who migrated to other states and got enrolled as voters there will be requested to shift their votes back to UP,” said a BJP office-bearer. “The gender ratio in the existing roll is 834 and the party’s assessment is that lots of women were left out or their names were deleted for various reasons during SIR. If they are eligible, the party will help them get enrolled.”



“The party will not pay much attention to the Muslim-dominated seats it never wins. We will deploy our workers in the constituencies where Hindu voters were deleted in large numbers during SIR and which we can win if their names are restored,” said the leader.

“The BJP will hold district and Assembly-level meetings by November 19 to discuss the strategy with ground-level workers. From November 20, our leaders and booth-level agents will fan out across booths,” said a leader who attended the Friday meeting with Adityanath.

World.title: Jharkhand Congress MLA booked for rape after 14-yr-old girl alleges assault, forced abortion
World.content:
An FIR has been registered under the Protection of Children against Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act against a Congress MLA following a complaint by a 14-year-old Adivasi girl alleging sexual assault at his residence in Ranchi. The complaint also includes allegations of physical assault, forced domestic labour and forced abortion.

According to the police, the complaint contains allegations of physical assault and rape against the MLA. In a complaint filed at Dhurwa Police Station, the minor girl said the MLA had brought her from her house on the promise of providing her education. She alleged that instead of being sent to school, she was made to do household work at the MLA’s residence.



In her complaint, the minor alleged that she was sexually assaulted on August 5, threatened into silence and forced to abort her pregnancy. The MLA has denied the allegations, calling them a conspiracy by former Congress leaders “working with the Opposition”.

He said the matter had reached senior Congress leaders and that he had been asked to cooperate with the investigation.

“Let the investigation begin. I will cooperate. The truth will come out,” he said, adding that party leaders and workers had extended their support to him. But the allegations have sparked a row, with BJP state president Aditya Sahu demanding the immediate arrest of the MLA. Sahu also alleged that the girl’s family had accused the MLA’s relatives of assault, abuse, and physical and mental harassment.



Questioning the silence of Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Sahu asked whether the party would take action against its MLA. He also questioned whether the ruling alliance would protect its political ally or ensure justice for the girl. “BJP would launch a statewide agitation if the MLA is not arrested immediately and the girl is not provided security,” he warned.

Congress spokesperson

Rakesh Sinha told The Indian Express that an FIR alone could not establish the allegations and that a conspiracy could not be ruled out. However, he said the matter was “sensitive, and the party would wait for the investigation”.

Asked whether the party would discuss the matter, Sinha said that, due to Chhath Puja, which is the biggest and most important festival, no meeting was likely over the next two days. If anything adverse emerged against the MLA, he could be expelled from the party, he said.

World.title: Himachal announces Rs 1,500 monthly aid, 300 units free power for women aged 18-59 yrs
World.content:
Around 3.50 lakh eligible women aged between 18 and 59 years are set to receive a monthly financial assistance of Rs 1,500 and 300 units of free electricity after the Himachal Pradesh Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, on Friday accorded its approval for the launch of the ‘Mukhya Mantri Apna Parivar Sukhi Parivar Yojna’ ahead of the Assembly elections due in the latter half of 2027.

Under the scheme, all eligible women in a family will receive monthly financial assistance, but only one member will be eligible for free electricity each month. For women above 59 years, the state government has already enhanced their monthly financial assistance from Rs 1,050 to Rs 1,500, according to a government spokesperson.

World.title: ‘Intensifying’ El Niño to persist until March 2027; strongest ever since 1950, says NOAA
World.content:
El Niño will continue to remain ‘strong’ to ‘very strong’ during the first quarter of 2027, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) said on Thursday.

The UN organisation further said that the current El Niño event continues to intensify, and would become the “strongest ever since 1950”. It is set to shatter all previously known records with respective to the sea surface temperatures along the equatorial Pacific Ocean.

El Niño is a naturally occurring phenomenon associated with warm seas along the equatorial Pacific Oceans. El Niño alters rain patterns, spikes temperatures, increases incidents of wild fires, leads to extreme weather in the form of fluids or droughts across the world.

World.title: These voters in Pune never moved, someone changed their addresses anyway
World.content:
MORE THAN two years ago, in October 2024, the Pune District Election Officer (DEO) first flagged to the Maharashtra Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) irregular patterns in voter applications for change in address to other constituencies. Two more letters followed five months later, one suggesting such applications were being submitted in bulk by persons other than the voters concerned.

On November 19, 2025, NCP leader Ajit Gavhane, hand-delivered a complaint with a list of 58 names and claimed the list was an example of “fraudulent deletions/ shifting of voters” and there were more than 15,000 cases. This finally led the Maharashtra CEO’s office to write to the Pune DEO ordering an inquiry, according to documents reviewed by The Indian Express.

At least six voters in the list whose addresses were changed and names deleted from their original constituency said they had neither shifted residences nor submitted any form for address change.



Fatimabi Mehboob Sayyed, one of the voters on Gavhane’s list, said her voter address was shifted to Ovala Majiwada in Thane without her knowledge.

Salar Shaikh, Welfare Party of India candidate in the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation election this year, said his name was shifted to neighbouring Pimpri. His voter ID has now been deleted from the SIR draft roll because, he alleged, the Booth Level Officer in Pimpri refused to fill his SIR enumeration form. “How was my name shifted in the first place,” he asked. He has filled Form 6 for re-inclusion in the voter list.

In his complaint, Gavhane had claimed these 58 voters were permanent residents of voter lists in Bhosari Assembly constituency and had “never filed any application for transfer or deletion of their names from the said voter list”. He had contested on an NCP (Sharad Pawar) ticket and lost the Bhosari Assembly seat in the 2024 state Assembly elections.

The Pune DEO received reports from eight election officers from Thane, Khed Alandi, Ambegaon, Khadakvasla, Nashik East, Bhosari, Kothrud and Pimpri. In his inquiry report, the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) of Bhosari constituency said the address of one voter in Gavhane’s list of 58 had changed within the constituency. The remaining 57 figured among the 5,603 voters, for whom Form 7 (the form for deleting a voter) had been automatically generated after address change applications were submitted and accepted at some other constituency.



The ERO of the new constituency approves or rejects the application on the EC’s ERONET software. If the Form 8 is approved, the software automatically creates a Form 7 in voters’ old constituencies to delete them from the voter list there. (File) The ERO of the new constituency approves or rejects the application on the EC’s ERONET software. If the Form 8 is approved, the software automatically creates a Form 7 in voters’ old constituencies to delete them from the voter list there. (File)

Following queries from The Indian Express, the Pune DEO had on October 31, 2026, directed authorities to take action against those responsible. He issued a show cause notice to Pimpri ERO over how the address change applications were accepted without filed verification. On November 1, the Pimpri Assistant ERO filed a non-cognizable offence report at the Nigdi Police Station under Section 31 of The Representation of the People Act, 1950, against persons who used four mobile numbers to file 40 Form 8 applications.

The Pune DEO finally assessed that in Gavhane’s list of 58 voters, three voters had died, 11 were living where they were registered, and voter registration (Form 6) applications had since been filed online to bring the remaining 43 back on the rolls in Bhosari Assembly constituency.

The Indian Express sent a query to state CEO S Chockalingam on November 2 asking for information on Gavhane’s complaint. On the same day, his office sent a letter to the Pune DEO asking for explanation and action taken.

Explained Form 8: How does it work? When voters shift to a different location, they have to submit Form 8 in the new cons­tituency to get their names enrolled in the rolls there. The Electoral Registration Officer of the new constit­uency verifies the docum­ents submitted. He can also ask the Booth Level Officer to verify the address. The ERO of the new constituency approves or rejects the application on the EC’s ERONET software. If the Form 8 is approved, the software automatically creates a Form 7 in voters’ old constituencies to delete them from the voter list there.

Pune DEO’s 3 letters, NCP leader’s complaint, and internal reports from 8 election officers

On October 17, 2024, Pune District Election Officer (DEO) Suhas Diwase first wrote to Chockalingam (Maharashtra CEO) that a large number of voters from different Assembly constituencies in his district were being shifted to other constituencies through applications of address change (done through Form 8). Many of these applications provided the same electricity bill as proof of the new address, and the name on the bill did not match the voter’s name. Further, many applications came from a single IP address.



Five months later, on March 20, 2025, Pune’s new DEO Jitendra Dudi wrote to the CEO office again and said that upon verification, it was found that the voters were living in the same place, and had not shifted.

Dudi followed up with another letter to the CEO on April 4, 2025, alerting that the number of such applications could rise because of the upcoming local body elections in January 2026. When a Form 8 (form for address change) is approved in the new constituency, the ERONET software automatically generates a Form 7, which is the form for deleting a voter in the voter’s original constituency.

He wrote that the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) in the original constituency from where voters are being shifted should have an option to “reject” the Form 7 on the ERONET software.
